title: chem-eng: revisit the 9-decimal-place input-change guard now that it buys no performance
description:
Follow-up from op-fm5 (2026-08-11).

Every transfer-function block gates on

    (current_input * 1e9).round() - (previous_timestep_input * 1e9).round() != 0.0

and only records an increment when that fires. The guard was originally a PERFORMANCE guard: under the old design each input change pushed a response onto a growing vector, so suppressing tiny changes suppressed vector growth. After the O(1) rewrite an increment costs a couple of flops and no memory, so the guard buys nothing.

It was deliberately KEPT in 0.2.0 so the recurrence ignores exactly the same sub-nano changes the old code did, i.e. so the rewrite was a pure cost change. But it has a real downside worth revisiting on its own merits: because previous_timestep_input is only updated when the guard fires, an input that ramps by less than 1e-9 per step is ignored INDEFINITELY rather than accumulating -- the block sees a frozen input until the running difference happens to cross the threshold. For a slow drift that is a genuine (if small) modelling error, and it is the sort of thing a real-time twin running for a long time can hit.

PROPOSED: either drop the guard entirely (increments of zero are free and harmless), or keep it but make it compare against the last ACCEPTED input in a way that lets sub-threshold changes accumulate. Whichever is chosen, re-run the analytic-superposition verification tests in */stable_transfer_functions/recurrence_tests.rs, and note that changing this WILL change numerical output very slightly, unlike the 0.2.0 rewrite.

Low priority -- correctness nit, not a defect anyone has hit.

title: njoy THERMR DEFECT: coherent-elastic discards the extra-temperature S(E) tables — sigma_coh_el is only ever available at the base temperature
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-11 by running the port against ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-crystalline-graphite.endf (MAT=30).

DEFECT: src/thermr/mf7.rs parse_elastic() reads the LTHR=1 coherent-elastic section correctly, but for each of the LT extra-temperature LIST records it keeps ONLY the temperature value and THROWS AWAY the S(E) table:

    for _ in 0..lt {
        let list = cur.read_list()?;
        extra_temperatures_k.push(list.head.c1);   // <-- S values discarded
    }

Consequently CoherentElastic (mf7.rs:33) stores a single s_of_e for the base temperature, and CoherentElastic::cross_section(&self, e_ev) (src/thermr/coherent.rs:29) takes NO temperature argument. There is no way to evaluate sigma_coh_el at any temperature other than the base one.

The struct doc is honest about this ('their S tables are not yet retained'), but src/thermr/mod.rs:17 lists coherent as '**done**', which overstates it.

WHY IT MATTERS (HTR-10 critical path): graphite is the HTR-10 moderator and coherent elastic is its DOMINANT thermal channel (measured via the port at 0.0253 eV: sigma_coh_el = 4.55 b vs sigma_inel = 0.49 b, so ~90% of thermal scattering). The graphite evaluation tabulates 10 temperatures: 296, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1600, 2000 K. The IAEA HTR-10 B1-B4 benchmarks are at 20/120/250 C (293/393/523 K) and operation runs hotter. Using the 296 K Bragg structure factor at 523 K or 1000 K gets the Debye-Waller suppression wrong and therefore the thermal spectrum and k_eff wrong.

FIX: retain the per-temperature S(E) tables (the LIST records also carry an LI interpolation scheme between temperatures), and give CoherentElastic a temperature-aware cross_section(e_ev, temp_k) / bragg_reflections(e_ev, temp_k). Related but distinct from op-cjw.22 (which is about interpolating the INELASTIC S(alpha,beta) across temperature).

SIZE: small-to-medium. The record layout is already parsed; this is retaining data that is currently dropped, plus threading a temperature through two methods and their callers (src/acer/thermal.rs is the only in-tree consumer).

notes.content: FIXED 2026-08-11 (this session; unverified-by-human, not committed yet). parse_elastic now retains every LT extra-temperature S(E) LIST (shared Bragg-edge grid validated, LI codes captured): CoherentElastic is now {bragg_energies_ev, temperatures_k, s_tables, temp_interp}. coherent.rs evaluates cross_section(e_ev, temp_k)/bragg_reflections(e_ev, temp_k)/s_of_e_at(temp_k) with the shared policy: NJOY rdelas tolerance match (T/1000+5 K) -> LI-law interpolation between bracketing tabulated temps -> NjoyError::TemperatureOutOfRange (new variant) outside the range. acer thermal_from_mf7 writes ITCE/ITCX from s_of_e_at(temp_k). MEASURED (tests/thermal_graphite_coherent.rs, MAT 30, 0.0253 eV, b/atom): 296K 4.5514, 400K 4.3731, 500K 4.2049, 600K 4.0418, 700K 3.8849, 800K 3.7344, 1000K 3.4529, 1200K 3.1968, 1600K 2.7529, 2000K 2.3871 - strictly decreasing (Debye-Waller), 48% suppression 296->2000K. Interpolated 523.15K = 4.1672 in (4.0418,4.2049); 393.15K = 4.3849 in (4.3731,4.5514); 293.15K snaps to 296K within tolerance and reports it. NOTE also found+fixed: endf::interp::terp1 had ENDF laws 3 and 4 SWAPPED vs ENDF-102/upstream endf.f90 (needed because MT4 extras are LI=4 log-lin in T); reconr linearize midpoint arm + its test updated. 393 lib tests + 6/6 graphite V&V pass, release mode.

Offline demonstration coupling a high-temperature gas-cooled reactor heat source to a petroleum refinery flowsheet, built from outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs unit operations plus an HTR-10 primary loop.

HEAT SOURCE CAVEAT — READ BEFORE CLAIMING ANYTHING: there is NO validated HTR-10 model in this workspace. docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md (audit 2026-08-06) records that nothing HTR-10-specific is in the repository, the packed-bed Ergun pressure drop is a todo!(), pebble-bed effective radial conductivity has zero code, the solid database has no graphite, and the existing htgr_sim_v1 example is PRISMATIC, not a pebble bed. Do not describe the heat source as validated. This epic must either block on the HTR-10 core work or run against an explicitly labelled surrogate heat source.

title: refinery: DECISION — energy balance and temperature match, then pick the demonstration scope
description:
Gating scoping bead. Everything downstream depends on the answer, so do this before writing any flowsheet code.

THE PROBLEM: HTR-10 is 10 MWth. A modest crude distillation unit furnace is tens to a hundred MW. The reactor cannot run a whole refinery, so the honest deliverable is a bounded process-heat demonstration, not a plant.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH:
1. Heat demand curve of each candidate refinery duty (crude preheat, atmospheric furnace, reboilers, reformer) in MW and at what temperature.
2. Available helium outlet temperature and duty from the HTR-10 model, and what fraction of each duty it can actually supply.
3. Temperature match: HTR-10 helium outlet is high enough for crude heating by a wide margin, but steam reforming sits near the top of the range. State which duties are reachable and which are not.
4. Choose the demonstration scope explicitly. Options include a single reachable duty at true 10 MWth scale, a scaled multi-module plant, or a deliberately labelled scale-up. Whichever is chosen, the scale assumption must be stated in the simulator UI and docs, not buried.

ACCEPTANCE: a written energy and temperature balance with numbers, and one recorded decision on scope. No fabricated figures — derive from the model and cited open literature.

title: refinery: transient mode — port the DWSIM dynamics integrator and dynamic-mode execution
description:
The maintainer wants a TRANSIENT simulator; steady state is the baseline starting point, not the destination.

UPSTREAM EXISTS — correcting a common assumption: DWSIM is not steady-state-only. DWSIM.DynamicsManager (12 files, 972 lines) carries Integrator.vb, Schedule.vb, Event.vb, EventSet.vb, MonitoredVariable.vb and CauseAndEffectMatrix.vb, and DWSIM.FlowsheetSolver handles dynamic-mode execution. So this is a port with a reference, not a from-scratch design.

SCOPE: the integrator loop and its time stepping, the schedule and event model, monitored variables, and the dynamic-mode branch of the flowsheet execution order. The DynamicsManager itself is a thin orchestration layer — the actual transient behaviour comes from unit operations carrying holdup, which is a separate bead.

Steady-state solve remains the initial condition provider for every transient run.

title: refinery: dynamic unit-operation holdup and inventory — what actually makes it transient
description:
An integrator alone does not make a transient simulator. Transient behaviour comes from state that accumulates: mass, energy and momentum holdup inside vessels, drums, columns and pipes.

SCOPE: add inventory state to the unit operations that need it — separator and vessel liquid level, column stage holdup, pipe line-pack, heat-exchanger metal thermal mass — and integrate those states rather than solving them algebraically. Steady state must fall out as the zero-derivative limit, which is a directly testable property.

TEST THIS PROPERTY EXPLICITLY: a transient run started from the converged steady state and held at constant boundary conditions must stay at that state. Any drift is a conservation bug in the integrator or the holdup terms.

Depends on the flowsheet data model and the integrator.

title: refinery: pressure-flow network solve for dynamic mode
description:
In steady state, flows are specified. In dynamic mode, flows must be SOLVED from the pressure field, otherwise a valve closing changes nothing downstream and the simulator is not really transient.

SCOPE: a simultaneous pressure-flow network over the flowsheet graph, with the resistance of valves and pipes and the head of pumps and compressors, so that flow rate becomes a computed variable driven by pressure differences and inventory changes. This is what couples a valve stroke to a downstream response.

Relates to op-1z3o.5 (the steady-state sequential-modular solver) but is a different mathematical problem — simultaneous rather than sequential — so it deserves its own solve path.

Reference DWSIM dynamic mode for the formulation. Enum dispatch over element types, no trait objects.

title: refinery: real-time pacing and digital-twin engine integration
description:
Once the transient solver runs, decide whether the refinery is a batch transient study or a real-time interactive twin, and if the latter, wire it into crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine alongside the reactor simulators.

The engine already provides widgets, animation, threading and an OPC-UA telemetry path. Note that op-xvye is an open P0 against the engine for pacing sign-collapse and u64 underflow in both simulation loops — fix or account for that before trusting real-time pacing.

Offline demonstration only. No connection to any live or operational system, per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md.

title: refinery: DECISION — real-time execution, which DWSIM dynamics does NOT give you
description:
MAINTAINER POINT, recorded 2026-08-11: porting the DWSIM dynamics gets a TRANSIENT simulator, not a REAL-TIME one. These are different problems and the port does not solve the second.

WHY: DWSIM Integrator.vb advances simulated time as fast or as slow as the solve happens to take. Each step calls flash and property evaluations of unbounded cost, and a stiff or poorly converging step can take arbitrarily long. Real-time requires bounded worst-case wall-clock per step, which nothing in the upstream provides.

WHAT MUST BE SETTLED:
1. Define the target. Soft real-time for an interactive twin (drop or interpolate on overrun) or hard bounded step. These have very different costs.
2. Measure first. Instrument the ported transient loop for per-step wall-clock, worst case not mean, before designing anything. op-fm5 is the precedent: a 28 us/step plateau was MEASURED in TUAS and drove a rewrite to O(1) recurrences.
3. The likely cost centres are flash calls in the inner loop and the recycle/pressure-flow convergence iteration count, both of which are unbounded by construction.
4. Candidate strategies, to be chosen on evidence not assumption: cache or tabulate property evaluations, fix the iteration budget and carry the residual forward, precompute reduced-order surrogates for slow blocks, or run the rigorous model off the real-time thread and pace a reduced model against it.
5. See docs/real-time-multifidelity-scoping.md, which already frames the multi-fidelity approach for this workspace.

ACCEPTANCE: a measured per-step cost distribution from the actual ported loop, a stated real-time target, and one recorded decision on strategy. Do not claim real-time capability without a measured worst-case number.

title: shortcut column follow-ups: one-composition K-value entry + promote mixture liquid density
description:
Follow-ups from the ShortcutColumn port (src/columns/shortcut.rs, ported 2026-08-11 from DWSIM ShortcutColumn.vb @ 1abf72d1b6b41d3e9a8cc770d3cc4e8fc76e5766, 9/9 tests green in release, Android check clean).

1. PropertyPackageModel has no one-composition K-value form. Upstream calls DW_CalcKvalue(z, T, P) (ShortcutColumn.vb:201); the port approximates it with ColumnThermo::k_values(z, z, T, P) — exact for Ideal, first-order for cubics. Add a K(z, T, P) entry to the package enum and switch the shortcut (and any future caller) to it.

2. Mixture liquid density (upstream AUX_LIQDENS Rackett route, PropertyPackage.vb:7674) is implemented inline in the shortcut sizing block via Kay's-rule pseudo-criticals into petroleum::aux_props::liquid_density_rackett. Promote a package-level liquid-density entry into crate::thermo so shortcut sizing, pump NPSH inputs, etc. share one implementation.

3. (Optional, NOT upstream) Kirkbride feed-stage correlation as an alternative to the ported Fenske-ratio method — only if a design comparison is wanted; the port is deliberately faithful to upstream, which uses the Fenske ratio (ShortcutColumn.vb:512-519).

title: refinery: scoping doc docs/reactor-scoping/nuclear-refinery.md
description:
Write the scoping document in the same shape as docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md and msre.md: framing, plant configuration, capability audit split into HAVE / SCAFFOLD / MISSING, open validation data with access tier, recommended sequencing, and open questions for the maintainer.

DO NOT assert report numbers, identifiers or measured values that have not been read from the actual documents. Mark anything unverified as unverified, exactly as htr10.md does.

title: refinery: crude assay and pseudo-component characterisation in dwsim-libs
description:
No refinery flowsheet can exist without this. A crude oil is not a component list, it is a boiling curve that must be cut into pseudo-components.

SCOPE: true-boiling-point curve input, cut into pseudo-components with normal boiling point, specific gravity and molecular weight; correlations for critical properties and acentric factor from Tb and SG; hooking the resulting pseudo-components into the existing property_package so they flow through flash and the K-value methods.

FITS WHAT EXISTS: crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/thermo/ already carries chao_seader_grayson.rs (hydrocarbon K-values) and black_oil.rs, both of which want pseudo-components as input. This bead supplies them.

Document every correlation with its source and stated range of validity per the human-interface rule. uom types on all public signatures.

title: refinery: rigorous distillation column (MESH equations, inside-out) in dwsim-libs
description:
The single largest missing unit operation. crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/ has heater, cooler, heat_exchanger, compressor, expander, pump, valve, mixer, splitter, separator, pipe and reactors — but no column.

SCOPE: multi-stage vapour-liquid column solving the MESH equations (material balance, equilibrium, summation, enthalpy balance), with condenser and reboiler, multiple feeds, side draws and pumparounds. Prefer the inside-out algorithm to reuse the existing flash_insideout.rs machinery rather than writing a new solver from scratch.

V&V per the workspace rule — methodology AND results: validate against a published test problem from the open distillation literature with the reference numbers, tolerances and the measured outcome recorded in the test doc comment.

Enum dispatch for column variants, no trait objects, no Box, no lifetime parameters.

title: refinery: flowsheet solver — sequential-modular execution with recycle convergence
description:
dwsim-libs has unit operations but no engine to connect them. A refinery is defined by its recycles (hydrogen recycle, pumparounds, stripper returns), so a flowsheet without recycle convergence is not a refinery.

SCOPE: material and energy stream types, a unit-operation enum covering the existing blocks, execution ordering with cycle detection, tear-stream selection, and an accelerated successive-substitution convergence loop (Wegstein or equivalent) with reportable residuals and iteration limits.

DESIGN RULES: unit operations dispatch through an enum, not Box<dyn>, so adding a block is a compile error at every match site. No lifetime parameters — share the property package with Arc.

ACCEPTANCE: a small flowsheet with a real recycle converges to a stated tolerance, with the residual history available for inspection rather than a silent converged/not-converged boolean.

title: refinery: nuclear process heater — the helium-to-process coupling unit operation
description:
THE actual nuclear part of this project. Replaces a fired furnace with a heat exchanger whose hot side is reactor helium.

SCOPE: a unit operation taking helium inlet temperature, pressure and mass flow on the hot side and a process stream on the cold side, returning duty and both outlet states, with a real pinch check so the model cannot silently transfer heat up a temperature gradient. Reuse the LMTD and NTU algebra already in dwsim-libs heat_exchanger; helium properties come from crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop (full Helmholtz EOS plus real transport correlations, already tested).

SAFETY-RELEVANT MODELLING NOTE for the docs: a real coupling would need an intermediate loop and tritium-permeation and pressure-boundary considerations between reactor and hydrocarbon process. This is an offline demonstration and models none of that. State that limitation explicitly rather than implying a deployable design.

Blocks on the scope decision (op-1z3o.1) and on a heat source existing at all.

title: refinery: steam-methane reformer as a Gibbs equilibrium block for hydrogen
description:
The classic HTGR process-heat application and the highest-temperature duty in the flowsheet, so it is the interesting stress case for the temperature match.

SCOPE: wire crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/reactors/gibbs_reactor.rs to a reforming feed, with the reformer duty supplied by the nuclear process heater rather than by burning fuel gas. Report approach to equilibrium, methane conversion and hydrogen yield as functions of temperature, pressure and steam-to-carbon ratio.

V&V per the workspace rule: validate the equilibrium composition against published equilibrium data or an independent equilibrium calculation, and record the actual numbers with tolerances in the test doc comment. Do not report a yield that was not produced by running the model.

Depends on the reformer being reachable at the available helium outlet temperature — see op-1z3o.1.

title: refinery: hydrotreater block consuming the reformer hydrogen
description:
Closes the loop between the hydrogen plant and the refinery, and gives the hydrogen recycle that makes the flowsheet solver earn its keep.

SCOPE: a conversion or equilibrium reactor block for hydrodesulphurisation duty using the existing conversion_reactor.rs / equilibrium_reactor.rs, fed by makeup hydrogen from the reformer plus a recycle stream, with a separator and recycle compressor closing the gas loop. Sour water and hydrogen sulphide handling can lean on the existing sour_water.rs property package.

Reaction stoichiometry and conversion data must come from open published sources with provenance recorded per DATA_POLICY.md. Kinetics may be lumped — say so in the doc comment rather than implying a mechanistic model.

title: refinery: V&V plan — what each block is validated against, and what cannot be validated
description:
Per VERIFICATION_AND_VALIDATION.md and the CLAUDE.md rule that V&V documentation must carry BOTH methodology and measured results.

THE HONEST POSITION: no integrated nuclear-refinery plant exists, so the whole flowsheet cannot be validated end to end. Validation is therefore per block, plus conservation checks on the assembly. Say this plainly in the docs instead of implying plant-level validation.

PER-BLOCK TARGETS: distillation column against a published test problem from the open separations literature; flash and property packages against the existing dwsim-libs test suite and published phase-equilibrium data; reformer against published equilibrium composition data; heat exchanger against LMTD/NTU analytical cases.
ASSEMBLY-LEVEL CHECKS: mass and energy closure across the converged flowsheet to a stated tolerance, and a pinch check proving no heat flows up a temperature gradient.
HEAT SOURCE: inherits the HTR-10 V&V status, which is currently nothing. Until the pebble-bed closures are validated, every result carries an explicitly labelled unvalidated heat source.

Record measured numbers with uncertainty and the date taken. Never report a result that was not produced by running the check.

title: Harden TampinesSteamArray::correct_thermo() against out-of-range (p,h) panics
description:
TampinesSteamArray::correct_thermo() (crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs, from op-21g.10) calls t_ph_eqm/v_ph_eqm/kappa_t_ph_eqm/mu_ph_eqm/lambda_ph_eqm/cp_ph_eqm directly per cell -- these PANIC (not Result) if (p,h) falls out of the valid IAPWS-IF97 range (e.g. below 273.15K), unlike OPCPFluidArray::correct_thermo() (outram-park-fork-coolprop), which does 'if let Ok(state) = flash::state_ph(...) { update } else { keep previous rho/T/psi for this cell }' -- a graceful degradation, not a panic, if a cell wanders out of range mid-simulation.

Fix direction (not yet decided/implemented): either (a) wrap the tampines-steam-tables (p,h) flash calls in a fallible variant if one exists or can be added, matching CoolProp's graceful-degradation pattern, or (b) some other guard against out-of-range panics during a running PIMPLE loop.

User explicitly deferred this (2026-07-13) -- wants to check the situation manually first before any fix is attempted. Do not implement without further discussion.

title: TampinesSteamArray::step() pressure oscillation with nonzero inlet velocity BC
description: Discovered 2026-07-14 while building set_inlet_velocity/set_inlet_enthalpy/set_outlet_pressure BC setters for TampinesSteamArray (lateral_coupling.rs), in service of wiring TampinesSteamArray into fhr_sim_v2's steam generator tube. First real exercise anywhere in the crate of step()'s pressure-velocity (PISO) coupling under a nonzero Dirichlet velocity BC -- every prior test uses default zero-gradient/passive BCs or drives he alone via set_temperature_vector. Reproduction: 10-cell, 1m pipe, 1e-4 m^2 area, dt=5e-5s (acoustically stable per dx/c_sound), pre-conditioned near 370K/1bar, then inlet velocity=0.5 m/s + inlet enthalpy=4.2e5 J/kg + outlet pressure=1e5 Pa fixed. Pressure develops a large non-physical oscillation within ~10 steps (ranging ~1e5 to ~9e5 Pa across cells against a fixed 1e5 Pa outlet BC and modest inflow -- nothing in the setup should drive a 9x pressure excursion) and panics out of the valid IAPWS-IF97 range by step ~27 (see ph_flash_eqm check_if_within_ph_validity_region). Kept as an #[ignore]d regression test: openfoam_algorithms::rhoPimpleFoam::lateral_coupling::tests::inlet_outlet_bcs_drive_flow_and_outlet_pressure_settles_near_imposed_value. Suspect the source_p boundary-flux special case for BoundaryCondition::FixedValue velocity (mod.rs step(), the 'match self.u.boundary[pi].bc' block) but not confirmed -- root-causing the PISO instability was out of scope for that session. Blocks: op-21g.6 (multiphase suite work that might build on this) is unaffected, but any consumer wanting to drive TampinesSteamArray as a prescribed-BC pipe (e.g. tampines fhr_sim_v2's steam generator tube) is blocked until this is fixed.

notes.content:
2026-07-14 follow-up: root-caused and fixed one real bug (phi_hbya boundary write-back missing for FixedValue velocity patches in mod.rs step() -- self.phi kept HbyA's always-zero-gradient boundary extrapolation instead of the corrected flux used in the pressure source, corrupting the next step's rhoEqn continuity). Also added the user-requested SIMPLE/PISO/PIMPLE infrastructure: get/set_n_outer_correctors, get/set_n_inner_correctors, get/set_pressure_under_relaxation, get/set_velocity_under_relaxation, and set_piso_algorithm/set_simple_algorithm/set_pimple_algorithm presets (mod.rs). With SIMPLE + heavy under-relaxation (alpha_p=0.02, alpha_u=0.3) and staying well clear of the saturation boundary, the pressure oscillation is much better behaved (bounded ~25% swing surviving 40+ iterations, vs a 9x blowup crashing by iteration 27 before the fix) but NOT fully resolved -- temperature still drifts upward and eventually exceeds the 1073.15K validity ceiling; the energy equation's stability under residual pressure noise was not root-caused. Separately (not the same run, found by moving inlet enthalpy near h_f at 1 bar): correct_thermo's (p,h) region classification and thermal_conductivity's internal (T,p) re-classification can disagree right at the saturation boundary, hitting pt_flash_eqm::cp_tp_eqm_single_phase's FwdEqnRegion::Region4 => todo!() panic -- this would block real steam-generator (boiling) use regardless of the pressure-oscillation outcome. All three findings documented in the (still #[ignore]d) regression test inlet_outlet_bcs_drive_flow_and_outlet_pressure_settles_near_imposed_value's doc comment. Net: real progress, but wiring TampinesSteamArray into a driven steam-generator-tube use case (e.g. fhr_sim_v2) remains blocked on findings 2 and 3.
2026-07-14: FINDING 3 (saturation-boundary todo!()) RESOLVED. lambda_ph_eqm's critical-enhancement term (thermal_conductivity::lambda_2_crit_enhancement_term_tp_two_phase_estimate) delegated cp/cv/kappa_t to single-phase (T,p) routines that todo!() in region 4 (T,p not independent on the saturation line). lambda_ph_eqm calls this for EVERY region (x=0 region1, x=1 region2/3, interior region4), so the fix branches: single-phase (x==0 or x==1) keeps the exact (t,p) single-phase values bit-for-bit (verified: the 53 single-phase steam-table lambda tests that a naive t_sat-everywhere version broke now all pass again); genuine two-phase (0<x<1) quality-weights the saturated region-1/region-2 values at t_sat, mirroring cp_ph_eqm's own region-4 handling. Two new verification tests (both pass): thermal_conductivity::tests::lambda_ph_two_phase_is_finite_and_bracketed (finite, positive, bracketed by sat vapour..liquid, monotonic in quality at 1 bar) and openfoam_algorithms::rhoPimpleFoam::tests::correct_thermo_survives_two_phase_boiling_cell (a TampinesSteamArray cell at 1 bar / h=1.5MJ/kg / x~0.48 survives correct_thermo, T~T_sat, all fields finite). Full suite 909 passed / 0 failed. This unblocks a boiling steam-generator-tube model. Remaining on this bead: the PISO/stiff-liquid pressure-oscillation robustness (findings 1-2) for driving TampinesSteamArray hard; the source-clobber root cause (separate) is already fixed + pushed in 540fd45.
2026-07-14: TampinesSteamArray WIRED into fhr_sim_v2's steam-generator tube (secondary_loop/mod.rs), replacing the lumped h_out=h_in+Q/mdot energy balance with the spatially-resolved (p,h) steam-table physics. Persistent array (build_steam_generator_tube), driven 25 acoustic-CFL substeps per TH step, outlet enthalpy read back to feed the turbine. New standalone validation test steam_generator_tube_boils_feedwater (feedwater 80degC -> boiling at 2 bar, x crosses 0 at step 5416, passes). New API set_uniform_velocity_field (pre-condition velocity to avoid water-hammer). Two integration bugs found + fixed (see tampines-steam-tables/docs/notes.md 'Correction log'): (1) default pressure floor was sat_pressure_4(273.15) EXACTLY -> clamped cells land on saturation line -> (p,h) validity guard's exact-equality Region-4 test todo!()-panics; fixed by nudging floor *1.001 into Region 1; (2) pre-init pressure (2 bar) mismatched operating outlet BC (1.2 bar) -> depressurisation rarefaction cooled a cell below 273.15K; fixed by matching pre-init to operating pressure. Live sim now runs 30s clean (0 panics), SG tube heats feedwater 90->97degC and warming. Maintainer guidance recorded: arrays use (p,h) flashing by default, not (T,p) single-phase. Remaining on this bead: the deeper stiff-liquid transient robustness (the array still panics if driven far outside its envelope, per the panic-on-out-of-range design) and enthalpy bounding as a future analogue to pressure bounding.

title: TampinesSteamArray energy over-cooling under fast flashing (Edwards blowdown plateau under-predicted)
description:
The Edwards-O'Brien blowdown V&V test (tests/edwards_blowdown.rs) exposes an energy-conservation limitation in TampinesSteamArray::step(). During the violent subcooled->two-phase decompression the h-form energy equation loses ~10x more enthalpy than the reversible dh=dp/rho, so the bulk liquid drops to subcooled and only flashes near ambient instead of holding the ~350-380 psia (p_sat at T0~505K) flashing plateau. Measured GS-1 plateau ~17 psia vs experimental ~350-367 psia; GS-1 pressure RMSE vs digitised Data ~276 psia.

Root cause: step() runs the explicit rhoEqn continuity rho = rho_old - dt*div(phi), but correct_thermo then OVERWRITES rho with the EOS (p,h) density each inner correction. That breaks the discrete cancellation of the h*div(phi) term in d(rho h)/dt + div(phi h) = dp/dt, so enthalpy is not conserved through a fast density change. Reducing dt (30us->10us) does not fix the ratio; it is structural.

NOTE: this is the ACCURACY limitation only. The STABILITY question Ethan raised (explicit scheme cools empty pipe to ~1C and pressure rebounds past 0.42s) is CURED by our PIMPLE array: past 0.42s min T=358K, tail pressure rebound +0.9 psia, void stable 0.997 -- no artefact. See test doc comment for full V&V write-up.

Possible fixes to evaluate (need own V&V): (a) conservative (rho*e or rho*h) energy update using the continuity-consistent density rather than the EOS density in the ddt term; (b) an internal-energy (e) formulation; (c) sub-cycling the flash within the corrector. Do NOT loosen the test tolerance -- assertions there are sanity-only by design.

notes.content: RESOLVED 2026-07-16. Fixed with two coupled thermodynamic corrections (no clamps): (1) conservative energy ddt using the CONTINUITY density rho_cont = rho_old - dt*div(phi) rebuilt from the final mass flux (new fvm::ddt_coeff_old), so (rho_cont-rho_old)/dt = -div(phi) exactly and the h*div(phi) term cancels term-for-term against div(phi h), restoring rho Dh/Dt = dp/dt -- this is approach (a) from the bead; (2) pressure-eqn compressibility psi = d(rho)/dp|_h (central finite-diff of the (p,h) flash at fixed enthalpy) replacing the frozen quality-weighted isothermal rho*kappa_T, which was ~100x too small in the two-phase dome and let the pressure overshoot through the plateau. Results: GS-1 flashing plateau 17 -> 393 psia (target ~350-367); RMSE vs Data 276 -> 60 psia; stable full 600 ms; no non-physical subcooling (void grows gradually, fluid holds near p_sat). All 915 lib tests still green. See collaboration/edwards_tampines_regen/debug_log.md and tests/edwards_blowdown.rs doc comment. Residual: plateau ~8% high + shallow late decline (HEM-closure accuracy, separate from the missing-plateau failure).

It is the blocker for HybridAllMach being usable; treat as its own future-work item, not a follow-up tweak. HybridAllMach is marked experimental in code until this is resolved.
notes.author: teddy0@snrsiDesktop

notes.content: FIXED 2026-07-16. Root cause: not a physics limit of HEM but a numerical stiffness in the rarefied emptying tail. As the pipe empties past t~0.18s a cell rarefies in a localized runaway (rho 127->23->vacuum over ~350 steps); the conservative-EEqn diagonal rho_cont*V/dt collapses to its 1e-4 floor, the solve becomes ill-conditioned, and one step tips he from 951 kJ/kg to -7.3e6 kJ/kg -> below the 273.15K (p,h) edge -> panic. Both continuity and momentum KNP dissipation independently trigger it, so it is the explicit deferred correction being over-driven in the rarefied tail, not a sign error. Fix: rarefied-tail density taper on the KNP blend beta *= clamp((rho_face-50)/(100-50),0,1), rho_face=min(rho_o,rho_nb). Dissipation zero below 50 kg/m3 (rarefied -> pure PIMPLE, stable), full above 100. Measured min dissipated-face density over the 0-0.15s ringing window is 106.5 kg/m3, so the taper is inert there. Results: full 600ms HybridAllMach completes (no panic/NaN, void in [0,1]), plateau 387.7 psia, GS-1 RMSE 30.6 psia, no cold tail; 0-0.15s ringing -55.5% and plateau retained bit-identically; default Pimple bit-identical (920 lib tests pass). See collaboration/edwards_tampines_regen/hybrid_stability_debug_log.md + figures_hybrid_stable/. Not committed (maintainer commits).

title: V&V: two-phase frictional pressure drop — Thom (1964) / Martinelli-Nelson (1948)
description:
No steady-state two-phase pressure-drop validation exists for TampinesSteamArray / tampines::components::Pipe. Only the transient (Edwards-O'Brien) path is exercised.

Thom (1964) gives two-phase multipliers r2, r3, r4 for boiling water/steam tabulated by pressure; Martinelli & Nelson (1948) covers 0.1 MPa to critical. Both are steam-water-specific and recommended at secondary-loop pressures, unlike the air-water-rooted Lockhart-Martinelli (1949).

Per maintainer direction 2026-08-04, any ported correlation code lands as a MODULE under tampines/src/hem/ or beside TampinesSteamArray in openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/ — not a new crate.

title: V&V: subcooled boiling void fraction — Bartolomei & Chanturiya (1967)
description:
Cross-sectionally averaged void fraction at axial stations in a vertical heated tube, upward flow. Range: p to 15 MPa, G to 2000 kg/m2/s, q to 2.2 MW/m2. Wall and subcooled liquid temperature available for one condition.

Citation: Bartolomej, G. G. & Chanturiya, V. M., 'Experimental study of true void fraction when boiling subcooled water in vertical tubes', Thermal Engineering 14 (1967) 123-128.

Access problem: the original Russian-journal paper is hard to obtain. The data is digitised in open-access validation papers, e.g. arXiv:1709.01783 (OpenFOAM two-phase boiling). Digitisation provenance MUST be recorded the way marviken_tests.rs records its graphreader points — which paper, which figure, which reader tool.

title: V&V (diagnostic): wet-steam condensing nozzles — Moore B, Barschdorff
description:
Quantifies what the HEM assumption costs in the existing converging_diverging_nozzles module versus real non-equilibrium (supersaturated / Wilson-line) condensation.

The four standard benchmark supersonic nozzles are Moore B, Barschdorff, IWSEP and SUT de Laval, with measured axial static pressure distributions and fog-droplet sizes. Primary sources are old conference proceedings (Moore, Walters, Crane & Davidson 1973, IMechE C37/73; Barschdorff 1971; Moses & Stein; Gyarmathy), but digitised geometry and pressure data for all four appear in the OPEN-ACCESS paper 'Numerical analysis of non-equilibrium steam condensing flows in various Laval nozzles and cascades', Eng. Appl. Comput. Fluid Mech.

NOT a pass/fail gate — HEM is expected to miss the condensation shock. The deliverable is the quantified gap, for the paper's V&V section.

Scope context: crates/tampines-steam-tables/docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md section 3.4.

envelope, design-basis accident/transient scenarios), produce:

Ties together essentially the whole suite (njoy -> openmc -> genfoam -> source

description: By-hand analytical derivation of the conservative energy discretisation that fixed the Edwards blowdown plateau collapse (op-21g.14). title: pflotran: 26.4k LOC written without upstream; licence never verified (provenance)
description:
PROVENANCE / RESEARCH-INTEGRITY issue under RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md.

crates/outram-park-fork-pflotran is 26,409 lines across 47 .rs files, written WITHOUT ever obtaining the upstream PFLOTRAN source.

Evidence:
- NOTICE:19-25 admits it outright: "LICENSE PROVENANCE -- VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISH. The LGPL-2.1-or-later determination above was taken from the PFLOTRAN documentation and the OSTI/DOECODE records (2026-07-20), not from a byte-for-byte reading of the upstream LICENSE/COPYRIGHT file (which was not reachable from this environment)."
- No upstream clone exists on this machine. /home/teddy0/Documents/research/ has openfoam, openmc, NJOY2016, dwsim, ThermoSysPro -- no pflotran. A find over the filesystem returns only /usr/include/paraview/vtkVisItPFLOTRANReader.h.
- upstream_source/ contains only README.md, which states "It holds no PFLOTRAN source yet".
- No .rs file in src/ carries a provenance header naming an upstream .F90 file, contrary to the workspace attribution rule.

WHY THE GAP IS LOAD-BEARING: the GPL-3.0-only relicensing relies on LGPL-2.1 section 3, which only works if upstream really is LGPL-2.1-OR-LATER and not a bare LGPL-2.1, LGPL-3.0, or a mixed-file situation. Nobody has read the upstream LICENSE/COPYRIGHT.

SECOND, SEPARATE CONTRADICTION: NOTICE:27-28 says "No PFLOTRAN source has been ported into this crate yet -- it is a documented scaffold", while README.md:55-61 describes RICHARDS flow, transport, energy, geochemistry, kinetics, reactive transport and multiphase as "real (verif-only)" with a 114-test suite. Root Cargo.toml:25-27 and workspace CLAUDE.md also still call it a scaffold. Either 26k LOC was written without upstream -- in which case "fork/translation of PFLOTRAN" is the wrong framing and the crate should be renamed/reframed as an independent implementation informed by published equations -- or code WAS derived and the per-file attribution is missing.

Note README.md:122 marks the provenance bead op-v6s.1 as "done (verify upstream before publish)" -- that should not read as done.

REQUIRED before this crate is published or described as a PFLOTRAN fork:
1. Obtain a PFLOTRAN clone and read LICENSE/COPYRIGHT byte-for-byte; record it in upstream_source/README.md.
2. Decide and state honestly whether this is a derived port (then add per-file provenance headers) or an independent implementation (then stop calling it a fork).
3. Reconcile NOTICE / README / root Cargo.toml / workspace CLAUDE.md so they agree.

Verified 2026-08-07 against the working tree.

title: DEM: history-free tangential contact prevents a true static packing
description:
Found while baking the pebble-packing artwork (crates/outram-park-fork-liggghts/examples/bake_pebble_packing.rs, 2026-08-06).

DemSimulation carries no accumulated tangential spring displacement between steps (documented in simulation.rs 'Honest scope'), so the tangential force is a Coulomb-capped dashpot only. Consequence: there is NO STATIC FRICTION. A grain resting on an inclined contact always creeps at a small terminal velocity, and a settled bed can never reach a strict zero-velocity rest state.

Measured evidence from the bake (2525 spheres, 74000 steps, dt=1e-4 s, dynamic-relaxation quench with the velocity field zeroed every 200 steps):
  - creep over two back-to-back 0.50 s windows: rms 4.18 % then 3.72 % of a pebble radius; max 16.6 % then 20.2 %. Steady, not decaying -> a floor, not an unfinished transient.
  - local solid fraction over the same windows: 0.6069, 0.6101, 0.6112 -> the packing STRUCTURE is stable even though grains keep creeping.
  - ensemble kinetic energy likewise floors out (~3e-1 J for 2525 pebbles) because the quench removes momentum that gravity immediately restores.

Fix: add per-contact tangential history state (the accumulated spring displacement xi_t, keyed by particle pair and carried across steps) so a resting contact can sustain a static tangential force. That also unlocks angle-of-repose verification, which is the standard DEM validation case for friction and is currently impossible.

Also worth having once that lands: a cone/frustum Boundary variant. The bake had to approximate the conical vessel bottom with 32 inscribed flat Wall half-spaces.

notes.content:
MAINTAINER'S CALL, 2026-08-06: not a blocker, and not to be treated stringently for artwork purposes.

The packing baked in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/pebble_packing.rs is ARTWORK. Its structure is settled — solid fraction stable at 0.6069 / 0.6101 / 0.6112 across measurement windows, against ~0.61 for a real pebble bed — and that is the only property the drawing depends on. The residual creep (rms ~4% of a pebble radius, steady rather than decaying) does not affect how it looks.

So: DO NOT re-run, re-settle, post-process or otherwise chase equilibrium for the sake of the widgets. Use the bake as-is.

This bead stays open because the underlying limitation is REAL and would matter if the DEM is ever used for physics rather than pictures: simulation.rs's tangential contact is history-free (a Coulomb-capped dashpot with no accumulated tangential spring), so there is no static friction and a grain on an inclined contact creeps indefinitely. Strict rest is unreachable. That is worth fixing when someone wants granular DEM results, not before.

Dropped to reflect that it gates nothing currently in flight. The honest caveat in the module doc STAYS — documenting the limitation costs nothing and prevents the packing being cited later as a settled-equilibrium result. Documenting it is not the same as being stringent about it.

Mesh Studio / cfmesh: pipe geometry with named inlet + outlet patches and wall boundary layers
description:
Captured 2026-08-04 from a half-formed idea the maintainer deferred -- CONFIRM THE INTENT before building.

As stated: 'I want boundary layers to be implemented for the pipe... should have inlet and outlet'.

Context it came out of: we had just run examples/mesh_studio (outram-blender, --features foam-mesh) on a cylinder primitive (r=2.0 m, h=10.5 m), which produced 34210 cells via the cfmesh tet -> dual -> prism-layer pipeline and exported an OpenFOAM polyMesh.

Likely reading (UNVERIFIED -- ask first): a pipe/cylinder meshed for CFD needs its boundary split into named patches -- inlet and outlet on the two end caps, wall on the curved surface -- and prism/boundary layers should be grown on the WALL only, not on the inlet/outlet planes. Growing layers on an inlet/outlet face is a classic meshing error. Today the boundary-layer controls in Mesh Studio (prism layers / first thickness / expansion ratio) appear to apply without any per-patch distinction, and it is not established whether the exported polyMesh names its patches at all.

Worth checking as part of this:
- Does outram-park-fork-cfmesh's pipeline expose per-patch boundary-layer control?
- Does the polyMesh writer emit meaningful patch names/types (patch vs wall) or one lumped boundary?
- Mesh quality on the cylinder run was already marginal (max non-orthogonality 87.2 deg, max skewness 7.994, and a stage note 'Delaunay improvement skipped -- no valid improving flips on this geometry'). Restricting layers to the wall may improve this.

Related: op-hzs.34 (outram-blender wall boundary-layer / prism-layer insertion).

title: tuas: Wakao packed-bed Nusselt has Re and Pr exponents swapped
description: VERIFIED 2026-08-11 against the working tree. crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/heat_transfer_correlations/nusselt_number_correlations/input_structs.rs, WakaoData::get() (~line 178-192) computes Nu = 2 + 1.1 * Re^0.3333 * Pr^0.6 (c=0.3333333333 applied to reynolds, d=0.6 applied to prandtl). The published Wakao correlation (Wakao & Funazkri 1978 for Sherwood; Wakao, Kaguei & Funazkri 1979 heat-transfer analogue, the form cited in the struct's own doc comment) is Nu = 2 + 1.1 * Pr^(1/3) * Re^0.6 -- the exponents on Re and Pr are SWAPPED in the code. The doc comment 'Nu = 2.0 + 1.1 * Re^0.333 Pr^0.6' faithfully describes the wrong code. Magnitude: at Re=4000, Pr=0.66 (helium in an HTR-10-like bed) the correct form gives Nu ~= 141, the as-coded form ~= 16 -- roughly a factor 9 under-prediction of particle-to-fluid heat transfer. Any packed-bed component using WakaoData inherits this. Found while building the HTR-10 pebble-bed CHT layer (op-jyyp.5); tampines/src/pebble_bed/cht.rs implements the correct form and carries a documented-discrepancy test referencing this bead. Fix in TUAS + audit callers; not fixed by the pebble-bed agent because TUAS ownership was scoped to the solid database only.

notes.content: Fixed and pushed 2026-08-11 in commit e0f0568a on develop. WakaoData::get now computes Nu = 2 + 1.1 * Pr^(1/3) * Re^0.6, with the 1979 Nusselt-form citation added alongside the 1978 Sherwood one (the doc comment previously cited only the mass-transfer paper while implementing the heat-transfer form). +196 lines of tests; cargo test --release -p tuas_boussinesq_solver --lib nusselt -> 14 passed, 0 failed, 103.67 s. Downstream follow-ups remain open and are NOT covered by this fix: op-fsk9 (the pre-fix baseline was never measured, so calibration masking is unresolved), op-29s8 (stale 'defect still current' notes in tampines pebble_bed), op-lmye (CIET heater v2 feeds hydraulic-diameter Reynolds into a particle-diameter correlation), op-fv5f (other op-4542 audit mismatches).

   regression test suite already both call the *same* shared constructor

Status: logged as TODO only, per user request ("mark this as todo, to be

design:
INVESTIGATION 2026-07-15 (teddy0 session). Corrected root cause + plan.

BASELINE (real cargo test --release runs):

  dataset_c C1-C9) currently PASS. None #[ignore]d, none loosened to pass.

  are JUSTIFIED, not arbitrary: patch_notes v0.0.1 records they match/beat the
  SAM publication's own experimental agreement (SAM max err 6.65% pri,
  6.76% DRACS). Do NOT loosen these (workspace hard rule).
- Regression assertions (0.1% flow, 0.01K temps) also pass.

REAL ISSUE = systematic DRACS mass-flow OVER-PREDICTION vs experiment,
growing with flow: a1 +4.1%, a3 +5.0%, a4 +5.4%, c4 +5.5%, c5 +5.2%.
This is exactly what mod.rs lines 118-128 and the TUAS paper flagged.

CORRECTED PREMISE (the original op-4wl.2 assumption is WRONG):
- There are NO separate "SAM educational-simulator" DRACS K values to pull.
  The educational simulator (examples/.../full_simulation/mod.rs,
  nat_circ_simulation/mod.rs) and the tests call the SAME shared
  dracs_loop_components::new_pipe_3x constructors. They are already identical.
- The NED 2021 paper (Zou, Hu, O'Grady, Hu, NED 377 111144) states SAM uses
  DRACS spatial nodalization "similar to the RELAP5-3D model of Zweibaum"
  (p.9) with the same K source -> SAM DRACS K ~= RELAP DRACS K. The only
  documented SAM-specific K deviations are pipe 3 (3.15->17.15) and pipe 22
  (9.95->45.95), BOTH primary-loop, BOTH already applied
  (new_pipe_3_sam_model / new_pipe_22_sam_model). Pipe 35b split also done.
- The over-prediction is a DOCUMENTED SAM limitation too: NED 2021 p.15
  "even with correctly calibrated parasitic heat loss, SAM-predicted mass
  flow rates are still consistently higher than experimental data for all
  simulated cases ... overestimates buoyancy or underestimates friction/form loss."
- ANL/NSE-19/11 appendix (per-pipe K table) not obtainable (publications.anl.gov
  403). Journal paper has no per-pipe K table. Do NOT fabricate SAM DRACS K values.

VALIDATED FIX (already proven, just not propagated to the coupled loop):
- isolated_dracs_loop_resistance_calibration/mod.rs recalibrates pipe 38
  form loss 0.8 -> 17.8, which removes the over-prediction: isolated-loop
  error vs SAM drops from +2.14% (K=0.8) to +0.14% (K=17.8) at the worst
  point (test9), and all 9 case_c isolated tests match SAM to <0.35%.
- BUT that calibration uses a LOCAL new_calibrated_pipe_38 (K=17.8). The

title: Velocity/Reynolds-dependent pipe-38 form loss to fix coupled DRACS low-flow cases (B1/C1)
description:
Follow-up to op-4wl.2/op-4wl.4 (pipe-38 K=0.8->17.8 SAM adoption, 2026-07-15). A single uniform form loss K=17.8 fixes the mid/high-flow DRACS over-prediction but cannot fix the two lowest-flow coupled cases B1 (655W) and C1 (841W), which already under-predict at K=0.8 and worsen to -6.62%/-6.80% under added resistance (form loss ~ v^2, negligible at low flow). They currently carry a documented per-point widened DRACS tolerance (B1 0.062->0.0676; C1 0.0676->0.069).

Proper fix: give pipe 38 a velocity/Reynolds-dependent loss of the form f_darcy = form_loss + b*Re^c, which is ALREADY supported by InsulatedFluidComponent::new_custom_component (see insulated_pipes_and_fluid_components/mod.rs:204, new_custom_component with reynolds_coefficient b and reynolds_power c). Shape needed: small a at low Re (helps B1/C1 low-flow under-prediction) rising to ~K=17.8-equivalent at high Re (preserves the mid/high-flow over-prediction fix). Calibrate b,c across all 25 coupled cases; re-validate the isolated-DRACS SAM reference (currently defined at constant K=17.8); then tighten B1/C1 tolerances back to the benchmark bound (0.062/0.0676) and recompute regression literals. Deferred from op-4wl.4 because per-iteration cost is a full ~50-min 25-case run and it would also require re-deriving the isolated SAM calibration.

title: root@vm
HTR-10 rung 1 enabler: cylindrical bounds, two pebble species, and packing fraction 0.61 in sphere_packing
description:
Parent: op-841p. The single hardest missing piece for an explicit-bed HTR-10 model, with the lines that prove each gap:

1. CYLINDRICAL BOUNDS MISSING. pack_spheres(radius, half_width, packing_fraction, seed) takes ONE cube half-width - crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/sphere_packing.rs:205 and :98-104. The HTR-10 bed is a 180 cm diameter cylinder above a conus.
2. TWO PEBBLE SPECIES MISSING. A single scalar radius, doc says 'all particles equal-radius' - sphere_packing.rs:99 and :195. The HTR-10 initial core IS the 57:43 fuel/dummy mixture; without two species there is no initial core.
3. PACKING FRACTION CEILING. MAX_PF_RSA = 0.38 at sphere_packing.rs:63, rejection at :211-216. HTR-10 needs 0.61. Plain RSA cannot reach it. PackingMethod::RsaDem and ::OdrDem both return Err(NotImplemented) at :160, proved by the test at :546.

So (3) requires implementing RSA-DEM or ODR-DEM. Reference: the Tan citations already recorded in crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/references.rs (TAN2026_RSA_DEM doi 10.1080/00295639.2025.2456456, TAN2026_ODR_DEM no DOI assigned).

Cross-check available: Choo and Xiao (2024, OPEN tier, crates/kovan-literature/open/papers/choo-htr10-criticality.json) generate their HTR-10 packing with LAMMPS discrete-element settling and report the radial distribution function peaking at 6 cm from direct pebble contact - a validatable signature for any packer that claims 0.61.

Also worth knowing: the measured 16890 balls and the 123.06 cm loading height are NOT independent - filling a plain cylinder to 123.06 cm at f = 0.61 gives 16890.0 balls (measured 2026-08-11 by htr10::neutronics::tests::measured_ball_count_follows_from_loading_height). A packer that realises a different fraction must reconcile with the ball COUNT, not the height.

title: kovan-literature: graph digitiser module (CLI + TUI + egui, graphreader-style)
description:
Extract data points from plot images in the literature archive. Requested by the maintainer 2026-08-11.

WHY THIS IS NEEDED AND NOT A TOY: several validation targets this project depends on exist ONLY as figures. docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md records that the HTR-10 safety demonstration tests (loss of forced cooling without scram, rod withdrawal without scram) should be expected as digitised plots rather than tabulated data, and the same is true of the MSRE reactivity-insertion figures noted in vtb-findings.md. Without a digitiser those benchmarks cannot be used at all.

THREE INTERFACES, one engine:
- CLI - FULLY AUTOMATIC, no human in the loop. Detects axes, calibrates, traces curves, emits points. This is the agent-facing path and must be scriptable and deterministic.
- TUI (ratatui) - HYBRID: automatic pass first, then human verification and correction.
- egui - HYBRID: automatic pass first, then human verification and correction, with a graphical interface modelled on https://www.graphreader.com/ - load image, set two reference points per axis, choose linear or log per axis, auto-trace the curve, then drag/add/delete individual points, and export.

The automatic-first-then-verify shape is the point: the machine does the tedious part, the human confirms it, and the confirmation is recorded rather than assumed.

MANDATORY OUTPUT REQUIREMENT: every digitisation records its own provenance - source document and figure number, axis calibration reference points, linear/log per axis, reading uncertainty, whether the points were auto-traced or hand-placed or corrected, and by whom and when. Under DATA_POLICY.md digitisation is a processing step and must be documented as one. An exported dataset with no calibration record is not usable as validation evidence.

GOLDEN ORACLE: the sibling bead covers the maintainer supplying hand-digitised points from the Tobias decay-heat figures. Those are the acceptance test - the digitiser output must be compared against them with a stated tolerance, and log axes must be checked specifically because that is where naive pixel interpolation goes wrong.

PORTABILITY (HARD RULE): the CLI and the ratatui TUI must compile and run natively on Termux/Android like every other non-GUI crate - a terminal app is IN scope, not exempt. Only the egui/eframe interface is a genuine GUI exemption and must be target-gated so the library still builds headless for aarch64-linux-android. Image decoding must be pure Rust with no C toolchain.

DESIGN: enum dispatch over axis types and trace strategies, no trait objects, no Box, no lifetime parameters. Offline and deterministic, consistent with the rest of KOVAN - no cloud, no ML service.

title: kovan: a note-taking interface over catalogued documents
description:
MAINTAINER REQUEST 2026-08-11: "I think there should be a good interface for me to make notes via kovan." Filed for a later session, not started.

THE NEED. The archive now holds 16 documents and is growing fast — five HTR-10 papers arrived in a single morning. Reading them produces exactly the kind of knowledge that currently has nowhere to live: which figure holds the LOFC transient, which table the correlation came from, why one paper contradicts another, what a number actually means in context. Today that ends up in commit messages, bead comments, or nowhere at all.

WHAT IT SHOULD PROBABLY DO — for the maintainer to shape, these are candidates not requirements:
- Notes ATTACHED to a KovanDocument, not floating in a separate file, so a note cannot outlive or drift from the document it is about.
- Anchored where possible: page, section, figure or table number. A note saying "the 1046.6 C figure is at 120 percent overload, not nominal" is worth far more when it points at the page.
- Cross-document links, since the interesting knowledge is comparative. Real example from 2026-08-11: HTR-10 own fuel temperature LIMIT is 1230 C per Gao and Shi, while the 1600 C that pervades the modular-HTR literature including kugeler2017vhtr is the GENERIC coated-particle retention limit. Conflating them would misstate a safety margin, and that distinction currently survives only in a bead comment.
- Links out to beads and to source files, mirroring what CATALOGUE.md already does by hand.
- Notes are the maintainer own voice and should be distinguishable from extracted document text — never silently merged into the markdown body.

INTERFACE. The TUI is the natural home (kovan-tui, or the digitiser TUI pattern from op-5v5.8), since note-taking is a human activity and the CLI is the agent path. A CLI verb for appending a note non-interactively is still worth having so an agent can record a finding for the maintainer to review.

RESPECT THE EXISTING GRAIN:
- Notes on a PROPRIETARY document must stay gitignored with it. A note quoting a paywalled paper at length inherits its restrictions.
- huang2025waterIngress is a special case: its full text is deliberately not extracted because of a TDM/AI reservation (op-b7bx). Notes on it are the maintainer OWN words about it, which is fine and arguably the whole point — but the tooling must not use notes as a back door to reconstructing the text.
- Provenance discipline as everywhere else: who wrote the note and when.

RELATED: op-5v5.8 (graph digitiser, whose review workflow already records who verified what and when — the same pattern), and the KovanDocument model in kovan-common, which is the source of truth and would need a notes field or a sidecar.

title: tampines: TwoFluid1d solver core — six-eqn semi-implicit march, traced drag + interfacial heat transfer, interfacial-pressure regularisation

notes.content:
Groundwork for this bead was written 2026-08-11 and is sitting UNCOMMITTED in the working tree — crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/properties.rs, +556 lines. Not backed up anywhere else. Recording it here so it is not mistaken for un-started work.

WHAT LANDED IN THE TREE:
- IF97 range constants pulled out as named public items: T_MAX_REGION_1 623.15 K, T_MAX_REGION_2 1073.15 K, T_MIN_IF97 273.16 K.
- Metastability limits: MAX_METASTABLE_LIQUID_SUPERHEAT 30.0 K, MAX_METASTABLE_VAPOUR_SUBCOOLING 30.0 K. These are the thermal-non-equilibrium excursion caps the six-equation model needs and the drift-flux/HEM models do not.
- SaturatedTransport { at(p), is_stale_for(p), liquid_prandtl(..), vapour_prandtl(..), liquid_conductivity(), vapour_conductivity(), check_same_pressure(..) } with TRANSPORT_CACHE_TOLERANCE 1.0e-2 — a per-pressure transport-property cache with a staleness test, so the interfacial heat-transfer closures do not re-flash IF97 transport every cell every step.
- PhaseState { liquid_at(p,h,saturated), vapour_at(p,h,saturated), thermodynamic_temperature(), mass_density() } — the per-phase (not mixture) thermodynamic state the six-equation energy equations march.
- Helpers check_flash_inputs(..) and invert_monotone_fast(..).

STATE: compiles; `cargo test --release -p tampines --lib multiphase_1d` -> 6 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored. None of those 6 exercises the new types — there is no TwoFluid1d solver to consume them yet, and two_fluid_tests.rs is still the 12-line placeholder registered so the module map stays stable.

CAUTION for whoever picks this up: TRANSPORT_CACHE_TOLERANCE = 1.0e-2 is a 1 % relative pressure window for reusing cached transport properties. That is an accuracy/speed trade nobody has measured the error of. Before the solver depends on it, quantify what a 1 % pressure staleness does to mu and k near the saturation line, where they vary fastest — or make the tolerance a documented, justified number rather than a chosen one.

  trailered commits, non-merge:  172   total 3,363,701,768   <- what query reports
  trailered commits, merge only:  75   total 2,513,257,137   <- silently dropped

That is 42.8% of the recorded token spend.

Why this looks unintended rather than deliberate: CLAUDE.md's historian section says lines come from 'git log --numstat --no-merges' and describes the merge exclusion for LINES only. Excluding merges is correct for lines (a merge re-reports its side branch's lines). It is wrong for tokens, because each API-Usage-Since-Last-Commit trailer is a DISJOINT delta -- prepare-commit-msg stamps the delta since the previous commit and post-commit advances the baseline, so a merge commit's trailer is real work not counted anywhere else. In this workspace merge commits are where the expensive part lives: reading the diff, running per-crate release tests, Android --all-targets, provenance and sign-off checks.

Largest dropped trailers:
  205,934,989  26080c16  Merge branch 'claude/outram-foam-8ookor' into develop
  186,299,135  423a5db3  Merge branch 'claude/outram-blender-mggk7u' into develop
  175,539,906  0d949263  Merge branch 'claude/outram-foam-8ookor' into develop
  130,215,239  53b5bef9  Merge branch 'claude/outram-foam-8ookor' into develop

Sites: token_usage.py cmd_query line ~329; historian.py line ~85.

Suggested fix: drop --no-merges from the TOKEN commit list in both tools while keeping it for the numstat/lines path, and report merge-commit tokens as a separate line so the split stays visible. Needs the maintainer's confirmation that counting merge commits is the intended semantics before any code change -- this bead is the finding, not an authorisation to edit.

title: basic-lib: SurfaceScalarField::uniform sets boundary face values to 0 (nulls fvm::laplacian boundary coeff)
description: Found during genfoam thermoMechanics mesh-solve port (op-p6p.11). outram-foam-basic-lib SurfaceScalarField::uniform() builds boundary patches via PatchField::zero_gradient(p.size), whose values are 0. Since scalar fvm::laplacian computes the boundary-face diffusion coeff as gamma.boundary[pi].values[fi]*area/d, a uniform gamma silently yields ZERO diffusion coefficient on every boundary face -> Dirichlet contributions dropped -> solve returns all-zeros yet reports converged (normalised_residual of x=0 with b=0 is 0). Workaround used in mesh_solve.rs: build the SurfaceScalarField with PatchField::fixed_value(size, k) boundary patches. Fix: SurfaceScalarField::uniform should set boundary values to the uniform value (fixed_value), or laplacian should treat a zero-gradient gamma patch as owner-extrapolated. Not my subtree; reporting per workspace rules.

offbeat: decide whether MaterialState needs minor-actinide (Am/Np) fractions for MA-MOX fuel
description:
MaterialState has no minor-actinide inventory, but several ported correlations
want one:

- thermalExpansionMatproUPuO2 and the Lemehov UPuO2 model discount the plutonium
  fraction by americium and neptunium number densities.
- Lemehov's melting-point correlation has an explicit Am term.
- conductivityKatoMox and conductivityMagniMamox currently carry Am/Np as variant
  payload precisely because MaterialState cannot express them.

The port assumes zero minor actinides and documents that this over-predicts the
melting point (and so under-predicts strain) for MA-bearing fuel.

If MA-MOX is in scope, add am_fraction and np_fraction to MaterialState and move
the Kato/MAMOX payloads onto it. If it is not in scope, close this and keep the

title: offbeat: wire rheology into the mechanics solve (inelastic strain feedback, state advance, timestep control)
description:
P0 mechanics (op-6sl.1) and P1 rheology (op-6sl.2) are both ported and tested,
but nothing wires them together yet. MechanicsSolver still assumes pure linear
elasticity; ConstitutiveLaw::correct is never called.

The rheology port documents exactly what the mechanics layer must do
(rheology/mod.rs, "what the mechanics layer must do"):

1. Pass mechanical strain = total strain MINUS eigenstrain. Passing total strain
   makes an unconstrained, freely expanding pellet look highly stressed -- and it
   will then creep, which is silently and badly wrong.
2. Own one RheologyState per cell.
3. Call correct() repeatedly inside the outer corrector loop from the SAME
   start-of-step state; call advance() ONCE, after convergence. Advancing inside
   the loop double-counts inelastic strain.
4. The corrected stress is softer than the elastic one, so the displacement field
   is no longer in equilibrium -- re-solve with RheologyState::inelastic_strain()
   fed back as an additional eigenstrain (upstream's correctAdditionalStrain).
5. Bound the timestep with CreepTimeStepControl: the creep integration is
   implicit in stress but explicit in state.

Acceptance: a stress-relaxation case where a clamped bar under sustained strain
relaxes toward the creep-equilibrium stress, verified against the closed-form
exponential decay; and a case where free thermal expansion with creep active
produces NO creep strain (the eigenstrain-subtraction check in item 1).

Blocked by nothing -- both halves exist.

description: root@vm
title: root@vm
offbeat: mechanics must gate on MATPRO Zircaloy Poisson exceeding 0.5 above ~1355 K
description:
The ported MATPRO Zircaloy correlations fit Young's modulus and shear modulus as
independent lines, so nu = E/(2G) - 1 crosses the incompressible limit of 0.5 at
T = 1354.84 K and reaches 0.912 at 1800 K -- the top of upstream's own stated
validity range. At 600 K a retained cold-work fraction above 0.1197 does the same.

Consequence: lambda = E*nu/((1+nu)(1-2nu)) is singular at the crossover and
sign-flipped beyond it, and mechanics::LinearElastic::new rejects such constants
outright, so a hot-Zircaloy case will fail where upstream would silently produce
a garbage stiffness.

This is a faithful port of a real upstream defect, not a porting bug. Upstream
neither detects nor guards it.

PoissonRatioModel::is_admissible() was added for exactly this. The mechanics
layer needs to gate on it -- decide the policy: clamp below 0.5, fall back to a
constant Poisson's ratio, or refuse the case with a clear error. Maintainer call.

title: offbeat: deferred sub-models from the P3/P4 port (cracking, PyC anisotropy, PARFUME swelling, Lassmann burnup, relocation recovery)
description:
Deferrals recorded by the P3/P4 port agents, each documented in-file at the point
it applies. Collected here so they are not lost:

- Isotropic cracking (nCracks / sliceMapper / lhgr crack-softening) on the UO2,
  MOX and SCK-CEN Young's-modulus and UO2/MOX Poisson models. Needs damage-model
  state and a slice mapper, so not a pure function of MaterialState. All variants
  currently return the upstream nominal value.
- Transversely isotropic PyC: upstream itself returns the isotropic average
  (E_r + 2 E_t)/3 with a TODO. Real anisotropy needs a direction-dependent
  modulus in the mechanics layer.
- PARFUMEPyC thermal-expansion spherical-to-Cartesian tensor rotation: upstream
  does it in correct() using mesh_.C()[cellI]; it is a mesh operation and belongs
  in the mechanics assembly.
- swellingPARFUMEBuffer / swellingPARFUMEPyC: they integrate eps += rate*flux*dt,
  so they need fast flux and the timestep, plus a 2-D table interpolator in
  temperature x Bacon Anisotropy Factor and a 1-D one in coating density.
- burnupLassmann / burnupLassmannFBR (~75 KB): TUBRNP-style radial depletion
  solving a reduced Bateman chain for ~14 nuclides plus radial power
  reconstruction. That is neutronics and needs a flux solution.
- Axial-shape half of timeDependentAxialProfile: needs a mesh, pin direction and
  the profiles/ library.
- Relocation recovery (recoveryFraction/relaxRecovery), slice averaging, the
  max/min ratchets and the sensitivity scaling: history/mesh/contact logic.
- SCIANTIX physics: returns NotImplemented, never a silent zero. Separate
  MIT-licensed code with its own licence-provenance and V&V obligations.

Most of these are blocked on the same two things: the damage model and the
slice mapper. Worth sequencing them behind those rather than picking them off.

title: offbeat: source real literature validity ranges for correlations where the port chose its own
description:
Upstream states a validity range for only a handful of correlations: MatproZy
(273-1800 K), RelapZy (290-1800 K), MatproZy heat capacity (273-2099 K), IAEAZy
(273-2000 K), Banerjee (293-1273 K), SneadSiC (200-2400 K), Gehr (293 K cut-off),
IAEAZy density (1800 K), Zy emissivity (1500 K), Philipponneau (500 K lower
bound), HofmanD9, Tobbe, Watrous, and Lemehov's composition window.

Every other range in the port is a convention chosen by this crate, and each doc
comment says so explicitly rather than inventing a literature bound -- a test
asserts that no variant invents one.

Follow-up: source the real bounds from the literature (the oxide-fuel solidus
above all) and tighten them, replacing the port-chosen conventions. Until then
nobody should cite a range from this crate as a published limit.

title: outram-mc: root-cause the transport_csg stuck-history (MAX_EVENTS guard is a band-aid)
description: Before the MAX_EVENTS=100k/history cap, a reflective-infinite-medium k-eff hung (~9 CPU-min, one looping history). Find the geometry/nudge corner case (suspect: history stuck near a reflective plane/corner or coincident-surface re-cross in run_keff_csg) and fix properly; the cap currently leaks such histories (small bias).

notes.content: Root-cause analysis (2026-07-24, from the op-6tz.34 work). The reflective-corner stuck-history is grazing-incidence ping-pong: a particle moving nearly parallel to a reflective wall, near a corner, alternately hits the two/three perpendicular walls at sub-nudge distances. Each fixed 1e-9 cm nudge advances it only ~1e-9 cm ALONG the wall, so traversing an O(1 cm) feature needs ~1e9 bounces >> MAX_EVENTS=100k -> the history is capped and leaked (the band-aid). This is distinct from op-6tz.34 (now fixed): that was a lattice-edge/wall coincident tie leaking histories OUT of the box; this is in-corner non-progress. A PROPER fix (per this bead: do NOT extend the band-aid) needs OpenMC-style token-based surface tracking (advance exactly to the surface, resolve the next cell by surface index + sense, and compose a corner reflection off all coincident reflective surfaces in one event) rather than a fixed position nudge. That is a larger rework best done against the OpenMC reference source (not available in this sandbox), so leaving open with this analysis. The residual ~2% surface-vs-delta gap in the op-6tz.34 regression test is plausibly this effect.

notes.content: Root-cause fixed: new Geometry::compose_corner_reflection in geometry.rs, called from cross_surface reflective arm. At a reflective corner/edge (other reflective walls within 1e-9 cm of the crossing point) it now reflects off ALL coincident walls in one event (reflections compose at a corner = retroreflection) instead of ping-ponging 1e-9 cm/event. Sign-agnostic crossing test so min-side corners handled; lone-wall case bit-identical. Marked honestly as a robustness fix for this crate's fixed-nudge tracker (no C++ ref on host). Regression tests in triso.rs. Measured: grazing history 100003 events + 20 corner leaks to 4 events + 0 leaks; small U235 reflective cube surface 2.22235+/-0.00334 vs delta 2.21925+/-0.00320 = 0.67 sigma. Suite green: 95 lib + 26 notebooks, 0 fail. CAVEAT: worktree based on main, 658 behind develop; develop-only nested-lattice ~2pct residual not measurable here. Verified fix ports cleanly to develop (cross_surface + triso imports identical). Not committed.
notes.author: root@vm

notes.content: Fixed in 69d8874 (integrated onto claude/outram-mc-setup-cb1bg9, which has op-6tz.34). Root cause: cross_surface reflective arm reflected a grazing near-corner particle off only the primary wall; the fixed 1e-9 cm nudge left it headed into the perpendicular wall(s), re-crossing at sub-nudge distances (~1e5-1e9 events → MAX_EVENTS leak, negative bias). Fix: Geometry::compose_corner_reflection composes the specular reflection of every reflective/white/periodic surface coincident with the crossing point (|evaluate(r)|<=1e-9) that the particle actually crosses (|u·n|>0, sign-agnostic for min/max-side axis-aligned walls). Retroreflection at a right-angle corner → particle leaves in one event. Lone-wall case is bit-identical to surf.reflect. MAX_EVENTS/NUDGE untouched. Tests: corner_reflection_composes_at_exact_corner (unit), corner_grazing_history_terminates_without_pingpong (worst 100003→4 events, 20→0 leaks), corner_reflective_cube_surface_tracking_unbiased (surface 2.22235±0.00334 vs delta 2.21925±0.00320, 0.67σ). 158 lib + 30 notebook tests pass; op-6tz.34 nested-lattice test still green. CAVEAT: robustness fix for this crate's fixed-nudge tracker (not an OpenMC routine port — only the physics is mirrored); non-orthogonal corners compose order-dependently (approximate), axis-aligned cube/lattice corners exact.

description:
Offline demonstration digital twin of ORNL's Molten-Salt Reactor Experiment (MSRE, 1965-69) built on the OUTRAM PARK suite. Scope per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md: OFFLINE DEMONSTRATION / V&V / education only — no operational or live-plant coupling; MSRE is a public, decommissioned benchmark (ORNL-TM / ORNL-4xxx report series), so 'real time' means a real-time-capable simulation loop replaying/assimilating the historical record, not hardware monitoring. Architecture: two-tier. OFFLINE high-fidelity (MC k-eig + depletion via outram-mc-libs+njoy; CFD via outram-foam; molten-salt Gibbs FP thermochemistry) generates reduced-order tables/models. MSRE-specific hard physics: (1) circulating fuel => delayed-neutron precursors advect out of core (flow-dependent reactivity) - the defining effect; (2) Xe-135 gas stripping; (3) FP migration into three destinations (noble gases->off-gas, noble metals->plate on graphite/Hastelloy-N, salt-seekers->dissolved/precipitate) governed by salt redox (UF3/UF4).

Phasing: P0 zero-power circulating-fuel kinetics -> P1 add TH feedback -> P2 Xe+depletion -> P3 FP migration+chemistry -> P4 data assimilation. Each phase validates against a published MSRE dataset. All AI-assisted output is untrusted draft pending human V&V.

notes.content: Implemented cyclic (periodic) patch support (2026-08-04). V&V (verification, untrusted AI draft pending human review): cyclic diffusion == all-internal regular-n-gon ring mesh (operators identical A.x to <1e-12; solved fields agree <1e-9); periodic advection conserves (A.ones=0) and == ring; interpolate/sn_grad/vector-Laplacian seam checks. WHAT REPRODUCIBLE MUST MEAN HERE:
1. Every stage re-runnable from committed inputs WITHOUT re-running the stage above. Each hand-off is a real on-disk artefact with its own provenance, not an in-memory value. The MGXS library in particular must be a file a human can inspect and diff.
