title: chem-eng: IntegralController RampResponseRealTime loses precision on long real-time runs
description:
FOUND 2026-08-11 while doing op-fm5. NOT measured yet -- this is a code-reading finding, so it needs a measurement before it is acted on.

alpha_nightly/controllers/integral_controller/mod.rs, RampResponseRealTime::set_user_input_and_calc (:165-204). The integrator is kept as a line, y(t) = gradient_gain * t + offset, and each input change updates BOTH terms:

    gradient_change = a_i * k_c / tau_i
    offset_change   = -a_i * time_of_input * k_c / tau_i

That is already O(1) per step, so op-fm5 does not touch it. The concern is numerical, not algorithmic: offset accumulates a term proportional to the ABSOLUTE simulation time of every past input change, so for a long-running real-time simulation both 'gradient_gain * t' and 'offset' grow without bound while their SUM stays bounded. That is textbook catastrophic cancellation -- the significant digits available to the integrator output shrink as the run goes on. A real-time twin is exactly the use case where t gets large.

WHAT TO DO:
1. MEASURE FIRST. Drive an IntegralController for, say, 1e6 to 1e8 seconds of simulated time with a changing input, and compare against a Kahan-summed or periodically-rebased reference. Report the actual relative error growth. Do not act on the hunch alone.
2. If confirmed, the fix is to carry the accumulated integral directly (I += k_c/tau_i * u * dt, or the exact ZOH equivalent) rather than reconstructing it from a slope and an intercept, or to rebase the time origin periodically.

Relates to op-fm5 (transfer-function O(1) rewrite) and op-1z3o.14 (real-time execution).

title: cfmesh: fix tet-primal mesh quality — it is the real non-orthogonality source, not the dual
description:
Mesh non-orthogonality in the cfmesh pipeline traces to the TET PRIMAL, not to the dual operation or the solver. Fix the tet mesher.

EVIDENCE THAT THE DUAL IS EXACT (measured 2026-08-07, test re-run and passing):
crates/outram-foam-mesh/tests/poly_dual_mesh.rs:212 dual_quality_is_exactly_orthogonal_on_a_uniform_block asserts max_non_ortho_deg < 1e-12, mean < 1e-12, max_skewness < 1e-12 (:226-232). Re-ran `cargo test -p outram-foam-mesh --release --test poly_dual_mesh`: 3^3 block -> 64 dual cells, non-orthogonality max 0.000 deg / mean 0.000 deg, skewness 0.0000, verdict GOOD; 4^3 block identical. The metric itself is closed-form validated in crates/outram-foam-mesh/src/mesh_quality.rs:600 (Cartesian block = 0) and :651 (sheared block matches atan(k) at 45/60/86 deg to 1e-10).

IMPORTANT CORRECTION -- that test is NOT of cfmesh's dual. It exercises outram_foam_mesh::poly_dual_mesh, the CELL-CENTRE polyDualMesh (poly_dual_mesh.rs:25-41). cfmesh uses a DIFFERENT algorithm, the median/Donald vertex-centred dual (crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/dual.rs:48-70, which says so explicitly). cfmesh's four dual tests (dual.rs:441, :474, :499, :543) check only closure, volume conservation, boundary match and face count. So "the dual is exact" is MEASURED for outram-foam-mesh's dual and only INFERRED for cfmesh's.
=> First sub-task: add an orthogonality test for cfmesh's own median dual on a uniform block. Until that exists the diagnosis is one step short of proven.

WHAT IS KNOWN ABOUT THE TET PRIMAL:
- crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/tet.rs:93 pub fn tetrahedralize(mesh: &VolumeMesh) -- centroid subdivision (every cell -> cell.face.edge tets). Its two tests (tet.rs:169, :197) assert ONLY positive volume, closedness, boundary area = 6, volume = 1, 4 triangular faces per cell. No non-orthogonality or skewness metric is asserted on the tet primal anywhere in the tree.
- crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/delaunay.rs:42-44 states the defect qualitatively: centroid subdivision "is not a Delaunay one -- some interior faces fail the empty-circumsphere (locally-Delaunay) test, which is what leaves slivers."
- crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/pipeline.rs:774-775 records uniform 0.40 m -> max non-orth 85.14 deg and uniform 0.30 m -> 85.38 deg, and :804-805 notes those runs "report polyhedral dual skipped -- their output is the tetrahedralization". Dualised rows at the same geometry measure 71.7-72.5 deg. This supports the direction of the claim.
  CAVEAT: those ~85 deg figures are DOC-RECORDED, not test-asserted. The test at pipeline.rs:812 runs only two of the eight table rows and asserts merely max_non_orthogonality_deg < 90.0 (:842). Do not cite 85.14/85.38 as measured-by-CI.

WORK:
1. Add an orthogonality/skewness test for cfmesh's median dual on a uniform block (close the inference gap above).
2. Add non-orthogonality + skewness metrics to the tet primal tests in tet.rs.
3. Replace or repair centroid subdivision with a locally-Delaunay tetrahedralization (see delaunay.rs) so slivers are removed at source.

NOTED TENSION: the same fleet added a solver-side non-orthogonal correction -- crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/fv_operators/fvm/laplacian_corrected.rs (untracked) and crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/tests/non_orthogonal_laplacian.rs. So "do not chase a solver-side correction" is an editorial recommendation the tree currently contradicts. The maintainer should decide whether that correction stays (it is legitimate OpenFOAM practice regardless) -- the point of this bead is that it must not be treated as a SUBSTITUTE for fixing the tet mesher.

title: cfmesh: hardcoded /tmp in mesh_studio example + temp-dir cleanup leak (claim corrected)
description:
Recorded with the original claim CORRECTED -- the /tmp-exhaustion framing did not survive verification, but two smaller real defects did.

ORIGINAL CLAIM: cfmesh's polyMesh round-trip test resolves its temp dir from the system temp dir and fails on a small or full /tmp -- an Android/Termux hazard.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE (verified 2026-08-07):
- Location confirmed: crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/foam.rs:171, in test write_polymesh_disk_round_trip (:167-178):
      let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("cfmesh_polymesh_rt_{}", std::process::id()));
- BUT the data written is trivial. The mesh is cartesian_box(..., [2,2,2]) (:170) -- 8 cells, 12 internal + 24 boundary faces, 27 points (asserted :174-175). The written polyMesh is a few kilobytes. "Fails on a small /tmp" does not hold; only a completely full or unwritable temp dir would fail it.
- AND it is not hardcoded to /tmp. std::env::temp_dir() on Unix honours $TMPDIR, falling back to /tmp. Termux sets TMPDIR to its own prefix tmp, so on-device this resolves to Termux's writable temp. (Not verified on an actual device.)

TWO REAL DEFECTS THAT REMAIN:
1. A genuinely hardcoded /tmp exists ELSEWHERE: crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/examples/mesh_studio/main.rs:130
       export_dir: "/tmp/mesh_studio/polyMesh".into(),
   That one ignores $TMPDIR and would be wrong on Termux. (The example is Android-gated at :32-49, so it does not break the build -- but the path is still wrong for any non-/tmp TMPDIR, including some CI sandboxes.) Fix: use std::env::temp_dir().
2. Cleanup leak: foam.rs:177 `let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);` sits AFTER the assertions at :174-176, so a failing assertion leaks the directory. Fix: scope-guard the cleanup.

Note also that foam.rs has no target_os = "android" gate anywhere in src/ (only #[cfg(test)] at :103); the crate's only Android gates are Cargo.toml:36 (dev-deps) and examples/mesh_studio/main.rs:32/35/49. That is fine for this test as written, but worth knowing.

          -> [2] MGXS generation
          -> [3] deterministic multiphysics (GeN-Foam, decided over bedok)
          -> [4] PRKE + decay heat (teh-o-prke)

SCOPING DOCUMENT: docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md - read it before starting any child. It carries the benchmark definitions, the capability audit with file:line evidence, the hand-off data at each interface, the validation chain, the blockers and the ordered plan.

TWO HARD ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINTS:
1. REPRODUCIBLE. Every hand-off is an on-disk artefact with provenance; every run writes a manifest (workspace commit, XS library + version, fidelity tier, MC seed, particle/generation counts, group structure, homogenisation choice, mesh + its generation parameters); MC is bit-identical for a fixed seed; the chain is drivable headlessly.
2. FRONTEND-DRIVABLE. Entry point takes a geometry description plus a run configuration, so outram-blender can drive it as a third solver bridge (op-hzs.53). Not test-only.

VALIDATION CHAIN, every comparison quoted in pcm WITH the MC statistical uncertainty:
- rung 2/3 k_eff vs rung 1 k_eff on the same problem
- rung 4 beta_eff / Lambda / reactivity coefficients vs those collapsed directly from the rung 3 flux
- whole chain vs IAEA-TECDOC-1382 B1/B2/B3/B4 and the measured 123.06 cm loading

DO NOT report a k_eff, a pcm discrepancy or a beta_eff that was not computed. Nothing here is validated.

title: tampines-steam-tables: bounds-checked facade for the (h,s) flash family
description:
Remaining scope from op-dt3.26, which covered (p,s), the two-phase (T,p,x) family, alpha_v/kappa_t on both (T,p) and (p,h), and the TampinesSteamTableCV constructors, but deliberately left (h,s) uncovered rather than half-gate it.

STILL UNCOVERED, all panic-only:
  hs_flash_eqm::t_hs_eqm, p_hs_eqm, v_hs_eqm, x_hs_eqm, cp_hs_eqm, w_hs_eqm,
  kappa_hs_eqm, mu_hs_eqm, lambda_hs_eqm, tpvx_hs_flash_eqm, hs_flash_region,
  find_pressure_from_hs_region_4
  plus TampinesSteamTableCV::new_from_hs, which resolves pressure via p_hs_eqm
  and so inherits the whole surface.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN op-dt3.26. Unlike (p,h) and (p,s), the (h,s) panic surface is not two bound checks. Traced 2026-08-11, there are 26 distinct panic!/todo!/unimplemented! sites:

  - hs_flash_eqm/mod.rs:389,392 - global entropy band [-0.00858, 11.92] kJ/(kg K)
  - nine entropy-band sub-routers (hs_region_low_entropy_region_1_and_4 through
    hs_region_high_entropy_region_2a_only), lines 511,516,538,542,584,588,611,615,
    636,640,679,683,756,760,794,804,816,843,847,884,889,921,926 - each panics on an
    enthalpy bound computed by h_ps_eqm(p_hi, s) / h_ps_eqm(p_lo, s), i.e. by a
    (p,s) flash that itself panics
  - additional_temperature_check_for_1073_15_k_isotherm at 958,961,971,980 - two
    entropy bounds plus a resolved-temperature check that runs p_hs_2a/2b then
    t_ph_eqm (so it also inherits the (p,h) panic surface)
  - find_pressure_from_hs_region_4:1033 - 'Solution not bracketed by pressure
    bounds', a BISECTION FAILURE, not an envelope violation
  - mod.rs:365 unimplemented!('Region 5 does not have (h,s) flashing') - believed
    unreachable, no sub-router returns Region5; needs confirming, not assuming
  - validity_range.rs:50 todo!() in hs_is_below_isobar_p_100_mpa_in_region1 -
    reachable only if that fn is called with h <= 1670.9 kJ/kg and s <= 3.778
    kJ/(kg K); currently no caller inside the crate, but it is pub

A faithful gate therefore has to MIRROR the entropy-band dispatch, not add a bounds check: pick the same band, compute the same enthalpy bounds (running check_ps_envelope first so the h_ps_eqm calls are themselves safe), mirror the 1073.15 K isotherm check (with check_ph_envelope before its t_ph_eqm), and then gate the post-routing calls too, since tpvx_hs_flash_eqm goes on to call v_ps_eqm(p_resolved, s) and x_ph_flash(p_resolved, h) with a pressure that comes out of a backward equation.

The bisection panic at :1033 cannot be gated by any input bounds check. Recommend find_pressure_from_hs_region_4 be changed to return Result (a separate, non-additive change needing maintainer sign-off), or the checked (h,s) facade be documented as covering the envelope panics only - which by the op-dt3.26 no-half-gating rule means it should not ship until that is resolved.

REQUIRED PATTERN (unchanged from op-t647/op-dt3.26): no catch_unwind ever; NaN rejected explicitly; typed errors; uom on the public surface; doc comments stating physical quantity, valid range and units; a panic-site-to-gate table in the module doc; and a sweep of the accepted set proving zero leaked panics before the gate is called complete.

title: GPU torus quartic root-finder disagrees with CPU mirror (spurious near-zero root)
description:
Unmasked by fixing op-bjd on 2026-08-06. Before that fix, probe() requested downlevel limits, surf_dist.bgl was rejected, and gpu_matches_cpu_reference never executed a single query — so this defect was invisible.

With real adapter limits sourced, the kernel runs and 13 of 15 surface types agree within the 1e-3*(1+|cpu|) tolerance. The TORUS types do not.

First divergence (NVIDIA RTX A5000 / NVK / Vulkan, 2026-08-06):
  query 16033 = surface 12 (XTorus), origin 10, direction 1
  gpu = 0.0000003120881   cpu = 0.49672258   |diff| = 0.49672228   tol = 0.0014967227

Decoding: the test batch is 27 origins x 48 directions = 1296 queries per surface, so query index / 1296 = surface index. Surface 12/13/14 are XTorus/YTorus/ZTorus.

The GPU returns a spurious near-ZERO root where the CPU finds a real crossing at 0.497 — a classic quartic root-finder failure mode (f32 conditioning in collect_real_roots_f32 / quartic_real_roots_f32, or the bisection bracket, or the coincident-epsilon guard). The WGSL is supposed to be a line-by-line translation of the Rust f32 mirror, so the two should agree far more tightly than this; a 0.5-cm disagreement is a logic divergence, not rounding.

Investigation entry points:
  - src/gpu/shaders/surface_distance.wgsl (torus + quartic path)
  - src/gpu/surface_distance.rs:451 quartic_real_roots_f32, :466 torus_distance_f32, :370 collect_real_roots_f32
  - The exact failing case is reproducible: XTorus{x0:0,y0:0,z0:0,a:1.0,b:0.3,c:0.3}, origin index 10, dir(1,48).

CURRENT STATE: gpu::surface_distance::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_reference FAILS on a GPU host. That is a real defect, not flakiness — do NOT loosen the tolerance to make it pass (workspace guardrail). The new hybrid test deliberately excludes tori so it tests work-splitting rather than this bug.
acceptance_criteria: gpu_matches_cpu_reference passes for all 15 surface types on a GPU host at the existing tolerance, with no tolerance loosening.

notes.content:
ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED AND EXACTLY REPRODUCED, 2026-08-06. Three independent investigations converged.

MECHANISM (certain):
surface_distance.wgsl:298   let c0 = gc * gc - 4.0 * a2 * gamma;

For the failing ray the two operands are BIT-IDENTICAL f32 values (both 6.7599992752075195), i.e. 100% cancellation, all 24 mantissa bits lost. The true value is exactly 0 -- confirmed in exact rational arithmetic: gc^2 - 4*a2*gamma = 2.6^2 - 4*1.69 = 6.76 - 6.76 = 0.

- Rust does NOT contract mul+sub, so the CPU f32 mirror computes c0 = 0.0 exactly. The degenerate root stays at exactly 0 (measured -1.78e-15) and the t <= eps filter discards it. Correct answer 0.49672258 returned.
- The GPU backend IS permitted to fuse gc*gc - X into an FMA (one rounding instead of two), which keeps gc^2 exact and yields c0 = +2.2888184503244702e-07 -- about half an ULP of 6.76, a value not even representable as a difference of two f32 near 6.76.
- That perturbs the root at 0 to t = -c0/c1 = 3.1208810e-07. Running the full WGSL algorithm in float32 both ways:
    no FMA: c0=0           roots=[-1.78e-15, 0.49672258]  -> 4.967226e-01
    FMA:    c0=2.2888e-7   roots=[3.120881e-07, 0.49672228] -> 3.120881e-07
  EXACT match to the reported GPU value 3.120881e-7 (8 significant figures).

WHY THE ORIGIN MATTERS: the test origin (0,-1.3,0) lies EXACTLY on the torus outer equator (a+b = 1.0+0.3 = 1.3), so the quartic has an exact root at t=0 and c0 is exactly 0. The fixture passes coincident:false for a point that IS coincident.

THREE CONDITIONS, ALL TRUE:
1. Total cancellation makes c0 pure rounding noise whenever the origin is on the surface.
2. FMA contraction is legal AND UNCONTROLLABLE: grep -rn NoContraction over naga-29.0.3/29.0.4 returns NOTHING -- naga never emits the SPIR-V NoContraction decoration, so the driver is free to fuse. This is the entire CPU/GPU divergence; the algorithm is otherwise identical.
3. The filter at wgsl:302 is an ABSOLUTE eps = 1.0e-7, roughly 10x BELOW the measured f32 noise floor for this geometry: ulp(gc^2)/|c1| = 8e-7/0.733 = 1.1e-6. The f64 reference (geometry/surface.rs:880) uses 1e-10/1e-8; the f32 twin scaled eps by only 1000x while the noise floor grew by ~1e9x. Any c0 perturbation of half an ULP or more yields a root >= 1.6e-7, which ALWAYS passes.

Neither existing filter catches it: the spurious-branch test G(t) = +2.6 > 0 PASSES, so the fake root sits on the geometrically correct branch. The root-finder is NOT at fault -- it correctly returns a genuine root of the quartic it was handed.

EMPIRICAL SCOPE (independent agent, full 19440-query sweep on the real adapter):
- 79 mismatches / 19440 = 0.41%
- Non-torus surfaces 0-11: ZERO mismatches across 15552 queries. Completely clean.
- XTorus 70, ZTorus 9, YTorus 0.
- ALL 79 come from the 5 (surface, origin) pairs where the origin lies exactly on the torus (implicit residual 2.2e-16). Perfect correlation, no false positives or negatives.
- The GPU is NEVER larger and NEVER misses when the CPU hits. Every mismatch is a spurious tiny root: min 1.006e-7 (barely over the 1e-7 threshold), median 1.85e-7, max 3.5e-6.
- YTorus is clean ONLY because none of the 27 lattice origins happens to sit on it -- predicted from the mechanism alone: on-surface origin counts are XTorus 4/27, ZTorus 1/27, YTorus 0/27, exactly matching the observed failure pattern.
- The trusted f64 path agrees with the CPU f32 mirror in every case sampled (q16033: f64 = 4.96722659144033e-1, cpu_f32 = 4.9672258e-1, gpu = 3.12e-7). THE CPU IS THE CORRECT SIDE.

FIX CONSTRAINTS (things that will NOT work, established):
- Normalising the quartic changes nothing: c4 = ga^2 = 1.0 exactly here, the quartic is already monic, and all coefficients are O(1). Nothing overflows or underflows f32.
- Disabling FMA is not available: naga emits no NoContraction decoration.
- Reformulating c0 as a difference of squares (gc-2a*sqrt(gamma))(gc+2a*sqrt(gamma)) only halves the error -- gc and 2a*sqrt(gamma) are themselves 2.6 vs 2.6, still cancelling. Not a real fix.

FIX MUST ADDRESS THE NOISE FLOOR. Candidates:
(a) Snap c0 to exactly 0 when |c0| is at or below the rounding noise of the cancelled subtraction, e.g. |c0| <= K * ulp(gc*gc). Directly cancels the FMA artifact and restores CPU/GPU agreement at the source.
(b) Make eps RELATIVE to the conditioning: eps = max(current, K * ulp(max|coeff|)/|c1|), i.e. track the ~1.1e-6 noise floor rather than a fixed 1e-7.
(c) Both. Apply the same change to the Rust f32 mirror so the twin stays a twin.

NOTE this is only partly a fixture artifact. A real transport run has particles sitting on and just off surfaces constantly, so the on-surface case is the norm, not a corner. Also: with coincident:true the eps becomes 1e-5, which WOULD filter 3.12e-7 -- so a caller that correctly flags coincidence escapes the bug.
notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-06. Verified on NVIDIA RTX A5000 / NVK GA102 / Vulkan.

TWO CHANGES, applied IDENTICALLY to both sides (shaders/surface_distance.wgsl and the Rust f32 mirror in gpu/surface_distance.rs), because the whole defect was the two drifting apart:

1. SNAP c0 TO ZERO BELOW ITS OWN ROUNDING NOISE.
   c0_raw = gc*gc - 4*a2*gamma
   c0_noise = C0_CANCELLATION_ULPS * F32_EPS * max(|gc*gc|, |4*a2*gamma|)
   c0 = 0 when |c0_raw| <= c0_noise
   Below that threshold the value carries no information -- it is indistinguishable from zero in f32 -- so this removes the FMA-vs-two-rounding divergence at source rather than downstream.

2. MAKE THE ROOT GATE TRACK THE NOISE FLOOR instead of sitting under it.
   eps = max(base_eps, min(c0_noise / |c1|, EPS_CAP))
   A residual perturbation dc0 displaces a simple root near zero by dc0/|c1|. The old fixed 1.0e-7 sat roughly an order of magnitude BELOW the measured f32 noise floor (~1.1e-6) for cm-scale torus geometry, so noise roots always passed. EPS_CAP = 1.0e-3 cm (10 um) stops a near-zero c1 from widening the gate enough to swallow a real crossing.

New shared constants, spelled identically on both sides (WGSL has no f32::EPSILON): F32_EPS = 1.1920929e-7, C0_CANCELLATION_ULPS = 4.0, EPS_CAP = 1.0e-3.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES (all established during investigation, recorded so they are not retried):
- Normalising the quartic: c4 = ga^2 = 1.0 exactly here, it is already monic and all coefficients are O(1). Would change nothing.
- Disabling FMA: naga emits no NoContraction decoration anywhere, so contraction is not controllable from the shader.
- Reformulating c0 as a difference of squares (gc - 2a*sqrt(gamma))(gc + 2a*sqrt(gamma)): gc and 2a*sqrt(gamma) are themselves 2.6 vs 2.6, so it still cancels. Halves the error at best.

RESULT: gpu::surface_distance::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_reference PASSES over all 19440 queries and all 15 surface types. Previously 79 mismatches (XTorus 70, ZTorus 9, YTorus 0, non-torus 0 of 15552). Full crate suite: 197 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored. cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android clean.

NO TOLERANCE WAS LOOSENED -- the test's pass criterion is unchanged at |gpu-cpu| <= 1e-3*(1+|cpu|). The kernel now produces the right answer.

title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
WGSL/Rust capacity mismatch: crits[3] OOB read and bp[5] OOB write when the derivative cubic reports 4 roots
description:
Found independently by two agents auditing the GPU surface-distance kernel, 2026-08-06. Latent, NOT the cause of op-9s8.11, but a genuine CPU/GPU divergence waiting for a degenerate cubic.

CAPACITY MISMATCH: the Roots struct in WGSL holds array<f32,4> and push_unique caps at "out.n < 4u" (wgsl:35, :77). The Rust mirror declares "let mut crit = [0.0f32; 3]" (surface_distance.rs:458) and push_unique_f32 caps at out.len() = 3. So the WGSL side can report FOUR critical points where Rust can only report three.

A cubic cannot HAVE 4 real roots, but collect_real_roots can REPORT 4: up to 3 bracketed roots plus critical points passing the residual test, when f32 noise splits a clustered triple root by more than push_unique's dedup radius of 1.0e-5 * (1.0 + abs(r)).

REPRODUCED by random search (400k trials):
  cubic_real_roots(1.0, -2.30112, 1.19506, -0.179715) returns n = 4
    -> [0.33104599, 0.33115199, 0.33128500, 1.63881624]
    true roots: 0.331034, 0.331270, 1.638816
  The three cluster members are ~1e-4 apart, wider than the 1.33e-5 dedup radius.

CONSEQUENCE when crit3.n == 4 (wgsl:227-228 passes ncr=4 alongside a 3-element crits array):
  - wgsl:141-143 and :150-152 read crits[3] -- out of bounds on array<f32,3>
  - wgsl:147-153 build bp with nb = 1 + 4 + 1 = 6, so bp[5] is an out-of-bounds WRITE on array<f32,5>, and the loop at wgsl:157 then reads bp[5]

WGSL bounds-CLAMPS rather than trapping, so this corrupts silently: the final breakpoint becomes crits[3] instead of +m, one interval collapses to zero width, and roots beyond the last critical point are MISSED -- wrong distance or INF returned with no diagnostic.

The Rust mirror cannot hit this: its capacity-3 cap makes the state unreachable. That asymmetry is the bug.

FIX DIRECTION: make the capacities agree. Either size the WGSL crits array to 4 and bp to 6, or cap push_unique at 3 on the cubic path so WGSL matches Rust. Whichever is chosen, apply it to BOTH sides -- the two are supposed to be twins.
acceptance_criteria: WGSL and Rust root-buffer capacities agree; a cubic that reports 4 critical points cannot index out of bounds on either side; regression test covers the clustered-triple-root cubic above.

notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-06, in the same pass as op-9s8.11 (same two files, same class of defect: WGSL and the Rust mirror drifting apart).

Both sides now clamp the cubic's root count to the mathematical maximum:
  const MAX_CUBIC_REAL_ROOTS = 3
  WGSL cubic_real_roots: out.n = min(out.n, MAX_CUBIC_REAL_ROOTS) before returning
  Rust cubic_real_roots_f32: .min(MAX_CUBIC_REAL_ROOTS) on the returned count

That is what keeps quartic_real_roots' 3-element crits array and collect_real_roots' 5-element bp array in bounds: with ncr <= 3, nb reaches at most 1 + 3 + 1 = 5, so bp[5] is never written and crits[3] is never read.

On the Rust side the caller's 3-slot buffer already bounded the count, so the clamp is normally a no-op there -- it is stated explicitly so the invariant is enforced the same way on both sides, rather than resting on a buffer size on one side and nothing at all on the other. That asymmetry was the bug.

Verified: full crate suite 197 passed, 0 failed; cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android clean.

NOT directly regression-tested: the trigger needs a cubic whose clustered triple root splits by more than push_unique's dedup radius (the reproducer found by random search was cubic_real_roots(1.0, -2.30112, 1.19506, -0.179715) -> n = 4). A targeted unit test for that input would be worth adding; filing that thought here rather than claiming coverage we do not have.
notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

description: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
WGSL relies on an unenforced ascending-order invariant that the Rust mirror enforces with an explicit sort
description:
Minor, found while diffing the WGSL kernel against its Rust f32 mirror, 2026-08-06. Behaviourally equivalent today; an unenforced invariant.

Rust surface_distance.rs:460 explicitly sorts:
    sort_small_f32(&mut crit[..nc]);

WGSL surface_distance.wgsl:226 does not, carrying only a comment:
    // crit3 is already ascending from collect_real_roots / quadratic fallback.

The comment is CORRECT today: both cubic_real_roots exits return ascending order (sort_roots at wgsl:175, and the quadratic_real_roots fallback which emits min/max at wgsl:200-201). So this is not currently a divergence in behaviour.

It is worth recording because collect_real_roots in WGSL relies on the breakpoint array bp being strictly increasing, and that holds ONLY if crits is ascending. The invariant is load-bearing but enforced on one side by an explicit sort and on the other by a comment. A future change to either cubic exit path breaks the GPU silently while the CPU stays correct.

FIX DIRECTION: either add the explicit sort to WGSL so both sides enforce it the same way, or add an assertion/comment on the Rust side that the sort is redundant -- but make the two agree on WHY the invariant holds.

title: Resume tutoring: rhoPimpleFoam momentum discretisation -> a_P u_P = H - grad(p) -> HbyA -> pressure equation
description:
TUTORING CHECKPOINT (one-step Socratic style per .claude/skills/tutor). Goal: teach the author rhoPimpleFoam's pressure-based algorithm from first principles, feeding (a) a new appendix section 'rhoPimpleFoam basic equations' and (b) understanding of op-26w Part 2 (compressibility psi = drho/dp|_h, why frozen isothermal kappa_T ~100x too small in the dome causes the plateau OVERSHOOT).

WHERE WE PAUSED: just wrote the continuous compressible momentum equation d(rho u)/dt + div(rho u u) = -grad(p) + div(mu grad u), labelled 4 terms (time, convection, pressure, viscous). Paused at the anchor question: identify the 3 'transport skeleton' terms (time+convection+viscous -> a_P, a_N, old-time) vs the 1 odd-one-out source (pressure).

NEXT STEPS (in order): (1) discretise momentum term-by-term into a_P u_P = H(u) - grad(p); (2) rearrange -> u_P = HbyA - rAU grad(p), with rAU=1/a_P, HbyA=H(u)/a_P (the code term that confused the author); (3) substitute the face velocity/flux into discrete continuity to BUILD the pressure equation (this closes the 'pressure is the orphan, continuity pins it' thread); (4) return to Part 2: compressibility psi and the plateau overshoot.

ALREADY COVERED & SOLID: Part 1 energy conservation fully derived by author (conservative vs non-conservative ddt differ by h*r; r=discrete continuity residual; rho_cont=rho_old-(dt/V)sum(phi.A) forces r=0). Author also patched the results-section discrete continuity eqn (added V_cell and face area vectors). FV diffusion stencil (rod example, a_P=a_E+a_W, Fick 2nd law) understood.

APPENDIX NOTE: 'rhoPimpleFoam basic equations' is textbook -- cite Jasak thesis, Ferziger & Peric, OpenFOAM programmer's guide; present as re-derived established background, NOT original, to keep novelty claims on the solver fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Author can derive a_P u_P = H - grad(p), HbyA, and the pressure equation unaided; appendix 'rhoPimpleFoam basic equations' drafted with textbook citations; then resume op-26w Part 2 (psi).

title: OpenFOAM upstream build not viable in remote container: background jobs reaped on idle
description:
Attempted to compile OpenFOAM Foundation dev (vendored at crates/outram-foam-turbulence-lib/upstream_source/OpenFOAM) in the Claude Code remote container, in order to run the incompressibleDriftFlux/dahl and multiphaseEuler/bubbleColumn coarse tutorials.

SETUP THAT WORKED: apt-installed flex + OpenMPI; built the wmake bootstrap tools (wmkdep, dirToString) via wmake/src/make; worked around the clone being named "OpenFOAM" while etc/bashrc expects "OpenFOAM-$WM_PROJECT_VERSION" by symlinking /opt/foam/OpenFOAM-dev to the vendored tree -- placed OUTSIDE the repo so build artifacts land in the gitignored dir and git status stays clean. Compilation itself is clean: zero real compile errors across ~1650 objects and 31 libraries.

BLOCKER: long-running background builds do not survive. Two launches died mid-build during idle gaps between turns (first ~35 min in, second ~8 min in). This is NOT resource exhaustion: no OOM entries, 14 GB RAM free, 19 GB disk free. setsid + nohup + detaching to PPID 1 did not help. Measured directly: a 9.3-minute FOREGROUND tool call advanced the build (objects 1618 to 1654, libs 28 to 31), while equivalent idle wall-clock advanced it by zero. Conclusion: the container only executes work while a tool call is active.

COST TO FINISH IN FOREGROUND: ~3800 of 5440 source files remain; at the observed rate in the current template-heavy stage that is roughly 4-16 hours of ACTIVE tool time (~25-100 dedicated 9.5-minute calls doing nothing but waiting). Not a sensible use of a session.

DIAGNOSTIC TRAP (cost an hour): pgrep -f make returns false positives because the claude process's own command line contains the word "make". Check liveness with: ps -eo pid,ppid,args | grep '[b]uild2.sh' and require PPID 1.

NOT BLOCKED, ALREADY DELIVERED (commit ce4bd82): the OUTRAM PARK equivalent V&V cases for all three targets, built from the upstream inputs verbatim, all passing -- GeN-Foam 1-D slab k_eff = 1.000008 vs analytical 1.000004 (0.4 pcm); dahl drift-flux settling 1.137e-3 m/s with the upstream simple closure reproduced exactly; bubbleColumn six-equation terminal slip 0.292 m/s with Schiller-Naumann drag.

SUGGESTED RESOLUTION: run the two OpenFOAM tutorials on a normal workstation and commit their reference output (mesh stats, alpha/U/T fields at the reported times) into the repo as stored benchmarks, so the Rust ports can be regression-compared without needing OpenFOAM in CI or in the container. Same pattern as the GeN-Foam/ESI bead.

ONE FINDING WAS DECODED FROM THE CIPHER AND IS FLAGGED AS SUCH in docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 7.2: the paper states that large differences have been reported between ENDF/B-VII.0 and ENDF/B-VII.1 results for HTR-10, 'almost exclusively caused by an update in the carbon capture cross section', citing Bostelmann and Strydom (2015). That matters directly - every published HTR-10 value we compare against is ENDF/B-VII.0 (INET's MCNP-4A work is ENDF/B-V), so a calculation on ENDF/B-VIII.0 is not comparing like-for-like. IT SHOULD BE RE-CHECKED AGAINST THE PDF before being relied on.

The PDF itself is fine - crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/tantillo2020hcpneutronics.pdf. This is a conversion problem, not a source problem. PROPRIETARY tier (Elsevier): re-ingest for our own use, do not re-host.

description:
ACTION ON THE MAINTAINER. The maintainer will supply digitised data points read off the decay-heat graphs in Tobias, A., "Decay heat", Progress in Nuclear Energy. These become the GOLDEN ORACLE for two separate pieces of work at once:

1. THE DECAY-HEAT MODEL (crates/teh-o-prke/src/decay_heat.rs). As of 2026-08-11 that module implements the 23-group 1978 draft ANS Standard fit from Tobias Table 16, and its unit tests verify the implementation against the paper OWN EQUATIONS (eq. 32 burst function, eq. 33 integral form) plus the total decay energy per fission. That is VERIFICATION - is it implemented correctly - and nothing more. There is currently NO comparison against an independent curve. Digitised plot points would turn this into a real check: reconstruct the published decay-heat curve from the 23-group parameters and compare against the digitised points from the same paper figures.

2. THE KOVAN GRAPH DIGITISER (see the sibling bead). The same digitised points are the acceptance test for the digitiser itself: run the digitiser over the Tobias figures and compare its output against the maintainer hand-digitised values. A digitiser with no ground truth is unfalsifiable.

WHY ONE DATASET SERVES BOTH: it is the same figures. Points read by hand validate the tool; the tool then scales to figures nobody wants to read by hand.

WHAT IS NEEDED, per figure supplied:
- which figure (number and page) in which document
- the axis calibration used (linear or log on each axis, and the two reference points per axis)
- the digitised (x, y) pairs
- an estimate of reading uncertainty - on a log axis this is NOT uniform and matters
- who digitised it and when

PROVENANCE (DATA_POLICY.md): digitisation is a PROCESSING STEP and must be documented as one. The scoping docs already flag that HTR-10 safety demonstration test data will arrive as digitised plots rather than tables, so getting this discipline right here pays off later.

The Tobias source PDF is at kovan_import/decay heat tobias.pdf and has NOT yet been catalogued into kovan - its access tier needs deciding first (Progress in Nuclear Energy is Elsevier, so most likely proprietary; the numerical parameters are facts and usable either way, only redistribution of the PDF is gated).

description:
crates/outram-foam-turbulence-lib has no usable wall functions, and the consequence is measured.

WHAT EXISTS: crates/outram-foam-turbulence-lib/src/wall_functions/mod.rs is the entire wall-function surface -- three free functions, y_plus (:37), u_tau (:50), nu_t_wall (:76). There is NO nutkWallFunction, kqRWallFunction, omegaWallFunction, epsilonWallFunction or nutUWallFunction implementation; those names appear only in prose (docs/model-reference.md:41, src/k_epsilon/mod.rs:59-60, README). Confirmed: a workspace-wide grep finds ZERO call sites for nu_t_wall / u_tau / y_plus outside the defining module, and the module contains ZERO #[test] functions.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE (re-run 2026-08-07, reproduced verbatim):
crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/tests/turbulence_coupling.rs, lid-driven cavity, genuinely Re = 100 (:234-235: 400 cells, U_lid = 1 m/s, nu = 1e-3 m^2/s, L = 0.1 m), Wilcox k-omega:

    => nu_t/nu = 257.4 to 330.2
    max |U_kOmega - U_laminar| = 2.249334e-1 m/s
A turbulent viscosity 257-330x the molecular value in a laminar Re=100 cavity is physically absurd and is the signature of a missing wall treatment.
(File the exact figure 257.4-330.2; the "260-330" recorded at turbulence_coupling.rs:46 and :264 rounds 257.4 up.)

SECOND DEFECT: the test PRINTS those values but asserts only finiteness and nu_t > 0 (:346-357). The magnitude is not gated, so a regression would not fail CI. Add a magnitude gate.

WORK:
1. Implement the standard wall functions as patch boundary conditions and wire them into the models.

MAINTAINER DECISION: full-text ingestion of TDM/AI-reserved publications (huang2025waterIngress is the pending case)
description:
crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/huang2025waterIngress.json (Huang et al. 2025, 'The water ingress analysis on steam generator heat-exchange tube rupture accident of HTGR', Ann. Nucl. Energy 211:110968, doi 10.1016/j.anucene.2024.110968) carries this copyright line:

  (c) 2024 Elsevier Ltd. All rights reserved, INCLUDING THOSE FOR TEXT AND DATA MINING, AI TRAINING, AND SIMILAR TECHNOLOGIES.

That is an explicit TDM/AI reservation, stronger than the plain all-rights-reserved notices on the older Elsevier papers in the archive. kovan lit import performs bulk full-text extraction into a machine-readable corpus, which is arguably exactly what the clause reserves. Full-text extraction was therefore deliberately SKIPPED at ingest (2026-08-11): the record is bibliographic metadata plus factual findings only (facts and numbers are not copyrightable expression).

DECISION NEEDED (AI_USAGE.md / DATA_POLICY.md): is full-text ingestion of TDM-reserved publications acceptable for this project? If NO, the record stands as-is and the paper is read by humans and cited normally. If YES under some rationale, the body can be extracted then.

AUDIT RESULT (librarian pass 2026-08-11): every proprietary PDF was grepped for the clause ('text and data mining' / 'AI training' / 'similar technologies'). ONLY huang2025waterIngress carries it. gao2002, wu2002, wang2014, tantillo2020, xhonneux2014, tobias1980: zero hits — their earlier full-text ingests do not retroactively violate an explicit reservation. Do not delete anything; nothing needs deleting per this audit.

notes.content:
MAINTAINER DECISION 2026-08-11: the metadata-only approach for huang2025waterIngress is APPROVED. Maintainer: 'I think you made the right decision on huang2025.'

So the standing rule for a document whose copyright line reserves text and data mining / AI training rights: catalogue the bibliographic metadata and the factual findings, and DO NOT run bulk full-text extraction into the corpus. The paper stays fully usable — read it, cite it, implement correlations from it, record its numbers with provenance, because facts are not copyrightable. Only the machine-readable full-text corpus is withheld.

Currently affected: huang2025waterIngress ALONE. A grep audit of all seven proprietary PDFs on 2026-08-11 found the clause in no other document; the earlier full-text ingests (wu2002, gao2002, wang2014, tantillo2020, xhonneux2014, tobias1980) carry no such reservation and need no action.

REMAINING WORK on this bead: make the rule enforceable rather than remembered. A future ingest should DETECT the reservation clause and refuse or warn, instead of relying on whoever is ingesting to read the copyright page carefully. Grep terms that caught it: 'text and data mining', 'AI training'. That check belongs next to the visibility inference in the ingestion path.

title: outram-mc-libs: surf_dist bind group exceeds max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage (GPU test fails)
description:
Found by the full workspace test run 2026-08-04. Test: gpu::surface_distance::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_reference. Suite otherwise green (163 passed, 1 failed, 2 ignored).

ERROR:
  wgpu error: Validation Error
   In Device::create_bind_group_layout, label = 'surf_dist.bgl'
     Too many bindings of type StorageBuffers in Stage ShaderStages(COMPUTE),
     limit is 4, count was 7. Check the limit max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage
     passed to Adapter::request_device

SITE: crates/outram-mc-libs/src/gpu/surface_distance.rs:861 (the 'surf_dist.bgl' layout).

NOT AN ENVIRONMENT PROBLEM: other GPU tests in this same crate pass on this machine (gpu::batched_flight::tests::gpu_lcg_state_matches_cpu, gpu::xs_interp::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_reference, gpu::union_grid::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_native_union), so an adapter is present and working. This layout specifically asks for more storage buffers than the device was granted.

TWO FIXES, DIFFERENT CONSEQUENCES -- pick deliberately:
  (a) Request a higher max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage when creating the device. Works if the hardware supports it, but silently narrows which GPUs can run this kernel, and wgpu's downlevel/WebGL tier caps this at 4. Check what limits Adapter::request_device is currently called with -- if it is using defaults, that is likely the whole story.
  (b) Pack the 7 storage buffers into 4 or fewer (combine into a single buffer with offsets, or move read-only data into a uniform/storage-texture). Portable across every adapter tier, more work.

Note the CPU path is the trusted/deterministic reference in this workspace and GPU is acceleration only, so this does not affect correctness of results -- but the test is genuinely failing and the GPU surface-distance path is unusable on any adapter with a 4-buffer limit.

Deferred by the maintainer 2026-08-04 (the sibling boon-lay WGSL reserved-keyword failure was fixed immediately in the same session).

notes.content:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED, 2026-08-06.

The limit was self-imposed, not hardware. src/gpu/mod.rs probe() requested wgpu::Limits::downlevel_defaults(), which pins max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage to 4. surf_dist.bgl binds 7 storage buffers (bindings 0-5 and 7; binding 6 is a uniform), so create_bind_group_layout rejected it.

What the hardware actually reports on this machine (sourced at runtime, not assumed):
  adapter                              NVIDIA RTX A5000 (NVK GA102), Vulkan, Discrete
  max_storage_buffers_per_shader_stage 524288   (wgpu's view; vulkaninfo maxPerStageDescriptorStorageBuffers reports 1048576 -- wgpu applies its own cap)
  max_storage_buffer_binding_size      2147483644
  max_buffer_size                      2147483648
  max_compute_invocations_per_workgroup 1024
  max_compute_workgroups_per_dimension  65535
  cpu_threads                          32 (i9-13900K, 24C/32T)

So we were asking for 7 against a self-imposed ceiling of 4 on a device that allows 524288.

FIX: probe() now requests adapter.limits() -- always satisfiable by definition, so it cannot fail where the old call succeeded. GpuContext gained a  field carrying the sourced GpuLimits.

NEW MODULE src/gpu/capabilities.rs (12 tests, all passing, builds on Android since it holds no wgpu types):
  - GpuLimits / DeviceClass / HardwareCapabilities -- limits read from adapter.limits() + get_info(), CPU threads from available_parallelism()
  - supports_storage_buffers(n) -- ask BEFORE building a layout; a device that genuinely cannot host the kernel now falls back to CPU instead of panicking
  - max_chunk_items(stride, workgroup_size) -- dispatch chunking from binding-size AND workgroup-count limits (4194240 queries here)
  - plan_split(...) -> WorkSplit with a SplitReason, guaranteeing gpu_items + cpu_items == total

HYBRID PATH: surface_distance_hybrid() splits a batch across both devices -- CPU half on a rayon parallel iterator inside a scoped thread while this thread drives the GPU dispatch, so they genuinely overlap. Auto policy gives a discrete GPU 0.75 and the CPU 0.25 (integrated 0.5/0.5; software adapter 0.0 since it IS the cpu). Those Auto constants are device-class heuristics, NOT measurements -- measured_gpu_fraction(gpu_rate, cpu_rate) is provided to compute the real ratio from a benchmark and feed it back as SplitPolicy::GpuFraction.

NOT CLOSING THIS BEAD YET: gpu_matches_cpu_reference still fails, but for a DIFFERENT and newly-visible reason -- the GPU torus quartic root-finder disagrees with the CPU mirror. Filed separately. This bead's specific defect (bind group exceeds the limit) is resolved; close it when you are satisfied that separation is right.

title: kovan-literature: expose public identifier derivation + extraction progress/provenance hooks
description:
Found while building the kovan-tui Ingest tab (interactive PDF import with a metadata review step), 2026-08-05.

Three gaps in kovan-literature's public API that kovan-tui had to work around:

1. NO PUBLIC IDENTIFIER DERIVATION (the important one). make_slug/make_id are private in crates/kovan-literature/src/metadata.rs and run exactly once inside extract_metadata. After a human corrects a wrong year/author, there is no way to ask the library to re-derive slug and id, so kovan-tui MIRRORS both functions in crates/kovan-tui/src/tui/ingest/metadata.rs (kept byte-for-byte compatible, pinned by a test reproducing the library's own doe2021test case). Real duplication that will drift. Proposed fix: pub fn derive_identifiers(doc: &mut KovanDocument) (or slug_for/id_for free functions) so both the TUI and any future corrector call the same code.

2. NO PROGRESS REPORTING. extract_metadata / pdf_to_markdown are all-or-nothing blocking calls with no callback and no page counter, so a UI can only show elapsed time (kovan-tui runs it on a worker thread and shows elapsed + a spinner, deliberately never a fabricated percentage). A per-page callback or an iterator over pages would let a real progress indicator exist honestly.

3. NO PER-FIELD PROVENANCE / CONFIDENCE. extract_metadata knows which source each field came from (Info dictionary, eScholarship cover page, text fallback) but discards it, so a reviewer cannot see which fields are guesses. Exposing e.g. title_source/year_source would make review screens sharper — arguably what a documented best-effort extractor owes its reviewer.

Motivating real case: importing the 1977 Argonne report ANL-7416 Supplement 2 yields title correct, year 2004 (the scanner's digitisation date), empty authors (real corporate author: Argonne Code Center), slug 2004anl7416. Correcting it in the TUI must produce argonnecodecenter1977anl7416 — which today needs the mirrored algorithm.

Context: crates/kovan-tui/DECISIONS.md, section 'Ingestion pass' (2026-08-05).

title: tampines-steam-tables: IF97 region router PANICS at exactly p = 100 MPa above 623.15 K
description:
A REAL PANIC BUG, not a documentation issue. Found 2026-08-11 while building the bounds-checked facade for op-t647; the facade had to exclude the point rather than fix it, because the fix belongs in the router.

THE DEFECT. In region_fwd_eqn_single_phase, the Region-2 and Region-3 dispatch arms use a HALF-OPEN pressure range `..100e6`. So p = 100 MPa exactly matches no arm and falls through the match, panicking, for any T above 623.15 K. At or below 623.15 K the point is accepted, so the failure is temperature-dependent and easy to miss.

THE KNOCK-ON, WHICH IS WORSE. Every (p,h) call at exactly 100 MPa panics, regardless of enthalpy — because the 1073.15 K isotherm helper internally evaluates h_tp_eqm_single_phase(1073.15 K, p), which lands in the broken arm. So the entire (p,h) family has an exclusive pressure ceiling for a reason that has nothing to do with (p,h).

100 MPa is the upper pressure bound of the IAPWS-IF97 validity region, so this is exactly the boundary a caller sweeping to the edge of the envelope will hit, and exactly the value someone writes when testing limits.

LIKELY FIX: `..100e6` should be `..=100e6` in the Region-2 and Region-3 arms. Verify against IAPWS-IF97 whether 100 MPa is inclusive in the standard (it is the stated upper limit, so it should be), then check every other range literal in the router for the same half-open/closed slip. Add a test that walks the exact envelope corners — p_min, p_max, T_min, T_max and their combinations — since that is the class of case no existing test covers.

INTERIM STATE: interfaces::checked (landed in commit 4feb6c84) documents and excludes the point, returning a typed error rather than panicking. That makes the facade safe but leaves the underlying router wrong, so anything calling the raw functions is still exposed.

title: outram-foam: Backward (BDF2) is not 2nd-order — ddtCorr is Euler-only while rAU uses 1.5V/dt
description:
The Backward (BDF2) time scheme is not delivering second-order accuracy, because the Rhie-Chow ddtCorr is hardcoded Euler while rAU picks up BDF2's 1.5V/dt diagonal. The two are inconsistent by a factor tending to 1.5 as dt -> 0.

ALL THREE PIECES, from source (verified 2026-08-07):

1. BDF2 coefficients -- crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/solvers/schemes.rs:126-131
       mat.ldu.diag[c] += 1.5 * v / dt;
       mat.source[c]   += (u_old.internal[c] * 2.0 - u_oo.internal[c] * 0.5) * (v / dt);

2. ddt_corr is hardcoded Euler regardless of scheme -- crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/fv_operators/fvc/ddt_corr.rs:58-74. It takes NO scheme argument: `let r_dt = 1.0 / dt;` (:67), `coeff * phi_corr * r_dt` (:73). Its own doc (:28, :53-57) says "Rhie-Chow time-derivative flux correction (Euler scheme) ... Mirrors EulerDdtScheme<Type>::fvcDdtPhiCorr".

3. rAU picks up the BDF2 diagonal -- crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/solvers/pimple_foam/mod.rs:394-412. u_eqn = ddt_term + div_term + ... (:394); let a = u_eqn.a_field() (:397), and a_field() returns the raw diagonal (crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/ldu_matrix/fv_vector_matrix.rs:109-121); then mesh.cell_volumes[c] / a_data[c] (:401). With Backward selected that diagonal contains 1.5*V/dt. The two are combined at :430-431 (rauf = fvc::interpolate(&rau); ddt_corr = fvc::ddt_corr(&u_old, &phi_old, dt)) and added to phiHbyA at :462.

NO ORDER-OF-ACCURACY TEST EXISTS for any ddt scheme. The only two Backward tests are:
- schemes.rs:275 backward_ddt_matches_the_bdf2_formula -- asserts COEFFICIENTS only (diag = 15, source_x = 35 at dt = 0.1), plus Euler fallback on start-up and SteadyState = zero. Algebra check, not a temporal convergence study.
- crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/tests/fv_scheme_selection.rs:342 backward_ddt_selection_is_live_and_not_worse_against_ghia -- asserts only that the run stays finite, that the selection is live (d_transient > 1e-9), and rms_b <= rms_e + 1e-4 with rms_b < 0.10. Its own doc (:338-341) says it "deliberately does not assert steady-state equivalence, because that is currently false."

MEASURED (re-ran cargo test --release --test fv_scheme_selection backward_ddt_selection):
    max |U_backward - U_euler|: transient (5 steps) = 2.829482e-2 m/s, long-time (12 s) = 1.649884e-2 m/s
    Ghia Re=100 centreline RMS at 12 s: Euler 0.0363, Backward 0.0359
This matches the dt = 4e-3 row of the doc table exactly.

HONESTY CAVEAT: the dt sweep at fv_scheme_selection.rs:303-308 (1.0394e-2 @ 8e-3 -> 2.9258e-2 @ 1e-3, i.e. the discrepancy GROWS as dt is refined -- the signature of an order-inconsistency) is a DOC-COMMENT RECORD of a manual sweep. The shipped test runs only dt = 4e-3 and asserts nothing about the trend. Only the 4e-3 row is reproducible from the tree today.

WORK:
1. Give fvc::ddt_corr a scheme argument so it matches the selected ddt scheme (OpenFOAM has backwardDdtScheme::fvcDdtPhiCorr for exactly this).
2. Add a temporal order-of-accuracy test (manufactured solution or Taylor-Green) that measures observed order and asserts ~2 for Backward and ~1 for Euler. The workspace V&V rule requires the measured result to be recorded in the test's doc comment.
3. Re-run the dt sweep under test so the rows at 8e-3/2e-3/1e-3 stop being doc-only.

title: tampines-steam-tables: HEM subcooled choke takes the wrong branch — Marviken test 24 resolves the DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO overlap zone
description:
get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_subcooled_liquid_ph (crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/choked_flow/stagnation_point_outside_vle_ph_dome_multiphase.rs) returns the bubble-point sonic-kink flux rho_f*c_2phi whenever the two-phase quality at the energy-balance maximum is < 0.03 and the v_b/c_2phi ratio has not exceeded DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO = 5.0. The file's own comment block flags this as the 'overlap zone' and says no local discriminator separates it, for want of experimental data.

Marviken test 24 is that experimental data, and it lands squarely in the overlap zone. Measured 2026-08-11 (crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/tests/marviken_tests.rs, bead op-21g.16):

- dispatcher vs Marviken test 24 (33 K subcooling, 40 points, NUREG/CR-2671 Fig 8:24): mean deviation -48.5 %, worst -70.2 %, 31 of 40 points outside the justified +/-25 % experimental band. The returned flux is nearly pressure-independent (16.85-16.95 Mg/m2 s) while the measurement rises 16.7 -> 56.6 Mg/m2 s.
- the BARE HEM maximum-mass-flux criterion (max over p of rho(p,s0)*sqrt(2(h0-h(p,s0))), built from the crate's public (p,s) flashes with no branch heuristics) on the identical case: mean deviation 9.0 %, signed bias -1.8 %, i.e. inside the band and essentially unbiased.
- same comparison on Marviken test 23 (3 K subcooling): dispatcher 12.6 %, bare criterion 10.1 %.

So the deficit is branch selection, not HEM physics. This is the SECOND time an apparent HEM limitation in this crate turned out to be a choke-finder branch problem (the first was the near-bubble-point artifact fixed in v0.2.1 — and that fix is what introduces this one).

Deliberately NOT fixed inside op-21g.16: retuning DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO against the very dataset used to validate would be fitting the model to its own validation case, and the current threshold is what protects the Zaloudek near-saturation curves (v_b/c_2phi <= 3.30 across all of them).

Work: find a discriminator that routes deeply-subcooled-but-below-5.0 states to the energy-balance maximum without disturbing any Zaloudek curve. Marviken 23/24 and the Moody deep-subcooled points now provide the constraint from the Bernoulli side; Zaloudek constrains the sonic side. Any change must keep all Zaloudek in-dome/subcooled/superheated tests green AND move marviken_tests::validate_against_marviken_test_24 from its characterisation envelope to the +/-25 % validation band — that test's assertions are written so it FAILS loudly if the deficit changes, and its doc comment plus the crate README/CLAUDE.md must be rewritten from 'characterisation' to 'validation' in the same change.

notes.content:
CORRECTION TO COMMIT e11989a7's MESSAGE, recorded 2026-08-11.

That commit says 'test 24 bare-HEM: mean|dev| = 9.0%' and frames it as 'HEM tracks the full-scale Marviken data to about 9% on average'. **That framing is misleading and this note is the correction of record**, since the commit is already pushed and cannot be cleanly amended.

THE ACTUAL RESULT, from the fleet's final report:
- Test 23 (3 K subcooling): VALIDATED. Mean |dev| 12.6%, inside a measured +/-25%-per-point digitisation budget.
- Test 24 (33 K subcooling): **NOT validated through the production dispatcher — a -48.5% SYSTEMATIC deficit.**
- The 9.0% (test 24) and 10.1% (test 23) figures are from the **bare HEM maximum-flux criterion**, NOT the production path.

So the commit quoted a bare-criterion number as if it characterised the model's production behaviour, and omitted that the dispatcher is nearly 50% low on test 24.

WHY THAT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS GOOD NEWS: the gap between the bare criterion (9.0%) and the dispatcher (-48.5%) is the evidence that this is a SOLVER BRANCH-SELECTION DEFECT, not a limitation of HEM physics. HEM itself reproduces test 24 to 9%; the dispatcher is picking the wrong branch. That is this bead, it is P1, and it is fixable — unlike a physics limitation, which would not be.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CROSS-FIDELITY COMPARISON: the sibling fleet building drift-flux and two-fluid Marviken cases was released against a stated HEM reference. They must compare against the BARE-CRITERION numbers (9.0% / 10.1%) as the honest HEM baseline, NOT the dispatcher's -48.5%, which reflects this defect rather than the equilibrium assumption. Comparing a higher-fidelity model against a broken branch selection would flatter it for the wrong reason.

Also corrected in the same report: test 23's subcooling is 3 K, not 33 K, against NUREG/CR-2671.

Diagnostic probe written 2026-08-11 and DELIBERATELY REVERTED, not committed — it was marked "TEMPORARY DIAGNOSTIC PROBE — REMOVE BEFORE COMMIT" in the source and was still in the working tree when the session died at ~12:52. Recording it here so the next person can re-create it in one paste instead of re-deriving it.

Location: get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_subcooled_liquid_ph, in
crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/choked_flow/stagnation_point_outside_vle_ph_dome_multiphase.rs,
inserted immediately after `subcooling_ratio` is computed and before the `if subcooling_ratio > DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO` branch. It required hoisting `let x_at_energy = two_phase_quality(p_energy, s0);` above that branch (it currently lives below it).

What it printed, one eprintln! per call, prefixed PROBE:
  branch       — which of the three arms is taken: "deep_escape" (subcooling_ratio > DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO), "sonic_kink" (x_at_energy < 0.03), or "energy"
  p0_MPa, h0_kJkg, T0_K   — the stagnation state
  dTsub_K      — sat_temp_4(p0) - T0, i.e. actual stagnation subcooling (NaN above p_crit)
  subratio     — the subcooling_ratio the deep-escape test uses
  x_at_energy  — the quality at the energy-maximum choke, i.e. the sonic-kink discriminator
  p_bub_MPa, p_energy_MPa, pe_over_pb   — the two candidate choke pressures and their ratio
  g_energy, g_sonic, ratio_ge_gs        — the two candidate mass fluxes and their ratio
  interior     — g_two_phase >= g_bubble, i.e. whether the energy max is a genuine interior stationary point or just the bubble endpoint
  g_two_phase, g_bubble

Purpose: the bead's thesis is that the Marviken test-24 points land in the "overlap zone" where subcooling_ratio never reaches DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO = 5.0 while x_at_energy < 0.03, so the solver takes the bubble-point sonic-kink branch (rho_f * c_2phi) when it should not. The probe is what turns that from an inference into per-point evidence: run the Marviken gate with it in place and read the branch / subratio / x_at_energy columns for the 40 test-24 points.

Reminder from the sibling bead op-21g.16: do NOT retune DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO or the 0.03 quality threshold against the Marviken data — that is fitting the model to its own validation set. The discriminator needs an independent basis.

title: fhr_sim_v2 reactor power oscillates after Nordheim-Fuchs kinetics swap (no delayed-neutron damping)
description:
User reports (2026-07-14): after replacing fhr_sim_v2's six-group SixGroupPRKE kinetics with teh-o-prke's Nordheim-Fuchs exact timestepper (op-dt3.7 / prke_backend/mod.rs), the reactor power oscillates a lot during operation. The old PRKE-based fhr_sim_v2 did not oscillate.

Likely root cause (physics, not a code bug): Nordheim-Fuchs is a PROMPT-only excursion model -- it neglects delayed-neutron precursor dynamics entirely (documented limitation in its module doc and the user-supplied design scaffold: 'Delayed-neutron-driven operational transients should remain in the PRKE subsystem'). The old six-group PRKE carried six delayed-neutron precursor groups whose decay constants act as a low-pass filter / inertia that damps the reactivity-power-temperature feedback loop. Nordheim-Fuchs has none of that damping, so the fuel-temperature feedback loop (alpha_f*(T-T_ref) -> power -> pebble-bed heating -> T) rings.

Contributing coupling detail in the fhr_sim_v2 wiring: each 1ms step, prke_backend overwrites nordheim_fuchs.fuel_temperature with the pebble-bed TH model's temperature (the authoritative, heat-removal-aware value), then steps NF. NF also advances T internally via its own adiabatic C_f dT/dt = P. The two temperature models can disagree step-to-step, feeding the oscillation.

Candidate fixes (not yet chosen -- discuss with user):
(a) Add the 'Delayed Neutron Layer' from the outram-park-dt-plan architecture (a precursor transfer-function bank, e.g. via chem-eng transfer functions) between the prompt-excursion layer and the TH layer, restoring delayed-neutron damping.
(b) Use Nordheim-Fuchs only for prompt-critical excursion DEMOS (its intended purpose) and keep six-group PRKE for quasi-steady operation in fhr_sim_v2 -- i.e. the NF swap may be the wrong model for this always-on operational sim.
(c) Relax/filter the pebble-bed->NF fuel-temperature hand-off and/or the reactivity feedback to damp the loop numerically (a band-aid, not physical).

Regression reference: git 86ccb04 (the NF swap) + 540fd45; the pre-swap PRKE version is the parent commit of 86ccb04's prke_backend.

notes.content: FIXED 2026-07-15 via option (a): added teh_o_prke::delayed_neutron_layer::DelayedNeutronLayer (5 first-order TransferFnFirstOrder lags) and wired it into fhr_sim_v2 prke_backend as a Lie-split point-kinetics update: NF advances the prompt part, the layer supplies the delayed source S=sum lambda_i C_i, total P = P_prompt + S*dt fed back to NF and to TH. Reconciled fuel-temp handoff: pebble bed is sole authoritative T owner; NF C_f aligned to pebble-bed heat capacity (8000kg*340). Headless regression (isolated kinetics+pebble-bed loop, dt=5ms, 80s, coolant fixed): prompt-only tail peak-to-peak = 194.2 MW on 31.8 MW mean (rings); with delayed layer = 0.0086 MW on 35.8 MW mean (22543x damping, settles). Regression tests added in both fhr_sim_v2 copies (engine canonical + tampines mirror): oscillation_regression::{delayed_neutron_layer_damps_power_oscillation, shipped_prke_timestep_settles}. Both fhr_sim_v2 copies build --release. beta_i/lambda_i from teh-o-prke six_group_constants U-235, reduced 6->5 groups (merged two fastest).

title: tampines components: physical size/volume representation for visualization
description:
Umbrella for giving tampines::components real physical dimensions.

FINDING (2026-08-03, while designing the digital-twin widget library): only Pipe carries real geometry (diameter, length, inclination, roughness -- crates/tampines/src/components/pipe.rs:37-43). HeatExchanger (heat_exchanger.rs:20) and SteamGenerator (via heat_exchanger.area) carry a heat-TRANSFER Area only, which is not an envelope -- a compact plate HX and a large shell-and-tube can share an area. Pump, Turbine, Valve, Condenser and CoolingTower carry no dimensional data at all.

WHY THIS BLOCKS THE WIDGET LIBRARY: outram-park-digital-twin-engine renders 'visual process objects whose rendering derives directly from physics state'. Its crate CLAUDE.md forbids new physics in the engine, so any dimension a widget needs must be added HERE, in tampines.

THE TRAP TO AVOID: HemSteamCv::get_volume() is reachable from Turbine (turbine.inlet) and SteamGenerator (secondary_side), but it is the THERMODYNAMIC control volume -- caller-supplied, unvalidated, used only to convert intensive to extensive properties (get_mass() = volume / specific_volume). The codebase convention is a 1 m3 dummy (TampinesSteamTableCV::get_ref_vol() returns exactly 1.0 m3) and Turbine::new never sets or scales it. Sizing a widget on it would draw every turbine identically at 1 m3. It represents the fluid parcel, not the machine casing. Do NOT use it for visual size.

Each child bead adds an honest envelope/size to one component. Prefer explicit named dimensions (casing length/diameter, shell height, footprint) over a bare Volume where the shape matters to the drawing; a single nominal Volume is acceptable where a rough size correlation is all that is wanted.

title: tampines: TampinesSteamArray (HEM) as the baseline two-phase solver, and the turbine built on it
description:
Maintainer's architecture direction, 2026-08-04:

  'tampines will be an improvement of the turbine from tampines-steam-tables.
   The turbine from tampines-steam-tables should be based on TampinesSteamArray
   (HEM code) which will be the baseline that other solvers will be built on.'

TampinesSteamArray lives at crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:705 -- the homogeneous-equilibrium (HEM) array. It becomes the BASELINE that higher-fidelity solvers are measured against and built on (see the sibling bead for drift-flux / 6-eqn).

Turbine consequence: the turbine model in tampines-steam-tables today is ThreePhaseElectricGeneratorTurbine (steam_turbine_equations/generator.rs) -- a real, working lumped torque balance giving omega, EMF, current and power, but purely electromechanical: it has no steam path. tampines' turbine should improve on it by coupling that rotor to a TampinesSteamArray steam path rather than taking torque as a free input.

Note tampines::components::Turbine (components/turbine.rs:13) is currently inert -- inlet: HemSteamCv + adiabatic_efficiency: Ratio, and expand_to() returns NotYetImplemented. That is the shell this work fills in.

Remember the workspace convention (memory: arrays use (p,h) flash): TampinesSteamArray/OPCPFluidArray default to (p,h) flashing because it carries phase data; (T,p) single-phase flashes panic on two-phase.

title: tampines: adopt OutramFoam drift-flux and two-fluid (6-eqn) models above the HEM baseline
description:
Maintainer's architecture direction, 2026-08-04: 'OutramFoam driftflux and 6 eqn models have already been ported in. These are to be introduced into Tampines.'

Already ported and available in crates/outram-foam-multiphase/src/:
  drift_flux.rs        -- drift-flux model
  two_fluid.rs         -- two-fluid (6-equation) model
  two_fluid_pimple.rs  -- its PIMPLE loop
  pimple.rs, wall_boiling.rs, chf.rs, dryout.rs

Task: introduce these into tampines as higher-fidelity options ABOVE the HEM baseline (see the sibling TampinesSteamArray bead), so a component can be run at HEM, drift-flux, or full two-fluid fidelity.

Design constraint (workspace rule): the fidelity choice is a CLOSED set, so it is enum dispatch -- never Box<dyn>/trait objects. A trait may still be used as a compile-time contract on each concrete model.

Cross-reference: the existing op-dt3.12/.13/.14/.15/.16 beads already track reduced 1D drift-flux / two-fluid / CHF / dryout / post-dryout for tampines -- check for overlap and either wire dependencies or close the duplicates rather than doing the work twice.

Note outram-foam-multiphase is a scaffold with no human V&V; anything adopted here needs V&V documenting methodology AND measured results per the workspace rule.

notes.content:
SEQUENCING (maintainer, 2026-08-04): 'the 1D versions of drift flux and 6 eqn are to be the bread and butter of tampines before the AI is in... Before PINNs and other AI accelerations of the solver are in.'

So the 1D REDUCED models are the primary deliverable, not the full 3D CFD ports. Those already have beads: op-dt3.12 (1D Drift Flux), op-dt3.13 (1D Two-Fluid), op-dt3.14 (1D CHF), op-dt3.15 (1D Dryout), op-dt3.16 (1D Post-Dryout). This bead is the umbrella that says where the physics comes FROM (outram-foam-multiphase) and that it sits above the HEM baseline (op-dt3.18).

Order: HEM baseline (op-dt3.18) -> 1D drift-flux + 1D 6-eqn (op-dt3.12/.13) as the workhorse solvers -> only THEN PINNs / AI acceleration. The 'AI' in the TAMPINES acronym is explicitly a LATER stage; the deterministic 1D solvers must be the trustworthy baseline it is measured against first.

title: tampines Turbine: implement expand_to() — IF97 (p,s) isentropic flash + Baumann wetness correction
description:
crates/tampines/src/components/turbine.rs:38 — expand_to() returns NotYetImplemented. It needs: isentropic outlet enthalpy via a real (p,s) flash on HemSteamCv (= TampinesSteamTableCV), then the efficiency correction, giving outlet state and shaft work W = mdot * eta_ad * (h1 - h2s).

Constant adiabatic_efficiency is not adequate at the LP end, which runs wet: apply a Baumann wetness correction (roughly 1 percent efficiency lost per 1 percent mean wetness) rather than a fixed Ratio.

Note the workspace convention: arrays default to (p,h) flashing because it carries phase data; a (T,p) single-phase flash panics on two-phase. The isentropic leg here is (p,s), which must land back on a (p,h) state.

Underlying isentropic/Schultz algebra already exists in outram_park_fork_dwsim_libs::expander::isentropic.

Scope context: crates/tampines-steam-tables/docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md section 1 and 3.1.
acceptance_criteria: expand_to() returns a physically valid HemSteamCv outlet plus shaft power for both superheated and wet inlet states; wetness correction applied and documented; no NotYetImplemented remains.

title: tampines Turbine: Stodola cone (ellipse) law for off-design mass flow vs pressure
description:
Efficiency alone pins the WORK but not the MASS FLOW. A digital twin that only holds a design point cannot do sliding-pressure operation, part load, or valve throttling. The missing constitutive law is Stodola's cone (ellipse) law, relating mass flow to inlet and outlet pressure and inlet temperature.

Reference implementation available: ClaRa's 'Steam Turbine L1' (ClaRaLibrary/ClaRa, xrg-simulation/ClaRa-official) is mass + energy conservation with Stodola's law and an isentropic efficiency — structurally the same design as the HemSteamCv-with-sink-terms direction in op-dt3.18. ClaRa official is 3-clause BSD, so GPLv3-compatible one-way and portable WITH its attribution header preserved.

DO NOT port from ThermoPower (casella/ThermoPower): Modelica License 2, not clearly GPL-compatible, does not cleanly permit forking. Read for ideas only.

Maintainer direction 2026-08-04: this lands as a MODULE under tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/ (alongside converging_diverging_nozzles/ and generator.rs), NOT a new crate.

tampines Turbine: couple the shaft-work sink to rotor inertia and the generator
description:
The turbine's energy sink term must be SHAFT WORK, not a prescribed heat sink, and it must feed the rotor inertia ODE J domega/dt = T_turb - T_gen. Without that coupling the twin cannot do load rejection or overspeed, which is the transient a turbine twin exists for.

ThreePhaseElectricGeneratorTurbine (tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/generator.rs) is a working lumped electromechanical rotor — torque balance, omega, EMF, current, power — but it takes torque as a FREE INPUT and has no steam path. This bead closes that loop: steam expansion supplies the torque.

Two design constraints from the 2026-08-04 review:
- Do NOT give the turbine CV real blade-path fluid inventory. Steam residence time is milliseconds; a CV with true blade volume adds a stiff acoustic mode that shrinks the timestep for no physics. Model the turbine as a quasi-steady junction (flow law + work extraction) between volumes, with storage in the steam chest and adjacent pipes. If the CV has volume, it represents the chest/casing.
- Casing heat loss is a genuine SECOND sink but is small (order 0.5-1 percent) — optional.

title: Nordheim-Fuchs exact timestepper -- prompt excursion + adiabatic fuel feedback
description:
Analytical (closed-form) integrator for prompt reactivity excursions with
adiabatic fuel-temperature feedback. Scaffolded from a design doc the user
supplied 2026-07-14 (Copilot-generated, pasted in chat). Purpose is NOT
reactor safety/licensing analysis -- it is an educational/visualization
model that removes prompt-lifetime stiffness (dt << Lambda) from real-time
sims, enabling interactive HTGR/fast-reactor demos on low-power devices
(Android tablets). Positioned as the "Prompt Excursion Layer" beneath the
existing delayed-neutron PRKE precursor-bank subsystem, which stays
untouched for delayed-neutron-dominated transients.

Physical model / assumptions:
- prompt neutrons only, delayed-precursor dynamics neglected
- lumped adiabatic fuel heat capacity C_f, uniform fuel temperature T_f
- fuel-temperature feedback only: rho_f = alpha_f * (T_f - T_f_ref)
- external reactivity rho_ext held constant over a timestep
- requires alpha_f < 0 (negative feedback) for a stable closed-form
  solution -- positive-feedback excursions are intentionally out of scope

Governing equations:
  dP/dt      = P * (rho_ext + alpha_f*(T_f - T_f_ref) - beta) / Lambda
  C_f dT_f/dt = P
where P = reactor power, T_f = lumped fuel temp, C_f = fuel heat capacity,
Lambda = prompt neutron generation time, beta = delayed neutron fraction,
rho_ext = externally imposed reactivity, alpha_f = fuel feedback coeff.

Reactivity-margin substitution r = rho_ext - beta + alpha_f*(T_f - T_f_ref)
collapses this to a Riccati-type ODE:
  dr/dt = (r^2 - gamma^2) / (2*Lambda)
  gamma^2 = r_k^2 + 2*Lambda*|alpha_f|*P_k/C_f   (real-valued since alpha_f<0)

Exact per-step update (closed form, no numerical ODE integration needed):
  r_{k+1}   = -gamma * tanh( gamma*dt/(2*Lambda) + atanh(-r_k/gamma) )
  T_f,{k+1} = T_f_ref + (r_{k+1} - rho_ext + beta) / alpha_f
  P_{k+1}   = C_f/(2*Lambda*|alpha_f|) * (gamma^2 - r_{k+1}^2)

This removes the dt << Lambda stability restriction a standard ODE stepper
would need, so timestep can be chosen for UI frame rate / TH-coupling
cadence / mobile performance instead of prompt-lifetime stiffness.

Explicitly OUT of scope for this model: delayed-neutron dynamics (stays in
the existing PRKE precursor-bank subsystem), licensing/safety-grade
calculations, reactor protection analysis, spatial kinetics, fuel-melt /
severe-accident modelling. It represents only the prompt self-limiting
mechanism via adiabatic fuel heating.

Deliverable here: the timestepper itself (struct + step function) living in
teh-o-prke, uom-typed per this crate's conventions, with a doc comment
carrying the methodology above (physical quantity / valid range / units,
per the root CLAUDE.md human-interface-layer rule -- alpha_f < 0 should be
a documented precondition, not silently assumed). Add a verification test
against a known Nordheim-Fuchs benchmark case once implemented (per this
workspace's V&V documentation rule: methodology + actual measured results
in the test's doc comment). nee_soon's consumption of this as its "Prompt
Excursion Layer" interface is a separate, dependent bead.

Bridges the prompt-only Nordheim-Fuchs layer to the TH layer, restoring delayed-neutron inertia/damping. Fixes op-dt3.11 when wired into fhr_sim_v2's prke_backend.

title: TransferFnFirstOrder response_vec growth in real-time loops (DelayedNeutronLayer / NF reactivity driver)
description: TransferFnFirstOrder (chem-eng) accumulates one FirstOrderResponse per input change and only clears after 20*tau. In DelayedNeutronLayer the slowest group (tau~80s) means the vector can grow to ~1.6M entries (20*80s at 1ms) before clearing in the always-on fhr_sim_v2 GUI loop, with O(n) per-step summation -> memory + slowdown over long real-time runs. Not a correctness issue (superposition is exact) and fine for the bounded headless regression tests (~seconds). Options: (a) add an exponential-integrator fast path to TransferFnFirstOrder / FirstOrderStableTransferFnNoZeroes that keeps O(1) state, or (b) periodic rebase of the lag to its current offset. Same concern applies to nordheim_fuchs's reactivity driver when the input changes every step. Surfaced during op-dt3.11.

title: NF reactivity driver: same TransferFnFirstOrder response_vec growth in per-step loops
description: Follow-up split from op-e46.4 (DelayedNeutronLayer O(1) fix, done). teh-o-prke nordheim_fuchs::advance_with_reactivity_driver takes a &mut TransferFnFirstOrder and calls set_user_input_and_calc every step; if driven in an always-on real-time loop with a changing commanded reactivity it accumulates one FirstOrderResponse per input change (pruned only after 20*tau), i.e. the same O(n)/step + unbounded-memory growth op-e46.4 fixed in the delayed layer. NOT currently triggered in the shipped fhr_sim_v2 (prke_backend uses nordheim_fuchs.set_external_reactivity(...) directly, no TransferFn), so latent, not live. Options mirror op-e46.4: give the caller an O(1) exponential/implicit-integrator reactivity-lag path instead of a growing TransferFnFirstOrder, or periodically rebase the lag. Reference op-e46.4 / op-dt3.11.

notes.content:
LIKELY RESOLVED BY op-fm5's fix (2026-08-11) -- maintainer to confirm and close.

The mechanism this bead describes no longer exists. As of chem-eng 0.2.0, TransferFnFirstOrder does not accumulate a FirstOrderResponse per input change: both of its constituent blocks (FirstOrderStableTransferFnNoZeroes and FirstOrderStableTransferFnForZeroes) now advance by an exact O(1) zero-order-hold recurrence carrying 2 and 1 state variables respectively, with no Vec and no 20*tau pruning. So nordheim_fuchs::advance_with_reactivity_driver can be driven in an always-on real-time loop at any timestep without the O(n)/step growth or unbounded memory.

Measured: filtered PID at dt=0.001 s with tau_d=80.8 s -- exactly the PRKE shape this bead worried about -- went from 2329.52 us/step and still rising at step 79,000, to a flat 0.17 us/step. Guarded by block_state_size_does_not_grow_with_step_index and pid_step_cost_does_not_grow_with_step_index in chem-eng.

No change was needed in teh-o-prke itself. Neither of the two remedies this bead proposed (an O(1) reactivity-lag path, or periodic rebasing) is required any more.

title: Steam generator widgets: bubble generation needs to be physically fussy
description:
Maintainer wants the boiling detail in the steam-generator widgets done carefully -- bubbles are the thing that gives away a boiling surface, and getting them wrong makes an otherwise good drawing read as decoration.

CURRENT STATE (b42df8f, crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/steam_generator.rs):
  - Horizontal U-tube (VVER): bubbles rise off the tube bundle.
  - Vertical U-tube (PWR): entrained droplets drawn in the steam space above the water level.
  - Helical coil: once-through, no level and no bubbles -- correct, leave alone.

Both are deterministic scatters seeded from a hash, which must stay true (the widget is rebuilt every repaint; a real RNG makes them shimmer).

WHAT 'FUSSY' SHOULD MEAN -- candidate list, to be refined by the maintainer:
  - Bubbles should NUCLEATE AT THE HEATED SURFACE, i.e. originate on the tubes, not appear uniformly in the water volume.
  - Bubble size should GROW as they rise -- coalescence plus falling static head. A uniform bubble size is the tell.
  - Void fraction should INCREASE UP THE BUNDLE in a recirculating SG, so the population should be denser and larger near the top of the heated length.
  - Density should scale with DUTY, so the bubble field responds to the power/temperature sliders rather than being static decoration.
  - Nothing below the level should be a droplet and nothing above it a bubble -- the two populations must not cross the free surface.
  - Rise should be plausible: roughly vertical, slight wobble, faster for larger bubbles.

NOT YET SPECIFIED: the maintainer has not said which of these bothers them most. Ask before doing all of it -- some are cheap and some (a real void profile) are not.

CONSTRAINT: this is offline demonstration ARTWORK, not a two-phase model. outram-foam-multiphase has real void/CHF/wall-boiling closures but they are not wired to anything and must not be dragged in for a drawing. Keep it a display heuristic and keep saying so in the docs.
