description:
Source: docs/melcor-parity-scoping.md (written 2026-08-07; banner-marked UNTRUSTED AI-ASSISTED DRAFT, human review pending).

Build a clean-room, lumped-parameter severe-accident capability from the PUBLIC MELCOR manuals (SAND2017-0876 / ML17040A420 and companions) plus legitimately-licensed component codes -- CFAST (NIST, public domain) for the executive and volume/vent architecture, AeroSolved/PartMC (GPL) for aerosols, FLEXPART (GPL-3.0) for dispersion.

WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT FROM EVERY OTHER PORT HERE: there is no open upstream. MELCOR, ASTEC and MAAP are all closed, and MELCOR specifically is distributed under a signed NDA that binds PEOPLE, not just artefacts. So this must be a clean-room reimplementation from public documents, assembled at COMPONENT level.

TARGET FOR THIS EPIC = "MELCOR-lite": a physically meaningful containment pressure, temperature and hydrogen history for a station-blackout-class LWR transient, with NO source term (no aerosols, no FP transport, no MCCI). Centres on a new NON-MESH lumped-parameter crate; touches outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs (flash kernel), tampines-steam-tables + outram-park-fork-coolprop (EOS), tuas_boussinesq_solver (conduction/convection), teh-o-prke (decay heat), outram-park-fork-offbeat (Zr oxidation), kovan-literature (manual ingest).

DONE = a runnable transient producing a citable containment P/T/H2 history, restartable, with plot-file output, and V&V documented (methodology AND measured results per the workspace rule) against public benchmarks -- QUENCH for oxidation, THAI HD/HM for hydrogen distribution, ISP-42/PANDA for containment mixing.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: intended use is education/research/V&V only -- never licensing, never PSA of a real facility, never emergency response. No MELCOR/ASTEC/MAAP/RELAP5/BISON/Griffin/SAM source may be touched or paraphrased by anyone, INCLUDING FROM MEMORY UNDER NDA. Every model must cite the public document it was written from, with ADAMS/SAND identifier, in its doc comment.

SCOPE ESTIMATES (self-labelled judgement in the source doc, +/- half their own value): MELCOR-lite ~70-105 kLOC; full parity ~200-320 kLOC. The COR full phase is explicitly marked as having NO honest schedule estimate.

DELIBERATELY NOT FILED as children of this epic, per the doc's own flags:
- MCCI / CAV: recommended DEFERRED. Blocked on closed CALPHAD databases (TAF-ID is signatory-only, NUCLEA restricted). The doc says explicitly: do not plan around acquiring them. title: tampines-steam-tables: region router accepts p = 0 Pa and the B23 line contradicts its own doc
description:
Two smaller sharp edges found 2026-08-11 in the full range-literal audit of region_fwd_eqn_single_phase done for op-cv1c. Neither is the op-cv1c defect and neither was changed by its fix (behaviour-only scope), but both are real.

1. p = 0 Pa is ACCEPTED, not rejected. The Region-2 arm's disjuncts use (0.0..=p_sat_reg4_pascal) and (0.0..=p_boundary_23_pascal) and (0.0..=100e6) — all START-INCLUSIVE at zero. IF97 is defined for p > 0 (the ideal-gas part of the Region-2 Gibbs function contains ln(pi), which diverges at p = 0), so a p = 0 call returns a non-finite value rather than panicking or erroring. The bounds-checked facade interfaces::checked already rejects p <= 0, so this only bites callers of the raw functions.
   Suggested fix: exclusive lower edges in the Region-2 arms, so p = 0 hits the router panic like any other out-of-envelope input. Behaviour change, needs its own test.

2. Doc/code contradiction on the B23 line. The doc comment on p_boundary_2_3 (region_3_.../aux_eqn_boundary_region_2_and_region_3.rs:4) says 'note that points ON this line belong to region 2'. But the router's Region-3 arm is (p_boundary_23_pascal..=100e6), start-INCLUSIVE, and it is matched BEFORE the Region-2 arm — so for T in [623.15 K, 863.15 K) a point at exactly p = p_B23(T) routes to Region 3, not Region 2. (This start-inclusivity predates op-cv1c, which only closed the upper edge.) The measured practical effect is small — at (623.15 K, 100 MPa) the two region equations differ by 3.245e-6 in h and 1.769e-5 in v — but one of the two statements is wrong and should be settled against the IF97 release, then the loser corrected.

3. Minor contract mismatch, same audit: ps_flash_eqm/validity_range.rs::is_outside_pressure_range PANICS on an out-of-range pressure while its ph_flash_eqm twin RETURNS true. Both are named as predicates and both are called as 'if is_outside_pressure_range(p) { panic!(...) }', so the ps version can never return true and its caller's panic is dead code with a worse message.

title: HTR-10 rung 2->3 seam: bridge MGXS into GeN-Foam nuclearData (RBF-parameterised over states)
description:
Parent: op-841p. THE RUNG 2 TO RUNG 3 INTERFACE. Wire to op-p6p.4 (genfoam neutronics/XS nuclearData structures, In Progress); do not invent a parallel format.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED IN THE CODE 2026-08-11 (crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/genfoam/):
- The whole genfoam subtree is 32,334 lines with 262 tests and NOT ONE todo!().
- neutronics/xs/ (2167 lines, 13 tests): CrossSectionData at xs/mod.rs:134, NuclearDataOneEnergy at xs/nuclear_data_one_energy.rs:63.
- GroupConstants at xs/group_constants.rs:59 IS THE LANDING STRUCT and is already uom-typed: diffusion_coefficient (m), nu_sigma_f (1/m), sigma_pow (J/m), sigma_removal (1/m), chi_prompt, chi_delayed, inverse_velocity (s/m), disc_factor. PrecursorConstants at :85 carries beta, beta_tot, lambda.

THE HARD PART, AND WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD: GeN-Foam's nuclearData is NOT an njoy/OpenMC MGXS library. It is a dict PARAMETERISED BY FEEDBACK VARIABLES via polyharmonic-spline RBF interpolation across perturbed reactor states. So the bridge is not a format conversion - it is 'run rung 1 at N perturbed states (fuel temperature, moderator temperature, density) and fit the interpolant'. Design the perturbation matrix explicitly and record it in the run manifest.

HOMOGENISATION IS THE OTHER HALF, AND IT IS EXPENSIVE TO GET WRONG. Wang et al. (2014), Ann. Nucl. Energy 64, 1-7 (PROPRIETARY tier - cite, do not re-host) measured, against continuous-energy MCNP5 on the detailed HTR-10 model: INFHOMMEDIUM +2820 +/- 19 pcm, LATTICECELL +681 +/- 24, MULTIREGION +661 +/- 21, LATTICECELL(CELLMIX) +653 +/- 21, MULTIREGION(CELLMIX) +470 +/- 22, DOUBLEHET +276 +/- 20. Worst is 10.2x the best. A homogenised pebble-bed model cannot reach the ~200 pcm accuracy this benchmark needs - which is exactly why the rung 2->3 homogenisation must be MEASURED against rung 1, not assumed. Captured as typed data in outram_park_digital_twin_engine::htr10::neutronics::wang_2014_unit_cell_bias.

description:
MEASURED 2026-08-07 (this was previously an unverified grep-level claim; it has now been benchmarked). Release build, AMD Ryzen 5 5600, rustc 1.97.0, std::time::Instant, 200-step windows per checkpoint, two 5,000-step warm-ups discarded. The temporary benchmark was deleted afterwards and the tree left byte-identical.

MECHANISM (confirmed):
crates/chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator/src/lib/beta_testing/stable_transfer_functions/first_order_transfer_fn.rs -- and a byte-identical twin under alpha_nightly/, which is the tier TUAS actually imports:
  :16      pub(crate) response_vec: Vec<FirstOrderResponse>,
  :113     self.response_vec.push(new_response);   -- one entry per input change; a real PID error signal changes every step (the guard at :89-92 only compares to 9 dp)
  :134-138 re-sums the ENTIRE vector every step via .iter_mut().map(|r| r.calculate_response(current_time)).sum()
  :147-230 clear_first_order_response_vector prunes via repeated .position() + .remove(index), itself O(n) per removal.

CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM -- growth is NOT unbounded in general. FirstOrderResponse::is_steady_state (:291-301) retires an entry once time_elapsed/process_time > 20.0, so the vector saturates at N = 20*tau/dt entries. Cost is linear in step index up to that horizon, then FLAT. It is unbounded only when the run never reaches 20*tau -- which is exactly what happened to teh-o-prke (tau1 ~ 80.8 s at 1 ms -> 1.6 M entries).

MEASURED per-step cost:
  A: TUAS's shipped PID, dt=0.04 s -- 5.33 us @100 -> 27.90 @1k -> 28.61 @10k -> 28.07 @39k   (total 1.13 s / 40k steps)
  B: PID, dt=0.1 s               -- 5.36 -> 11.34 -> 11.45 -> 11.46                            (0.46 s / 40k)
  C: PID, dt=0.001 s             -- 52.4 us @1k -> 259.3 @5k -> 528.3 @10k -> 1084.6 @20k -> 1131.3 @40k -> 1133.3 @79k  (79.5 s / 80k)
  D: bare ProportionalController -- 1.83 @100 -> 9.30 @1k -> 9.34 @39k                          (0.37 s / 40k)
  E: PID tau=1000 s, dt=0.04 s   -- 5.34 @100 -> 35.96 @1k -> 105.57 @5k -> 367.04 @20k -> 692.35 @39k, never plateaus (15.7 s / 40k)

O() CONCLUSION: per-step cost is O(min(n, 20*tau/dt)) -- linear in step index during the ramp, then a flat plateau. Case C is decisive: growth is exactly linear (5k->10k = 2.04x, 10k->20k = 2.05x against 2.00x step ratios) then goes flat at step 20,000 = exactly 20 s / 0.001 s, the retirement horizon. Case E, whose horizon (500,000 steps) is never reached, grows linearly for the whole run and never plateaus. So: O(n^2) total while ramping, O(n * 20*tau/dt) once saturated.
Cost per response term is constant at 9.3 / 9.5 / 9.3 / 9.4 ns/term for A/B/D/C -- which nails the mechanism quantitatively.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS EVEN THOUGH IT SATURATES: TUAS's SHIPPED config sits at a permanent flat 28 us/step for ONE PID, and it runs two PIDs plus a P block -- ~66 us/step of pure controller overhead, forever, for arithmetic that needs ~1 ns. Halving the timestep doubles it.

TWO AGGRAVATING FINDINGS:
- first_order_transfer_fn_with_zeroes.rs:27,29 carries TWO such vectors, so every first-order-with-zero block costs 2N terms.
- proportional_controller/mod.rs:29-44 implements a PURE GAIN G(s) = K_c as (K_c*s + K_c)/(s + 1) through the same machinery, so a P controller does O(20/dt) work per step. Its own doc at :58 says "probably overdoing it in terms of computation cost but that's not an issue ... yet".

TUAS PID PATH CONFIRMED (library code, not #[cfg(test)]):
crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/pre_built_components/ciet_three_branch_plus_dracs/ciet_educational_simulator_loop_prototypes/version_3/mod.rs:508-512 AnalogController::new_filtered_pid_controller(1.75, 1.75 s, 1.0 s, 1.0); second CTAH controller :521-525; ProportionalController delay block :533-536; timestep 0.04 s (:108). Also version_2.rs:482,495 and ~20 further sites in DRACS regression/validation tests, plus coupled_dracs_loop_tests/isolated_dracs_loop_resistance_calibration/mod.rs:331.

REMEDY -- copy what teh-o-prke already did. Commit 46194ba6 (2026-07-15, bead op-e46.4), single file, +229/-80: deleted the five TransferFnFirstOrder lags and replaced them with a fixed-size 5-element state array advanced by a closed-form backward-Euler recurrence (delayed_neutron_layer.rs:405-413):
    C_i^{n+1} = (C_i^n + dt*(beta_i/Lambda)*P) / (1 + dt*lambda_i)
No Vec, no history, public API unchanged, guarded by an O(1) regression test precursor_update_is_o1_per_step (:555). The precedent numbers are recorded in-tree and were verified: delayed_neutron_layer.rs:88-89 "measured ~49 us -> ~1.8 ms/step from step 1k to 40k"; :549 "Representative: ~0.7-1.0 ns/step, flat across blocks".

A first-order lag must carry ONE state variable, not a history of every input it has ever seen.

RELATED: op-e46.5 already tracks a latent second instance -- nordheim_fuchs::advance_with_reactivity_driver still takes a &mut TransferFnFirstOrder.

HARDWARE CAVEAT: absolute microsecond figures are specific to this CPU. Machine-independent are (a) the linear relation between per-step cost and step index in the ramp regime, (b) saturation landing exactly at 20*tau/dt steps, (c) cost scaling exactly with live-term count.

notes.content:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11 (awaiting maintainer review; NOT closed by the agent).

APPROACH CHOSEN: option 1, the exact O(1) recurrence. Not time-bucketing. The recurrence reproduces the pre-existing semantics EXACTLY rather than approximating them, so bucketing was not implemented and no grouping error had to be quantified. It is the zero-order-hold / step-invariant discrete equivalent, exact for piecewise-constant input; module docs cite Astrom & Wittenmark, Seborg et al., Franklin/Powell/Workman, Ogata, Hochbruck & Ostermann, Oppenheim & Schafer, and Smith (open access). No editions/years/pages given -- none verified against a physical copy.

SCOPE: all FIVE vector-carrying block types, in BOTH tiers (alpha_nightly and beta_testing), not just the first-order one named in the original report:
  first_order_transfer_fn.rs                (1 vec -> 2 scalars)
  first_order_transfer_fn_with_zeroes.rs    (2 vecs -> 1 scalar)
  second_order_transfer_fn.rs               (1 vec -> 3 scalars, enum per damping regime)
  decaying_sinusoid.rs                      (1 vec -> 2 scalars, decaying rotation)
  decaying_exponentials.rs                  (1 vec -> 3 scalars; alpha_nightly only)
The two tiers are now byte-identical apart from the tier import path; previously they had drifted (beta_testing's decaying_sinusoid had a '>' vs '>=' heaviside that dropped the cosine value at t == start_time; unified on alpha's correct '>=').

MEASURED, same harness before and after (release, AMD Ryzen 5 5600, rustc 1.97.0, 200-step windows, two 5,000-step warm-ups discarded). Baseline reproduces this bead's original figures:
  A PID dt=0.04, 40k:   28.35 us/step plateau -> 0.17 us/step;  1.188 s -> 0.007 s
  B PID dt=0.10, 40k:   13.15 us/step         -> 0.17 us/step;  0.478 s -> 0.007 s

  F PID tau_d=80.8 dt=0.001 (the PRKE shape): 2329.52 us/step still rising -> 0.17 us/step; 127.599 s -> 0.014 s
Per-step cost is now FLAT in the step index in every case, including E and F whose retirement horizons are never reached.

PHYSICS UNCHANGED: the summed output over each of the six runs is identical before and after to the three decimal places printed (e.g. case A sink 17175484.304 both times). The only intended difference is that the old code discarded exp(-20) = 2.06e-9 of each step response when it retired one; the recurrence carries that residual, so the new answer is marginally MORE accurate.

VERIFICATION (methodology + results in each test doc comment): each recurrence checked against the closed-form analytic superposition of the retained response structs, over 2000 steps, tolerance 1e-9. Max abs differences measured 2026-08-11: first order 6.33e-15; with zeroes 1.69e-15; second order 9.05e-15 / 5.11e-15 / 6.94e-15 (zeta = 0.35 / 1.0 / 2.4); decaying sinusoid 4.16e-16 sine, 4.86e-16 cosine; decaying exponential 8.60e-16 overdamped, 6.66e-16 critically damped; irregular time grid 7.99e-15; dead time 6.11e-15. All round-off, not discretisation error.

  block_state_size_does_not_grow_with_step_index -- 100k steps at dt=0.001 with tau=80.8 s; state size identical at step 100 and step 99,999 ([2,1,3,2,3] alpha, [2,1,3,2] beta). Pre-0.2.0 the counts would have been 101 and 100,000.

title: TUAS Wakao fix: the BEFORE baseline was never measured, so calibration masking is unresolved
description:
The Wakao correlation was corrected on 2026-08-11 from the transposed `Nu = 2 + 1.1 Re^0.333 Pr^0.6` to the published `Nu = 2 + 1.1 Pr^(1/3) Re^0.6`. The implementing fleet captured AFTER numbers but stopped with the BEFORE baseline outstanding, so the question the whole task existed to answer is still open.

THE QUESTION. Wakao sits on a CALIBRATED CIET path — ciet_heater_v2, the porous-media components, the heater top/bottom heads. The crate CLAUDE.md records that CIET steady-state natural-circulation and isothermal tests agree with published Zweibaum (2015) and Zou et al. (2019) data to within ~6 percent. If a heat-transfer coefficient was calibrated against experiment WHILE the correlation was wrong, the calibration absorbed the error, and correcting the correlation should have moved that agreement.

So: did agreement change? Nobody measured. Three possibilities and they have very different consequences:
1. Agreement unchanged -> the calibrated path was insensitive to Wakao, or the calibration dominates it. Fine, but worth knowing.
2. Agreement degraded -> the calibration WAS masking the error, and re-calibrating against experiment with correct physics is a separate, larger job needing maintainer sign-off. Do NOT re-tune to hide it and do NOT revert the correlation to keep tests green.
3. The tests never exercise Wakao at all -> a coverage finding, and it would explain how a factor-5.84 error at Re = 1000 survived.

HOW TO GET IT. Run the CIET suite on a worktree at the pre-fix commit and compare against the post-fix numbers. Both runs are expensive: the full TUAS lib suite measured 2959.84 s (49 minutes) on this machine, and per CLAUDE.md it must run in PARALLEL, never with --test-threads=1. A killed run is neither a pass nor a fail.

COMPOUNDING FACTOR, see op-lmye: ciet_heater_v2 feeds a HYDRAULIC-diameter Reynolds number to Wakao, which is defined on PARTICLE diameter. So the calibrated path had TWO errors — a transposed correlation and a wrong length scale. Fixing one without the other may move agreement in a confusing direction, and any baseline comparison must say which fixes were in place for each run.

THIS IS A CLASS, NOT AN INCIDENT. The same audit filed op-ctbq (Pr_bulk/Pr_wall swapped in PipeGnielinskiCalibrated - the same transposition class, still latent), op-tidc (Sieder-Tate bounds inverted), op-i7od (LMTD ambient helper sign/panic), and op-a3yi. A correlation module with this many transposition and inversion defects deserves a systematic pass against the published forms, not one fix at a time.

description: root@vm
title: root@vm
cargo fmt -p is destructive in this workspace: 222 files, +21057/-4495
description:
Found 2026-08-11 by the njoy/outram-mc agent while following the CLAUDE.md bookkeeping-pass routine, which tells agents to run `cargo fmt -p <crate>`.

MEASURED: `cargo fmt -p njoy-outram-park-fork -p outram-mc-libs` rewrote **222 files, +21 057 / -4 495 lines**. None of it was wanted; all of it was reverted and the real edits replayed by hand. The final semantic diff for that task was 4 files, +587/-48.

ROOT CAUSE: the repository is not rustfmt-clean and carries no `rustfmt.toml`, so `cargo fmt` reformats to upstream defaults across every file it touches, not just the ones being edited. The two conditions compound — no pinned style, and a large body of never-formatted legacy code.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE AGENT: the workspace CLAUDE.md "Bookkeeping pass" section instructs agents to run a formatter as part of a routine that is explicitly designed to be run per-crate by a fleet. Anyone who follows that instruction literally detonates a 20k-line diff into a branch, and if they do not notice, it lands. The instruction is currently a trap.

Also relevant: the same day, a `rustfmt --check` on four `tampines-steam-tables` files showed the legacy formatting problem directly — `ps_flash_eqm/validity_range.rs` would be substantially rewritten by rustfmt despite the change under review being three lines.

OPTIONS, maintainer's call:
1. Add a `rustfmt.toml` pinning the current style closely enough that a format pass is a no-op on untouched code, then format the workspace once in a single dedicated commit.
2. Format the workspace once, in its own commit, on a quiet branch, and accept the one-time churn — after which `cargo fmt -p` becomes safe and the CLAUDE.md instruction becomes true.
3. Amend CLAUDE.md to forbid `cargo fmt` and require `rustfmt` on individually named changed files only.

Until one of these is done, CLAUDE.md should carry a warning next to the bookkeeping-pass formatter step. Do NOT let an agent format the workspace as a side effect of unrelated work.

outram-blender: weld / remove-doubles (merge coincident vertices within tolerance)
description: Merge vertices closer than a tolerance into one (Blender's Mesh > Merge by Distance / bmo_remove_doubles / weld modifier). Spatial-hash bucketing for O(n); rebuild faces on the merged vertex set; drop faces that collapse to a degenerate (<3 distinct verts) after welding. Hardens boolean output and imported polygon soups before the CSG/polyMesh export bridges. New MeshOp::Weld { tolerance } variant + dispatch. V&V: coincident-duplicated cube welds 16->8 verts back to chi=2; a slit sphere seam welds to watertight; tolerance=0 is a no-op.

title: root@vm
outram-blender: fill holes (cap open boundary loops -> watertight)
description: Detect boundary loops (edges incident to exactly one face) and cap each with a centroid-fan triangulation, making an open surface watertight. Blender analogue: bmo_holes_fill / Fill Holes. Winding of each cap triangle is chosen opposite to the boundary directed edge so it stays consistent with the existing surface (adjacent faces traverse the shared edge in opposite directions). Directly serves the MC CSG bridge, which needs closed geometry. New MeshOp::FillHoles variant + dispatch. Pairs with weld (op-hzs.22): weld stitches near-coincident seams, fill-holes closes true gaps. V&V: cube with one face removed -> chi back to 2, watertight (every edge borders 2 faces); an already-closed mesh is a no-op.

title: root@vm
outram-blender: solidify (shell thickness -> closed solid)
description: Give a surface thickness: offset a copy of every vertex inward along its area-weighted vertex normal by 'thickness', add the inner shell with reversed winding (cavity-facing), and bridge open boundary edges with rim quads. Blender analogue: MOD_solidify (simple mode). Turns a surface patch into a volume (CFD wall meshing) or a closed mesh into a hollow shell. Reuses the boundary directed-edge tracing from fill_holes and consistent-winding rules. New MeshOp::Solidify { thickness } variant. V&V: open grid -> closed slab chi=2, watertight; closed cube -> nested outer+inner shells (hollow box) chi=4, each shell watertight; thickness=0 collapses inner onto outer.

title: root@vm
outram-blender: recalculate normals (make winding consistent + outward)
description: Blender's Recalculate Normals Outside (mesh.normals_make_consistent). BFS over face adjacency (shared undirected edges): flip any neighbour that traverses a shared edge in the SAME direction as its already-oriented neighbour, making each connected component consistently wound; then per component compute signed volume and flip the whole component if negative so normals point outward. Unlike boolean_general::orient_outward (which only whole-mesh-flips an ALREADY-consistent mesh by volume sign), this repairs an inconsistently-wound polygon soup -- foundational for boolean, the CSG inside-test, and solidify. New MeshOp::RecalculateNormals. V&V: a cube with a subset of faces reversed recovers full consistency + positive signed volume; an all-inward cube flips outward; an already-correct cube is unchanged.

description: Fan-triangulate every polygon face into triangles and rebuild a triangle-only Mesh. Distinct from export::triangulate, which yields a GPU-style IndexedTriangles index buffer, not a Mesh. A triangle Mesh is what Loop subdivision, QEM decimation, and the MC/CFD export bridges prefer. Winding preserved. New MeshOp::Triangulate. outram-blender: bisect (plane cut / half-space clip)
description: Blender's Bisect. Cut a mesh by a plane (point + normal) and keep the half where n.(x-point) <= 0, clipping every face against the half-space with Sutherland-Hodgman. New crossing vertices deduped per undirected original edge so adjacent faces share them. Leaves the cut open (composes with fill_holes to cap). Directly serves the CSG/MC half-space workflow. New MeshOp::Bisect { point, normal }. V&V: cube[-1,1]^3 bisected by z=0 (+z) -> open half-box; fill_holes(that) -> watertight chi=2 with signed volume = 4 (half of 8); plane fully outside keeps mesh unchanged; plane fully inside-out yields empty mesh.

outram-blender: revolve / spin (surface of revolution)
description: Blender's Spin. Sweep a profile polyline around an arbitrary axis (point + direction) by an angle in N segments (Rodrigues rotation), connecting consecutive rings with quads. Full 360deg closes the seam (wrap), a partial angle leaves it open. Off-axis profile points only in v1 (on-axis pole points documented as needing a subsequent weld). Generates pipes/tubes/vessels/cones -- surfaces of revolution, on-theme for reactor geometry. Free generator fn (like primitives), not a MeshOp. V&V: a 2-point off-axis segment revolved 360deg/16 -> open 16-gon tube V32 F16 chi0; fill_holes(that) -> closed prism chi2 with positive volume ~ 16-gon*height; a partial 180deg sweep leaves an open strip.

outram-blender: read polyMesh (import) — round out polyMesh I/O
description:
outram-blender can already WRITE OpenFOAM polyMesh three ways (export::to_polymesh_text -> 5 ASCII strings; export::write_polymesh -> disk; feature-gated export::to_poly_mesh -> real outram_foam_basic_lib::io::poly_mesh::PolyMesh). It has NO reader, so a polyMesh cannot be loaded back into a Mesh. Add the import side to complete round-trip polyMesh I/O.

Recommended route (low-risk, no new parser): under the foam bridge feature, add export::from_poly_mesh(&outram_foam_basic_lib::io::poly_mesh::PolyMesh) -> Mesh that converts the PolyMesh points + faceList into the half-edge Mesh boundary surface (Mesh::from_polygons). The foam crate already provides PolyMesh::read(dir) (crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/io/poly_mesh.rs:212), so from_poly_mesh + PolyMesh::read gives full disk read for free. Optionally also a feature-free ASCII parser (points/faces only) for standalone use without the foam dependency.

Caveats to document: a polyMesh is a VOLUME mesh (points/faces/owner/neighbour/cells); outram-blender's Mesh is a boundary surface, so import reconstructs the face soup (all faces), not cells. Winding/owner-neighbour orientation may need a recalc_normals pass.

V&V: round-trip a primitive — write_polymesh(cube) or to_poly_mesh(cube) -> from_poly_mesh -> assert V/E/F/chi == original cube (8/12/6/2), watertight after an optional recalc_normals. Methodology + measured results in the test doc comment per the workspace V&V rule.

title: root@vm
outram-blender: multifidelity neutronics pipeline as a third solver bridge
description:
MAINTAINER REQUEST 2026-08-11: once the HTR-10 multifidelity neutronics pipeline lands, wire it into the outram-blender port.

THE PIPELINE: rigorous Monte Carlo -> MGXS -> deterministic multiphysics -> PRKE + decay heat. Each rung trades fidelity for speed and is validated against the rung above it. Scoped under op-jyyp (HTR-10 simulator); the scoping document is docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md.

WHY BLENDER IS THE RIGHT HOME. crates/outram-blender is the mesh-authoring frontend and ALREADY carries exactly this pattern twice over:
- an opt-in Monte Carlo bridge: mc-export -> sim -> MC Studio
- an OpenFOAM volume-meshing bridge: foam-mesh -> foam_mesh -> tet-dual Mesh Studio
The multifidelity pipeline becomes a THIRD bridge of the same shape — author the geometry, then drive the fidelity ladder from it. The existing MC bridge is the closest precedent and should be read first; rung 1 of the pipeline is the same Monte Carlo engine that bridge already targets, so this may extend that bridge rather than sit beside it. Decide which and record why.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT ALREADY COMMUNICATED UPSTREAM. The pipeline agent has been told to give the pipeline a HEADLESS, SCRIPTABLE entry point taking a geometry description plus a run configuration, rather than something only callable from a test — precisely so a frontend can drive it. If that constraint was not honoured, fixing the pipeline API is in scope here before wrapping it.

REPRODUCIBILITY CARRIES THROUGH THE BRIDGE. The pipeline must emit a run manifest recording the workspace commit, cross-section data and version, MC seed and batch counts, group structure and homogenisation choice. A frontend that drives the pipeline must PRESERVE and surface that manifest rather than hiding it behind a button — a result a user cannot trace back to its inputs is not usable as evidence. Same discipline as the graph digitiser bead op-5v5.8, which must record calibration with every export.

chem-eng: reconcile the new z_domain c2d port with the ZOH recurrences already in stable_transfer_functions
description:
FILED 2026-08-11. Two agents landed overlapping mathematics in this crate on the same day; they must be reconciled rather than left as duplicates.

WORK A (op-fm5, landed, uncommitted in tree): every transfer-function block in BOTH tiers now advances by the exact zero-order-hold / step-invariant discrete equivalent, hand-derived per block. Lives in:
  src/lib/alpha_nightly/stable_transfer_functions/{first_order_transfer_fn,first_order_transfer_fn_with_zeroes,second_order_transfer_fn,decaying_sinusoid,decaying_exponentials}.rs
  src/lib/beta_testing/stable_transfer_functions/{same, minus decaying_exponentials}.rs
  verification + O(1) regression tests: */stable_transfer_functions/recurrence_tests.rs
Each carries a module doc deriving Phi = exp(A T), Gamma = integral_0^T exp(A s) ds * B and citing Astrom & Wittenmark, Seborg et al., Franklin/Powell/Workman, Ogata, Hochbruck & Ostermann, Oppenheim & Schafer, and Smith (open access). No editions/years/pages -- none verified against a physical copy, and that constraint should be kept.

WORK B (concurrent, same day): a z_domain module ported from the GNU Octave control package (GPLv3-or-later), including c2d. That is the SAME transformation, generically implemented.

THE QUESTION TO SETTLE: should the hand-derived per-block recurrences call into z_domain::c2d, or stay as they are?
Arguments for keeping them as-is: they are exact closed forms specialised per block (2-3 scalars, no matrix algebra, no allocation), they are what makes the 0.17 us/step figure possible, and they are already verified against the analytic superposition to ~1e-15. Routing them through a general c2d would likely cost performance and would put an Octave-derived GPL port on the hot path of every controller step.
Arguments for reconciling: one source of truth for the discretisation, and z_domain::c2d could be VERIFIED AGAINST the per-block closed forms -- which is probably the real win here, and is cheap: the recurrence_tests.rs analytic-superposition harness can be pointed at c2d output directly.

RECOMMENDED: keep the specialised recurrences on the hot path; add a cross-check test that z_domain::c2d reproduces them for a first-order lag and for all three second-order damping regimes. That gives the shared-truth benefit with no performance cost.

ALSO CHECK: LICENCE PROVENANCE. The crate was relicensed Apache-2.0 -> GPL-3.0-only on 2026-08-11. The op-fm5 recurrences are original work (derived from textbook-standard mathematics, nothing copied) and carry no upstream provenance. The z_domain code IS an Octave port and needs its NOTICE/attribution-header treatment kept intact per the workspace rule. Do not let a later refactor blur which files are which.

title: tuas: LMTD ambient heat-flux helper has opposite sign conventions and panics when ambient hotter than fluid
description: Found 2026-08-11 by correlation audit during op-4542. crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/heat_transfer_correlations/parallel_heat_exchangers.rs:121-145. The equal-temperature early return computes U*A*(T_amb - T_fluid) (heat INTO fluid, matching the doc); the LMTD branch passes ambient as the cold pair and fluid as the hot pair, yielding T_fluid - T_amb (heat OUT of fluid) -- opposite sign convention between the two branches. Inline comment at L133-134 claims delta T = ambient - fluid, contradicting the actual argument order. Additionally log_mean_temperature_difference panics when hot < cold, so the function panics outright whenever ambient is hotter than the fluid -- the very heat-input case its doc describes.

title: chem-eng: z-domain follow-ups — d2c ZOH (matrix log), c2d foh/impulse-invariant, order > 2 support
description:
CONTEXT: on 2026-08-11 the crate was relicensed Apache-2.0 -> GPL-3.0-only (see crate NOTICE) and a SISO port of the GNU Octave control package's c2d/d2c/tf/filt core landed in src/lib/beta_testing/z_domain/ (upstream gnu-octave/pkg-control commit f39e2625bffc56864c3af746b4410bb71ce6bbb1, GPLv3-or-later side only; the BSD-3 SLICOT kernels were NOT ported). Implemented and verified (11 tests, methodology + measured results in verification_tests.rs doc comments): Zoh, Tustin, TustinPrewarp, MatchedPoleZero c2d; Tustin, TustinPrewarp, MatchedPoleZero d2c; O(1) DF2T discrete stepping.

DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT, in scope for this bead:
1. d2c by zero-order hold — upstream inst/@ss/__d2c__.m computes it with a matrix logarithm (logm of the augmented [A B; 0 I] matrix). Needs a general dense matrix log; not half-implemented.
2. c2d by first-order hold (foh) and impulse-invariant methods — upstream inst/@ss/__c2d__.m (foh via augmented matrix exponential) and imp_invar.m.
3. System order > 2 for Zoh and MatchedPoleZero — currently ZDomainError::UnsupportedOrder, because poles/zeros come from the quadratic formula. General order needs a polynomial root finder (companion-matrix eigenvalues) and/or a scaling-and-squaring expm. Tustin variants already handle any order.
4. Consider whether z_domain should be wired into the controllers layer (a discrete PID via c2d of the analog PID) and whether TUAS-facing alpha_nightly needs a twin — currently z_domain exists in beta_testing only, documented in crate CLAUDE.md.

LICENCE RULE for any follow-up: per-file provenance. If a follow-up ports SLICOT-derived material (anything under slicot-reference/ or the __sl_* kernels), that file's BSD 3-Clause notice must be carried verbatim; do not relabel it GPL. See crate NOTICE.

title: VERIFY CITATIONS: textbook references for the O(1) / ZOH recurrence were supplied from model knowledge, not checked
description:
ACTION: a human must verify these citations against the actual books before any of them appears in a publication, an arXiv draft, or anywhere the project asserts provenance.

WHAT HAPPENED. On 2026-08-11 an AI assistant supplied the literature basis for the exact zero-order-hold / step-invariant discretization used to replace the growing response vectors in chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator (bead op-fm5), and for the analytic exponential integration in crates/teh-o-prke/src/decay_heat.rs. The citations were produced FROM MODEL KNOWLEDGE while offline. Authors, titles and publishers are asserted with reasonable confidence. EDITIONS, YEARS, PAGE NUMBERS, CHAPTER NUMBERS AND EQUATION NUMBERS WERE NOT VERIFIED AND MUST NOT BE ASSUMED CORRECT.

This is exactly the failure mode RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md exists to prevent, and exactly the class of error AI_USAGE.md requires a human to catch. A plausible-looking but wrong citation is worse than no citation, because it survives review by looking right.

CITATIONS TO CHECK:

Sampled-data control theory (the primary basis - the discretization is EXACT, not an approximation, for piecewise-constant input):
1. Astrom, K. J. and Wittenmark, B., "Computer-Controlled Systems: Theory and Design", Prentice Hall. Claimed to derive x[k+1] = Phi x[k] + Gamma u[k] with Phi = exp(A*T) and Gamma = integral_0^T exp(A*s) ds * B in its sampling-of-continuous-systems chapter. VERIFY the chapter and that the result is stated as exact.
2. Seborg, D. E., Edgar, T. F., Mellichamp, D. A. and Doyle, F. J., "Process Dynamics and Control", Wiley.
3. Franklin, G. F., Powell, J. D. and Workman, M. L., "Digital Control of Dynamic Systems", Addison-Wesley.
4. Ogata, K., "Discrete-Time Control Systems", Prentice Hall.

Numerical ODE framing (used in decay_heat.rs, where the motivation is stiffness rather than sampling):
5. Hochbruck, M. and Ostermann, A., "Exponential integrators", Acta Numerica, volume 19 (2010), pages 209-286. The volume, year and page range are asserted and SHOULD BE CHECKED - a journal citation with a specific page range is the easiest of these to get wrong and the easiest to verify.

Signal-processing framing (one-pole IIR filter via impulse invariance):
6. Oppenheim, A. V. and Schafer, R. W., "Discrete-Time Signal Processing", Prentice Hall.
7. Smith, J. O. III, "Introduction to Digital Filters", W3K Publishing. Claimed to be freely available from Stanford CCRMA. If true this is the only OPEN-ACCESS item in the list and the one to prefer where a paywall-free citation is wanted - VERIFY the free availability and the exact title, which has appeared with an "with Audio Applications" subtitle.

ACCESS TIER. Items 1-6 are commercial textbooks and one paywalled journal - proprietary under DATA_POLICY.md. Do NOT ingest them into crates/kovan-literature/open/. The mathematical results are textbook-standard and freely implementable; only the publications are gated. Item 7, if the free availability checks out, may be catalogued open.

ACCEPTANCE: each citation either confirmed with its verified edition/year/pages recorded in the doc comment, or corrected, or removed. Until that is done, every doc comment carrying one of these must retain its unverified-citation disclaimer.

title: njoy endf::interp::terp1 had ENDF laws 3/4 swapped - FIXED 2026-08-11, needs human review
description: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-11 while wiring S(alpha,beta) temperature interpolation (op-1y4y/op-cjw.22 session; fix in working tree, not committed). DEFECT: src/endf/interp.rs terp1 attached the wrong formulas to ENDF INT codes 3 and 4: code 3 (LinLog) computed ln(y)-linear-in-x (which is ENDF law 4) and code 4 (LogLin) computed y-linear-in-ln(x) (which is ENDF law 3). Verified against ENDF-102 0.5.2 and upstream NJOY2016 endf.f90 terp1 (i=3: y=y1+log(x/x1)*(y2-y1)/log(x2/x1); i=4: y=y1*exp((x-x1)*log(y2/y1)/(x2-x1))). The unit tests only covered laws 1/2/5, which is how it slipped through. IMPACT: any TAB1 with INT=3 or INT=4 segments evaluated via terp1/eval_tab1 (reconr linearize, photon, nuclear_data/secondary, purr heating, groupr kinematics LEP) interpolated with the wrong law; most neutron XS tables are INT=2 so the blast radius is limited, but MF7 MT4 extra-temperature LISTs are LI=4 and would have been wrong. FIX: formulas swapped back to ENDF semantics, upstream-parity flat-segment short-circuit (y1==y2 -> y1) added, pinned unit tests for laws 3 and 4 added, reconr/linearize.rs midpoint_energy arm updated (geometric mean now for LinLog|LogLog) and its lin_log_adds_points test corrected to INT=4 (its comment always said 'linear in E but log in sigma'). 393 lib tests pass after the fix. REMAINING: human review; consider re-running any V&V gates for modules that consume INT=3/4 data (RECONR Doppler gates were green after the fix in this session's lib run).

title: tuas: no gas phase in the Material type system — blocks MELCOR-style CVH
description:
crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver has no gas phase in its type system.

- Material enum (src/lib/boussinesq_thermophysical_properties/mod.rs:14) has exactly 2 variants: Solid(SolidMaterial), Liquid(LiquidMaterial).
- LiquidMaterial (:126) has 7 variants: TherminolVP1, DowthermA, HITEC, YD325, FLiBe, FLiNaK, CustomLiquid(...). All six named fluids are single-phase heat-transfer oils or molten salts. No steam, water, water-vapour or air.
- SolidMaterial (:58) has 5 variants: SteelSS304L, Copper, Fiberglass, PyrogelHPS, CustomSolid(...).
- Crate-wide greps for GasMaterial, enum Gas, Material::Gas, VapourMaterial, SteamMaterial, LiquidMaterial::Steam return ZERO hits in src/. Greps for gas|vapou?r|superheat|two-phase|quality in the thermophysical-properties module return zero.

This is architecturally consistent -- the crate is named *Boussinesq*, i.e. incompressible single-phase by construction -- so treat it as a SCOPE BOUNDARY, not an oversight. But the practical consequence is real: MELCOR-style control-volume hydrodynamics (non-condensable gases, vapour/liquid pools, phase change) has no representation here, and adding one means a new Material arm plus every match site updated. Under the workspace no-trait-objects/enum-dispatch rule that is a breaking change to a published enum.

Decision needed from the maintainer: extend tuas, or build CVH in a separate lumped-parameter crate (see the MELCOR-lite epic) and leave tuas single-phase.

Verified 2026-08-07 against the working tree.

notes.content:
UNBLOCKED 2026-08-11 — the sibling HEM Marviken reference has landed (bead op-21g.16, crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/tests/marviken_tests.rs, 6 active tests, ~1.4 s).

READ THE MODULE //! DOC OF THAT FILE FIRST. It states the full reproducible case setup (nozzle 500 mm bore / 166 mm long / L/D = 0.3, converging only, rounded 250 mm-radius inlet; steam dome 4.96 MPa / Tsat 263 degC; vessel water 260 degC for test 23 and 230 degC for test 24 = 3 K and 33 K nominal subcooling, NUREG/CR-2671 Table 4:2 rows 3-6; discharge into containment, peak 236/328 kPa, back pressure assumed 1 atm and shown immaterial since the lowest choke pressure is 2.774 MPa), the data provenance and digitisation uncertainty, the error budget, and a numbered lessons section written specifically for this bead.

HEM reference numbers to compare against (measured 2026-08-11, v0.2.5, release):
- crate HEM dispatcher: test 23 mean |dev| 12.6 % / signed +5.9 % / max 23.1 % (VALIDATED); test 24 mean |dev| 48.6 % / signed -48.5 % / max 70.2 % (NOT validated).
- bare HEM maximum-mass-flux criterion: test 23 mean 10.1 % / signed -10.1 %; test 24 mean 9.0 % / signed -1.8 %.
Use the BARE-CRITERION numbers as the HEM reference for the three-fidelity comparison. The dispatcher's test-24 deficit is a branch-selection defect (bead op-dqng), not HEM physics, and comparing against it would flatter drift-flux for the wrong reason.

Falsifiable expectation recorded there: a non-equilibrium model should NOT gain much on the subcooled branch (HEM is already unbiased there once the right branch is taken). It should gain at the flashing-inception knee of test 24 (3.0-3.3 MPa, where HEM over-predicts up to +26.5 % then under-predicts up to -18.2 %, i.e. puts the knee at too high a pressure) and on test 23's saturated branch (uniform -10.1 % bias, the L/D < 1.5 length effect NUREG/CR-2671 section 9.2 reports).

Tolerance: +/-25 % per point, +/-15 % on the mean. The dominant error term is experimental scatter (+/-12.9 % for test 23, +/-20.0 % for test 24, measured), not digitisation (RMS 6.3 %) and not numerics (<0.001 %). Do not read a 10 % result as better than a 15 % one on this dataset.

EXPLORATION FIRST (marviken_drift_flux_explore, run before any assertion was written, at 5 stagnation points 2.829/3.150/3.725/4.772/4.975 MPa): NO interior maximum anywhere — the steady flux rises monotonically down to the 101.325 kPa containment pressure, as anticipated for a semi-implicit pressure-based scheme with no imposed choking criterion (the RELAP5 situation). 68/69 sweeps in the full gates have no interior maximum; the single exception (4.306 MPa, t24) wins by 0.3 % = plateau noise. title: root@vm
outram-mc-libs: rng::lcg::prn omits OpenMC's PCG-RXS-M-XS output permutation
description:
`outram_mc_libs::rng::lcg::prn` (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/rng/lcg.rs:26) does NOT reproduce OpenMC's `prn`.

Upstream (/home/teddy0/Documents/research/openmc/src/random_lcg.cpp:32-44):

    *seed = (prn_mult * (*seed) + prn_add);
    uint64_t word = ((*seed >> ((*seed >> 59u) + 5u)) ^ *seed) * 12605985483714917081ull;
    uint64_t result = (word >> 43u) ^ word;
    return ldexp(result, -64);

i.e. a PCG-RXS-M-XS output permutation of the LCG state, scaled by 2^-64 (full 64-bit resolution).

Ours:

    *seed = seed.wrapping_mul(MULT).wrapping_add(INC);
    (*seed >> 12) as f64 * (1.0 / (1u64 << 52) as f64)

i.e. the raw top 52 bits of the state, no permutation. The doc comment claims 'Maps to double prn(uint64_t* seed) in OpenMC' — it does not.

MEASURED EVIDENCE (2026-08-06). From seed = 1, first five draws:
  ours:   0.423209170872713, 0.509407442883721, 0.648359393963430, 0.382863390508260, 0.795447749253532
  openmc: 0.710817359881671, 0.752996005805941, 0.330118988789542, 0.467186818550906, 0.046254968305997
The LCG STATE recurrence is identical on both sides (state after 5 draws = 0xCBA276B4B881A9F0 either way), so future_seed / jump-ahead / init_seed / the GPU integer-state mirror tests are all unaffected and remain correct. Only the state -> double output mapping diverges.

IMPACT. Our uniforms are a statistically reasonable generator (top bits of an LCG), so this is not a correctness catastrophe the way op-rbo was — but it does mean this crate can NEVER reproduce an OpenMC random sequence bit-for-bit, which undercuts the crate's stated purpose (CLAUDE.md: 'the crate's entire value is fidelity to OpenMC'). It also violates the mandatory porting rule: the current implementation is a re-derivation, not a port.

WHY NOT FIXED UNDER op-rbo (deliberate scoping decision, 2026-08-06). Blast radius is far larger than init_seed's:
  - every random number in the crate changes -> every k-eff, every V&V CSV, every openmc_notebook_comparison must be re-run;
  - the WGSL shaders (src/gpu/shaders/*, gpu::batched_flight / batched_event) derive their f32 uniform from the state with the port's formula and would need matching changes plus new GPU-vs-CPU mirror numbers;
  - crates/raffles consumes rng::lcg::prn directly (samplers.rs:315,437,541,1085) and its sampler outputs/recorded results would shift; that crate was explicitly out of bounds for the op-rbo agent.
This needs its own planned change with a full re-run of the crate's recorded statistics, not a drive-by.

ALSO NOTED while auditing rng/lcg.rs (no action taken):
  - future_seed matches upstream (random_lcg.cpp:91-120) exactly, including operation order. Verified.
  - MULT / INC / DEFAULT_STRIDE match prn_mult / prn_add / DEFAULT_STRIDE exactly. Verified.
  - NOT ported at all: future_prn (:50), advance_prn_seed (:82), init_particle_seeds (:70), and the N_STREAMS = 4 stream-index constants (random_lcg.h:12-16). init_particle_seeds in particular is the idiomatic upstream way to give one particle its four streams; callers here hand-roll it. Consider porting them for API parity.
  - Lcg64 is new work (an oorandom::Rand64 compat shim for boon-lay), not an OpenMC port; its rand_u64 returns the raw LCG state, whose low bits are weak. Fine as-is but should not be mistaken for an upstream-faithful API.

title: HTR-10: wire the graphite/moderator feedback channel into PRKE (remainder of op-jyyp.6)
description:
The graphite/moderator reactivity channel itself has landed as `crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/feedback.rs` (GraphiteModeratorFeedback: own temperature state, own caller-supplied coefficient, lumped m*cp ODE step, thermal time constant; 6 tests green). What remains of op-jyyp.6 is the KINETICS WIRING, which deliberately did NOT go in the tampines library:

- The tampines library is free of teh-o-prke (it is only an Android-gated dev-dependency), so feedback.rs returns a plain dimensionless reactivity for a caller to sum with a fuel Doppler term and feed to a kinetics solver.
- The wiring therefore belongs in an example or in nee_soon, where a neutronics dependency is appropriate. Do not add teh-o-prke to the tampines library to close this.

Also outstanding, and the real blocker on any quantitative use: a MODERATOR-ONLY temperature coefficient. None is supplied, on purpose. The published HTR-10 figures in IAEA-TECDOC-1382 part 2 Table 4-33 (NRG -7.37e-5/-8.05e-5 per C; INET/VSOP -7.49e-5/-9.15e-5 per C) are ISOTHERMAL coefficients (fuel + moderator moved together); they are exposed in feedback.rs as clearly-labelled constants for validating a whole-core isothermal calculation, and using one as alpha_m would double-count fuel Doppler. A moderator-only coefficient has to come from a neutronics calculation that perturbs the moderator alone (rung 3 -> rung 4 hand-off, docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 5.4).

Measured supporting figure (2026-08-11, feedback.rs::graphite_thermal_time_constant_is_long): the derived HTR-10 pebble-graphite inventory of 5129.16 kg against a bed conductance of 97473.9 W/K gives a thermal time constant of 89.37 s - and that is the pebbles alone, excluding the 1 m side reflector. Against an effectively instantaneous fuel Doppler response, this is why the two channels must stay separate.

title: HTR-10 rung 1: pebble-bed Monte Carlo reference k_eff, with sigma and stated data provenance
description:
Parent: op-841p. Rung 1 is the reference every other rung is validated against, so its credibility is the pipeline's credibility.

TARGET SEQUENCE, cheapest first, each with a published number to hit:
1a. TRISO grain unit cell, infinite medium. DONE as a code exercise: crates/outram-mc-libs/examples/htr10_fuel_zone_kinf.rs (see comment on this bead for the measured numbers). Free-gas thermal scattering, so NOT a physics result.
1b. Infinite pebble-bed lattice k_inf vs Serpent 1.6321 / HCP 1.6416 (Tantillo et al. 2020, Nucl. Eng. Des. 362, 110603, PROPRIETARY tier - cite, do not re-host).
1c. BCC fuel + graphite ball lattice k_inf vs MCNP5 1.77078 +/- 0.00008 (Wang et al. 2014, config b, PROPRIETARY tier).
1d. B1 detailed core k_eff at the measured 16890-ball / 123.06 cm loading vs MCNP5 1.01620 +/- 0.00014 (Wang et al. 2014, config c).

Steps 1a-1c are reachable with the existing reflective-cube driver run_keff_delta. Step 1d needs run_keff_csg plus a bed model.

EVERY REPORTED k MUST CARRY: sigma, particles per generation, inactive and active generation counts, RNG seed, cross-section library and version, fidelity tier (from_core LOW vs from_endf HIGH), and the thermal-scattering treatment. A k_eff without sigma and without data provenance is not a result.

STATE WHICH PROBLEM: B1-as-defined (helium, 20 C, dummy balls 1.73 g/cm3 and 1.3 ppm boron) or B1-as-measured (humid air 0.1013 MPa at 15 C, water-vapour density 2.57e-5 g/cm3, dummy balls 1.84 g/cm3 and 0.125 ppm). They differ by about +1000 pcm - larger than the published code-to-code spread of 683 +/- 22 pcm. Conflating them invalidates the comparison against the measured 123.06 cm.

Benchmark specification is typed data at crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/neutronics.rs. Scoping: docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 4.1.

notes.content:
RUNG 1 STEP 1a COMPLETED as a code exercise, 2026-08-11. crates/outram-mc-libs/examples/htr10_fuel_zone_kinf.rs.

PROBLEM: HTR-10 fuel-zone infinite medium, run twice - kernels resolved explicitly as randomly packed spheres, then the same nuclide inventory homogenised. Atom densities straight from IAEA-TECDOC-1382 Table 4-38 (OPEN tier, part 2 line 1101). Kernel volume fraction of the fuelled zone = 8335 * (0.025/2.5)^3 = 8.335e-3.

MEASURED (main run, 400 particles/generation, 10 inactive + 40 active, RNG seed 1, packing seed 20260811, 1018 kernels of r = 0.025 cm in a reflective cube of half-width 1 cm, realized packing fraction 0.008328, T = 293.15 K, delta tracking with a bin-maximum bounding majorant):
  heterogeneous k_inf = 1.57269 +/- 0.00877
  homogenised   k_inf = 1.45189 +/- 0.00820
  delta k = -12081 +/- 1201 pcm; delta rho = -5291 +/- 526 pcm; 10.1 sigma
A smoke run at 200/8/25 gave 1.60870 +/- 0.02031 and 1.47273 +/- 0.01489, agreeing with the main run to 1.6 sigma on the heterogeneous case.

SIGN IS A PHYSICS CHECK AND IT PASSES: resolving the kernels depresses the flux inside each lump at the U-238 resonance energies, so fewer resonance absorptions per U-238 atom and k rises; homogenising removes the depression so it must come out lower. It does.

THIS IS NOT A PHYSICS RESULT AND NOT AN HTR-10 CRITICALITY RESULT:
- Thermal scattering is FREE GAS. Graphite S(alpha,beta) does not reach the transport path (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/thermal.rs:24-26). On a graphite-moderated thermal system this alone disqualifies the absolute number.
- It is a fuel-zone infinite medium - no shell, no dummy ball, no bed, no reflector, no leakage. NO published HTR-10 value corresponds to this problem, so the absolute k_inf cannot be compared to the literature at all.
- TRISO coatings unresolved (op-6tz.35). LOW fidelity tier (flat nu-bar, Watt chi stand-in, ~+500 pcm on Godiva). k_std is a generation-batch SEM with no inter-generation correlation correction. op-rbo and op-jis inherited.
- The delta k is NOT comparable to Wang et al.'s unit-cell biases: theirs are multigroup XS PROCESSING biases against a CE reference on the full model and run the other way (+2820 pcm for INFHOMMEDIUM). This is a CE GEOMETRIC effect on a different problem.

WHAT IT DOES ESTABLISH: the rung-1 chain runs end to end on this reactor's real materials, reproducibly from a stated seed, with a correctly signed self-shielding effect.

COST WARNING for step 1d: thermal neutrons in graphite scatter hundreds of times per history. The 400/10/40 run took roughly 20 minutes for 40,000 histories. Budget compute accordingly.

Full write-up: docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 11.

VTB generic-pbr ZBS 18-point k_eff table cannot be reproduced by the ZBS correlation with helium -- reference data suspect
description: FINDING 2026-08-11, from implementing the analytic ZBS closure (op-jyyp.3). The 18-point pebble-bed effective-conductivity tabulation in reference-data/virtual_test_bed/htgr/generic-pbr/pbr.i block keff_pebble_bed (300-2000 K, 11.94-44.95 W/(m K)) -- transcribed as the reference table in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/zbs.rs and named the acceptance target for the analytic ZBS -- CANNOT be produced by the Zehner-Bauer-Schlunder correlation with the deck's own stated inputs (eps=0.39, d_pebble=0.06 m, emissivity=0.8, graphite k_s=26 W/(m K), helium at 6 MPa). Evidence, all computed 2026-08-11: (1) full ZBS (van Antwerpen 2010 form, contact phi=0.0077, C=1.25) with helium k_f from the KTA 3102.1 correlation gives 2.08 W/(m K) at 300 K vs the table's 11.94 (-83%), 10.5 vs 27.3 at 1000 K, 29.0 vs 45.0 at 2000 K; (2) inverting for the fluid conductivity the table would require gives k_f = 3.8 W/(m K) at 300 K rising past 40 at 1300 K -- no gas has this; (3) physically, stagnant-helium graphite pebble-bed effective conductivity at ambient is order 1-2 W/(m K) (SANA/HTTU-class experiments), so 11.94 at 300 K is not a physical stagnant-bed value under any correlation. The generating configuration is unknown -- SAM is closed-source, and the ANL reports (ANL/NSE-19/46, the NT24-115 SAM thermal-fluids paper, ANL pebble-temperature paper) cite the ZBS model but do not print the evaluation that produced this table. The analytic ZBS in crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/zbs.rs carries a documented-discrepancy test recording the full 18-point comparison. CONSEQUENCE: the zbs.rs module doc in the digital-twin-engine frames this table as 'the published reference an analytic ZBS implementation must reproduce' -- that framing needs revisiting by the maintainer (that crate is owned by another agent; not edited). The table remains a faithful transcription of what the VTB/SAM model USED; the question is whether it is what ZBS PRODUCES. Options: keep the table as the interim bed conductivity (it is what the VTB transient models ran with), use the analytic ZBS, or obtain the full NEA PBMR-400 spec / SAM documentation to resolve the generating inputs.

title: HTR-10: graphite properties in the solid material database
description:
Nothing downstream works without this. The TUAS solid database currently holds only copper, stainless, fibreglass, aerogel, FeCrAl and a generic heating element. There is no graphite anywhere in the workspace.

SCOPE: matrix-grade and reflector-grade nuclear graphite with density, specific heat capacity and thermal conductivity as functions of temperature, plus conductivity degradation with fast-neutron dose. Dose dependence matters because irradiated reflector conductivity falls substantially and that changes the passive decay-heat path.

boon-lay DEFECT: TRISO release verification test asserts against itself, not the reference
description:
A correctness defect independent of HTR-10, surfaced by the HTR-10 capability audit. Raised here because the scoping doc flags it as warranting its own bead.

THE DEFECT: crates/boon-lay/.../release_fraction_crp_6_case_1a_1b.rs:50 wraps its assertion against the published reference range in catch_unwind and DISCARDS the result, then asserts the code own output against a value that lies OUTSIDE that reference range. title: HTR-10 V&V: PBMR-400 coupled benchmark first, then HTR-10 criticality and safety demonstration tests
description:
Per docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md section 5: target PBMR-400 BEFORE HTR-10. It is the most completely specified open pebble-bed benchmark and it exercises exactly the coupling that has to be built. Reaching HTR-10 measured transients with an unvalidated bed model would be guessing.

SEQUENCE:
1. PBMR-400 OECD/NEA coupled benchmark — steady state, then depressurised and pressurised loss of cooling, then rod withdrawal.
2. HTR-10 initial criticality (critical loading height) from the IAEA HTGR benchmark programme.
3. HTR-10 safety demonstration tests — loss of forced cooling without scram, and control-rod withdrawal without scram. Expect digitised plots rather than tabulated data, and record the digitisation procedure and its uncertainty as part of provenance.

Per the V&V rule, documentation must carry BOTH methodology and results: the reference, the inputs, the pass criterion, AND the measured numbers with uncertainty and the date taken. Depends on the bed closures and the graphite feedback channel.

Report disagreement honestly. A documented mismatch is a result; a quietly loosened tolerance is not.

notes.content:
HTR-10 thermal-hydraulic V&V targets, extracted 2026-08-11 from Gao, Z. and Shi, L. (2002), Thermal hydraulic calculation of the HTR-10 for the initial and equilibrium core, Nucl. Eng. Des. 218, 51-64, doi 10.1016/S0029-5493(02)00198-X. PROPRIETARY (Elsevier, all rights reserved) - catalogued at crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/gao2002htr10th.json, gitignored. Cite it and implement from it; do NOT re-host the PDF.

This paper closes the gap that the VTB cannot: docs/reactor-scoping/vtb-findings.md records that VTB has NO HTR-10 thermal hydraulics at all. Gao and Shi supply calculated power, temperature and flow distributions for BOTH the initial and the equilibrium core.

QUANTITATIVE TARGETS TO VALIDATE AGAINST:
- Maximum fuel temperature 1046 C at 120 percent overload. This is the headline number to reproduce.
- HTR-10 maximum fuel temperature LIMIT is 1230 C under normal and accident conditions, per the experiment specification. NOTE this is NOT the 1600 C figure that appears throughout the modular-HTR literature (including the JRC book kugeler2017vhtr) - 1600 C is the generic coated-particle retention limit, 1230 C is HTR-10 own specified limit. Do not conflate them.
- Bypass flow through the gaps between graphite components is under 10 percent of rated flow. Any bed model that ignores bypass is therefore making a 10 percent error in core flow.
- Uncertainties the paper explicitly carries into the peak fuel temperature: non-uniform burnup, power distribution deviation, manufacturing deviation of fuel elements, graphite balls mixed with fuel balls in the initial core, and heat-transfer calculation deviation. A V&V comparison that ignores these is comparing a best-estimate to a conservative number.
- Initial core contains graphite balls mixed uniformly with fuel balls to suppress excess reactivity; the equilibrium core has none. These are two DIFFERENT validation cases, not one.

Confirms the operating point already taken from the IAEA benchmark: 10 MW, 3.0 MPa, 4.3 kg/s, 700 C outlet, 250 C inlet, feedwater 104 C, steam 440 C at 4.0 MPa.

tampines: gas-phase component layer for the HTR-10 helium primary circuit
description:
Replaces the mistaken op-jyyp.4, which proposed adding a gas arm to the TUAS Material enum. Maintainer ruling 2026-08-11: TUAS is for SALT solvers only and must never gain a gas arm; gas belongs in tampines.

THE NEED. An HTR-10 primary circuit is a helium loop at 3.0 MPa flowing 4.3 kg/s between 250 C and 700 C. Nothing in the workspace can currently model that with prebuilt components: TUAS has the component library but is salt-scoped, and tampines has the composition role but its component layer returns not-implemented for everything except Pipe::step.

WHAT TO BUILD. A gas-phase component layer in crates/tampines that can represent a forced-convection helium circuit: pipe/duct pressure drop and heat transfer for a compressible gas, the pebble-bed core as a porous component, and the circulator. Properties come from crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop, which already carries a full Helmholtz EOS for helium plus real NIST-lineage viscosity and thermal-conductivity correlations tested against tabulated reference states — consume those, do not reimplement or hardcode.

KNOWN DEFECT TO FIX WHILE HERE. htgr_sim_v1 currently hardcodes a constant helium viscosity despite the real correlation existing one crate away in coolprop. That shortcut should not survive into the gas layer.

RELATED WORK ALREADY LANDED. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/ carries the cited HTR-10 design point and a verified KTA packed-bed pressure-drop implementation (reproduces the VTB gold values to every quoted digit). The gas layer should consume that rather than re-deriving it.

ALSO NOTE op-ql8 — tampines already has an open bead to wire the tested dwsim flash and finish the NotYetImplemented component wrappers. These two overlap; sequence them together rather than in conflict.

Do not widen TUAS. If a change appears to require touching tuas_boussinesq_solver Material enum, stop and reconsider the design.

notes.content:
SCOPE REFINEMENT from the maintainer, 2026-08-11: TUAS is not salt-only — it also does LIQUID METAL, even though salt was the original intent. So the boundary that matters is PHASE, not chemistry: TUAS covers LIQUIDS (molten salts and liquid metals), and GAS is the excluded phase.

That makes the ruling sharper rather than weaker. Do not read the earlier note on op-jyyp.4 as 'TUAS is for salt' — read it as 'TUAS is for liquids, and helium is not a liquid'. Adding a liquid-metal coolant to TUAS would be in scope; adding a gas arm is not, and that is why the HTR-10 helium circuit belongs in tampines.

Practical consequence for whoever implements this bead: do not try to generalise the TUAS Material enum into a phase-generic abstraction as a way of sneaking gas in. The liquid assumption is baked into the solver itself — TUAS is the Thermo-hydraulic Uniphase Advection and Convection Solver built on the Boussinesq approximation, which assumes small density variation. Helium at 3.0 MPa over a 250-700 C range varies in density by roughly a factor of two across the core, so the Boussinesq assumption does not hold for it. The exclusion is physical, not merely organisational.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
FINAL SCOPE FRAMING from the maintainer, 2026-08-11 — supersedes the two notes above, which were successively too narrow:

TUAS handles anything SINGLE-PHASE and NEARLY INCOMPRESSIBLE. That is liquids in practice — molten salts and liquid metals. An incompressible gas would technically fit the solver, but that restriction is severe enough that the maintainer explicitly does NOT want gas promised as a TUAS capability. Treat gas as out of scope for TUAS, full stop.

TAMPINES IS THE SUPERSET THAT INCLUDES TUAS. That is the architectural point and it resolves the whole question: gas support does not require widening TUAS, because tampines already sits above it and composes it alongside outram-park-fork-coolprop, tampines-steam-tables, outram-foam-basic-lib and chem-eng. Adding a gas layer at the tampines level is the natural place for it, not a workaround.

So the correct reading of this bead is not 'TUAS cannot do it, so find somewhere else'. It is 'tampines is where the superset lives, and a compressible helium circuit is a superset capability'.

Physical justification, unchanged: helium at 3.0 MPa across 250-700 C varies in density by roughly a factor of two through the core, so the nearly-incompressible assumption TUAS is built on genuinely does not hold for the HTR-10 primary circuit.

HTR-10 accident: air ingress and graphite oxidation
description:
One of the three HTGR-specific accident sequences, none of which had a bead before 2026-08-11. Source material is already in the archive: kugeler2017vhtr (EUR 28712 EN, open) covers modular-HTR safety and its appendix summarises the key safety experiments.

THE PHYSICS. If the primary boundary fails and air enters a hot graphite core, graphite oxidises: C + O2 -> CO2 and the Boudouard reaction C + CO2 -> 2CO, which is endothermic and becomes significant at high temperature. The consequences that matter are structural degradation of the graphite (it is the core structural material AND the moderator), a chemical heat source, and CO production. Reaction rate is diffusion-limited or chemically-limited depending on temperature, so the regime matters more than the raw Arrhenius constant.

WHY THIS IS TRACTABLE HERE. crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs already carries the reactor and equilibrium machinery this needs, with zero todo!(): gibbs_reactor.rs (multiphase Gibbs energy minimisation), equilibrium_reactor.rs, conversion_reactor.rs, pfr.rs, cstr.rs, plus a full reactions model. Graphite oxidation is a gas-solid equilibrium-plus-kinetics problem of exactly the shape that layer already solves. Reuse it rather than writing fresh chemistry.

Depends on graphite properties (op-jyyp.1) for the solid side and on the bed model for where the heat goes.

Kinetics must come from open published sources with provenance per DATA_POLICY.md. If only a lumped rate is used, say so in the doc comment rather than implying a mechanistic model.

title: HTR-10 accident: water/steam ingress and the water-gas shift reaction
description:
The second HTGR-specific accident sequence. HTR-10 has a once-through helical-coil steam generator with helium on the shell side at 3.0 MPa and water/steam in the tubes at 4.0 MPa, so the water side is at HIGHER pressure than the helium. A tube rupture therefore drives water into the primary circuit, not the other way round.

THE PHYSICS. Steam meets hot graphite: C + H2O -> CO + H2 (the steam-graphite reaction, endothermic), followed by the WATER-GAS SHIFT reaction CO + H2O <-> CO2 + H2. Consequences: graphite corrosion, hydrogen generation, and a moderator/reactivity effect from the water in the core. The shift reaction is equilibrium-limited and strongly temperature dependent, which is exactly what a Gibbs minimiser is for.

THE PAYOFF THE MAINTAINER IDENTIFIED. This is the same chemistry as the refinery epic op-1z3o. crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/reactors/gibbs_reactor.rs serves both, and DWSIM SHIPS TWO WATER-GAS SHIFT REFERENCE FLOWSHEETS that are converged cases with known answers:
  PlatformFiles/Common/tests/WATER_GAS_SHIFT_REACTION.dwxmz
  PlatformFiles/Common/tests/Flowsheet5_StudyOnTheEffectsOfInertsOnWaterGasShiftReaction.dwxmz
in the pinned upstream clone at /home/teddy0/Documents/research/dwsim-upstream (branch windows, commit 1abf72d1b6b41d3e9a8cc770d3cc4e8fc76e5766, GPL-3.0). Those are ready-made V&V cases for the shift chemistry, and validating the reactor block once serves BOTH the refinery hydrogen plant and this accident sequence.

So: validate the shift reactor against the DWSIM reference flowsheets first, then apply it to the graphite-steam system. Do not build a second, separate shift implementation.

title: HTR-10 accident: primary depressurisation and choked flow
description:
The third HTGR-specific accident sequence, and the prerequisite for the other two: a break has to be characterised before you can say how much air or water enters through it.

THE PHYSICS. Helium at 3.0 MPa discharging to a ventilated confinement at atmospheric pressure is deeply choked (critical pressure ratio for a monatomic gas, gamma = 5/3, is about 0.487, so any downstream pressure below ~1.46 MPa gives sonic flow). Blowdown rate sets the depressurisation timescale, which sets when natural circulation can establish and therefore when air ingress begins. The PBMR-400 benchmark distinguishes PRESSURISED from DEPRESSURISED loss of forced cooling precisely because the two give very different core temperatures.

THE PAYOFF THE MAINTAINER IDENTIFIED. crates/tampines already has a critical_flow module. CAUTION: bead op-bcg records that its documentation CLAIMS Marviken validation THAT DOES NOT EXIST. So the critical-flow solver is a real asset but an unvalidated one, and op-bcg must be resolved before any depressurisation result is quoted. Marviken is a steam/water critical-flow test series in any case; a helium blowdown is a single-phase compressible gas problem and needs its own verification, most naturally against the analytical choked-flow solution for an ideal monatomic gas before moving to real-gas helium from outram-park-fork-coolprop.

SEQUENCING: verify choked flow analytically -> depressurisation transient -> then the air-ingress and steam-ingress beads, which both depend on knowing the break flow.

Also relates to op-1z3o.12 (pressure-flow network solve for the refinery dynamic mode) — both need flow driven by pressure difference rather than specified, so the formulations should be consistent even though the fluids differ.

notes.content:
CORRECTION 2026-08-11 — this bead understated existing progress. Maintainer: 'while marviken validation is not done, edwards is.'

VERIFIED IN CODE. Edwards-O'Brien pipe blowdown IS implemented and tested in crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/ (not in critical_flow/). tests.rs records the actual case inputs — initial enthalpy h = 9.857170e5 J/kg, pipe L = 4.096 m, D = 0.073 m, horizontal — and geometry.rs and drift_flux.rs carry Edwards-specific doc comments in the V&V style. So depressurisation-transient capability is NOT starting from zero.

WHAT op-bcg ACTUALLY SAYS, restated precisely so the two are not conflated: the false claim is in crates/tampines/src/critical_flow/, whose docs reference Moody / Zaloudek / Marviken data. Marviken is not done. Edwards is. Those are different modules and different benchmarks — do not treat op-bcg as invalidating the Edwards work.

THE REMAINING GAP FOR THIS BEAD IS STILL REAL, AND IT IS A FLUID-PHYSICS GAP, NOT A MISSING-CODE GAP. Edwards-O'Brien is a FLASHING TWO-PHASE WATER blowdown: subcooled water depressurises, flashes, and the choking is two-phase. An HTR-10 primary depressurisation is SINGLE-PHASE COMPRESSIBLE HELIUM. The drift-flux machinery Edwards validates is not the machinery a helium blowdown needs.

So the sequencing stands but the starting point is better than written:
1. Verify single-phase compressible choked flow analytically for an ideal monatomic gas (gamma = 5/3, critical pressure ratio ~0.487), which is a closed-form check.
2. Move to real-gas helium properties from outram-park-fork-coolprop.
3. Then the depressurisation transient.
The Edwards work gives a validated transient-blowdown framework to build within; it does not give helium choking for free.
