tampines pebble_bed::zbs is 317 lines with ZERO tests — never checked against its reference table
description:
Landed 2026-08-11 by an agent that was STOPPED MID-TASK, so it never wrote tests or filed its own handoff. Found during the session-end sweep.

STATE. crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/zbs.rs is 317 lines implementing the Zehner-Bauer-Schlunder effective bed conductivity: new(), htr10(), deformation_factor(), radiation_ratio(), effective_conductivity(), stagnant_conductivity(). It contains NO todo!() and NO unimplemented!() — it is a real implementation, not a scaffold. It also contains ZERO #[test]. crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/mod.rs (41 lines) declares only `pub mod zbs;` so the tree is self-consistent and cargo check --workspace --all-targets passes with 0 errors.

THE PROBLEM. The whole acceptance criterion for this model was that it reproduce the verified 18-point reference table, and that check has never been run. An untested 317-line correlation is not evidence of anything — it is a plausible-looking implementation whose agreement with the reference is unknown.

THE ORACLE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS READ-ONLY. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/zbs.rs carries the 18-point Zehner-Bauer-Schlunder tabulation transcribed verbatim from the NRIC/INL Virtual Test Bed (reference-data/virtual_test_bed/htgr/generic-pbr/pbr.i), spanning 300-2000 K and 11.940293-44.9504677 W/(m*K), with an exact-at-nodes interpolant already verified (max relative error 0.0, monotonic over 1701 samples). Do not edit that file; consume it as the oracle.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Test the analytic model against all 18 points and record the ACTUAL agreement with a stated tolerance and date, per the V&V rule. If it disagrees, report the disagreement — do NOT tune the model to match, and do NOT loosen the tolerance.
2. Add the analytic limits, which are falsifiable and cheap: zero emissivity must recover the stagnant-gas-plus-solid limit with no radiation term; the effective conductivity must lie between the series and parallel bounds of its constituents; and it must increase monotonically with temperature once radiation is active.
3. State the homogenisation assumption in the doc comment explicitly rather than leaving it implicit.

NOTE the radiation contribution grows strongly with temperature and is what carries decay heat out during a loss of forced cooling. If it is wrong or absent the passive safety case looks better than it is, which is the specific way this model could quietly mislead.

title: tampines: the remaining three pebble-bed conduction scales (TRISO, pebble, CHT) plus the feedback channel
description:
Handoff for work an agent was STOPPED MID-TASK on, 2026-08-11. It never filed its own follow-up, so this records where it actually stopped.

WHAT LANDED (committed at 4feb6c84, compiles clean, workspace cargo check --all-targets = 0 errors):
- crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver: NuclearGraphiteMatrixA3 and NuclearGraphiteIG110 added to SolidMaterial, with solid_database/nuclear_graphite.rs implementing them. No todo!(). All the non-exhaustive match sites the new enum variants created were filled — that is the enum-over-trait-object design working as intended, forcing every dispatch site to be handled.
- crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/: mod.rs (41 lines) + zbs.rs (317 lines, UNTESTED — see the sibling bead).

WHAT DID NOT LAND. The maintainer directed that all four nested conduction scales live in crates/tampines. Only the bed scale exists. Still to build, and they NEST — each level effective property is the next level input, which is why they belong together:

1. TRISO PARTICLE CONDUCTION. The coated-particle stack: UO2 kernel, porous carbon buffer, IPyC, SiC, OPyC. Cited HTR-10 geometry from the IAEA benchmark: kernel radius 0.025 cm, UO2 density 10.4 g/cm3, 5.0 g heavy metal per pebble, 17 percent enriched. MAINTAINER APPROVED REUSING crates/boon-lay, which already has four-layer TRISO CSG geometry and per-layer temperature-dependent properties — take the GEOMETRY and conduction properties, NOT the release model, which op-jyyp.10 records as unvalidated (its verification test wraps the reference assertion in catch_unwind and discards it). There is currently no tampines -> boon-lay dependency edge; add it as a path dependency. Both crates are GPL-3.0 so there is no licence question.
2. PEBBLE CONDUCTION. 6.0 cm sphere, 5.0 cm fuelled zone, unfuelled graphite shell, matrix graphite 1.73 g/cc. The fuelled zone is a TRISO dispersion in graphite, so its effective conductivity comes from level 1 plus a packing model — do not treat it as homogeneous graphite without saying so.
3. CONJUGATE HEAT TRANSFER. Bed to helium via the Wakao particle-to-fluid Nusselt correlation already in TUAS (nusselt_number_correlations/input_structs.rs:152, already expressed on pebble diameter, the right form), and the solid path onward to the reflector. Check what conjugate-heat machinery exists before writing new.
4. GRAPHITE/MODERATOR FEEDBACK CHANNEL (op-jyyp.6). Its own reactivity channel, NOT lumped into fuel Doppler — the large graphite mass is what gives HTR-10 its long thermal time constant and self-limiting transient response.

TEST WITH ANALYTIC LIMITS, which are genuinely falsifiable: uniform properties must collapse a multilayer solution to the single-material result; zero radiation must recover the stagnant-gas-plus-solid limit; effective conductivity must lie between series and parallel bounds. Each level independently testable so a failure localises to a scale.

Per Wang et al. 2014 (catalogued proprietary) treating the double heterogeneity as homogeneous costs roughly +2800 pcm in k_eff; the thermal analogue is real too, so state the homogenisation assumption at each level in the doc comments.

title: TUAS nuclear graphite: two documented assumptions carrying real physical risk
description:
Raised by the implementing agent 2026-08-11 as part of op-jyyp.1 (landed in commit 4feb6c84, crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/.../solid_database/nuclear_graphite.rs, 871 lines, 6 V&V tests). Both assumptions are documented at the site rather than hidden, but both should be reviewed before any result depending on them is trusted.

1. ONE cp CURVE SERVES BOTH GRADES. The specific-heat table is grade-insensitive: NuclearGraphiteMatrixA3 and NuclearGraphiteIG110 dispatch to the same shared enthalpy and cp functions. The enum arms were deliberately duplicated per variant rather than collapsed into an or-pattern, precisely so this decision stays greppable and has to be revisited explicitly if the assumption is challenged. Check whether the grades genuinely share a cp curve within the accuracy this work needs.

2. THE A3 DAMAGE FACTOR IS APPLIED TO IG-110, WHICH THE VTB DOES NOT DO. The fast-neutron-fluence conductivity degradation was fitted for matrix graphite A3 and is being reused for IG-110. The source the correlations came from does not make that extension. Irradiated reflector conductivity drives the passive decay-heat path, so if IG-110 degrades differently this propagates straight into the loss-of-forced-cooling result — the exact place where an optimistic error makes the safety case look better than it is.

WHAT THE TESTS ACTUALLY ESTABLISH, per the implementing agent: "Nothing here is checked against HTR-10 measurements. The tests verify transcription and interpolation against hand evaluations of the same formulas — that is all they establish." The word "validated" appears nowhere in the added code or docs, correctly.

Measured behaviour for reference: damage factor is 1.0 at zero fluence and 0.139 at gam = 15, still positive, with the zero crossing near gam = 19. The fluence gate is [0, 15] and returns an error rather than clamping.

title: HTR-10: Ergun / KTA packed-bed pressure drop — implement the existing todo!()
description:
A declared-but-unimplemented gap with a known location, so this is a well-bounded first coding task.

CURRENT STATE: the packed-bed pressure-drop variant is declared WITH its citation at crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/.../fluid_component_calculation/mod.rs:48 and is a todo!() at :161. Meanwhile the gFHR pebble-bed components carry the comment "not putting in ergun equation yet" SEVENTEEN times and use pipe friction on a pebble-derived hydraulic diameter instead — so the wrong correlation is currently in use in more than one place.

SCOPE: implement the Ergun form (viscous plus inertial terms in bed voidage and particle diameter) and the KTA correlation used for pebble beds specifically, then replace the seventeen pipe-friction stand-ins. Verify against the analytical limits and published packed-bed data with the numbers recorded in the test doc comment per the V&V rule.

Note the TUAS porous-media component states its own gap: pressure-drop correlations are not properly implemented so it behaves like a pipe. This bead closes that.

title: HTR-10: pebble-bed effective radial thermal conductivity
description:
Literally zero code in the workspace, and it is the single most important closure for HTR-10 passive safety behaviour — it sets how fast decay heat conducts radially out of the bed when forced cooling is lost.

SCOPE: an effective conductivity model summing the solid, stagnant-gas, particle-contact and radiation contributions, with the near-wall region correction where bed voidage rises and the correlation changes. Radiation matters increasingly at the high temperatures reached in a loss-of-forced-cooling transient, so it cannot be dropped.

Depends on graphite properties. Validate against published packed-bed afterheat-removal experiment data — German AVR-era and THTR-era packed-bed heat-transfer experiments are the relevant open source. Record the measured comparison with uncertainty in the test doc comment.

HTR-10: add a gas arm to the TUAS Material enum
description:
Small structural unblock with large leverage. The TUAS Material enum is solid-or-liquid only, so the entire TUAS prebuilt component library cannot currently be used for a helium loop — which is most of what an HTR-10 primary circuit is.

SCOPE: add a gas variant and wire it through the property dispatch so gas-phase components resolve density, viscosity, conductivity and heat capacity. Helium properties should route to crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop, which already carries a full Helmholtz EOS plus real NIST-lineage viscosity and conductivity correlations, tested against tabulated reference states.

notes.content:
CORRECTED BY THE MAINTAINER 2026-08-11 — THIS BEAD AS WRITTEN IS WRONG. DO NOT IMPLEMENT IT.

Maintainer ruling: TUAS should NEVER have a gas arm. That was never its intent — tuas_boussinesq_solver is for SALT solvers only. Its Material enum being solid-or-liquid is a deliberate scope boundary, not an oversight, and adding a gas variant would widen a crate past its designed purpose.

GAS BELONGS IN tampines, which is the central thermal-hydraulic framework and already composes tuas, outram-park-fork-coolprop, tampines-steam-tables, outram-foam-basic-lib and chem-eng. Helium properties already exist in outram-park-fork-coolprop (full Helmholtz EOS plus real NIST-lineage viscosity and conductivity correlations, tested against tabulated reference states), so the work is exposing them through tampines rather than duplicating them.

The underlying NEED is still real — an HTR-10 primary circuit is a helium loop and nothing in the workspace can currently represent one with prebuilt components. But the fix is a tampines-side gas component layer, not a TUAS enum variant. See the replacement bead.

Note this also affects the framing of the earlier scoping document: docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md lists 'Gas arm in the TUAS material enum' under MISSING with the note that the whole TUAS prebuilt component library cannot be used for a helium loop. That entry should be rewritten to point at tampines when someone next edits that file.

title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
HTR-10: radial pebble conduction, fuel zone to pebble surface
description:
Sets the fuel-to-coolant temperature difference and therefore the Doppler feedback the kinetics sees. Without it the sim cannot report a credible fuel temperature.

SCOPE: radial conduction through the pebble — fuelled inner zone containing the TRISO particles, then the unfuelled graphite shell — to the pebble surface, coupled to the bed via the Wakao particle-to-fluid Nusselt correlation that already exists in TUAS (input_structs.rs:152, already expressed on pebble diameter, which is the right form).

NOTE: GeN-Foam has a pebble routine that was deliberately NOT ported; the appbuilder crate says so explicitly. Consider whether porting it is cheaper than writing fresh.

Current fhr_sim_v2 pebble TH does NOT transfer here — it is a single lumped enthalpy control volume for a UO2 pebble with externally supplied heat transfer coefficient and area, defaulting to a constant-heat-capacity heuristic. It is UO2, not a graphite matrix.

Depends on graphite properties.
teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
HTR-10: separate graphite/moderator temperature feedback channel
description:
Central to HTR-10 loss-of-flow behaviour and currently absent — only lumped fuel feedback exists.

SCOPE: carry graphite moderator temperature as its own state with its own reactivity coefficient, distinct from fuel Doppler. In a pebble bed the large graphite mass is exactly what gives the reactor its long thermal time constant and its self-limiting transient response, so lumping it into fuel feedback destroys the physics that makes HTR-10 interesting.

Wire into the existing six-group PRKE in crates/teh-o-prke alongside the fuel Doppler channel.

Required before attempting any loss-of-flow transient — see the sequencing in docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md section 5.
teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
HTR-10: reflector, core barrel and cavity-cooling decay-heat path
description:
THIS IS THE HTR-10 PASSIVE SAFETY CASE and there is no model of it. The scoping doc recommends budgeting for it rather than deferring it indefinitely, because it is the thing that makes the reactor worth simulating.

SCOPE: the heat removal route from bed to reflector to core barrel to reactor pressure vessel to the reactor cavity cooling system, by conduction and radiation, with no forced flow. This is what carries decay heat out during a loss of forced cooling without scram, and it is what the safety demonstration tests actually exercise.

Depends on graphite properties and bed effective conductivity — every temperature in this path is set by those two closures.

Also requires trustworthy decay heat, which is currently a separate defect — see the decay-heat bead.

title: HTR-10: fix or replace decay heat — currently self-flagged as suspect
description:
crates/teh-o-prke/src/decay_heat.rs:12 carries the original author own comment doubting its correctness on unit grounds. It is also not currently wired into htgr_sim_v1 at all.

SCOPE: verify the existing implementation against a standard decay-heat curve, fix or replace it, and wire it into the simulator. An ANS-5.1-form decay-heat standard curve with open published coefficients is the natural reference.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE: the entire passive safety case is a decay-heat removal argument. A loss-of-forced-cooling transient computed with a wrong decay-heat source is meaningless no matter how good the conduction model is.

Record the verification numbers and the reference curve in the test doc comment per the V&V rule. Related: op-7rf covers a decay-heat sign error in the melcor work — check whether the same error class is present here.

title: HTR-10: helical-coil once-through steam generator with sliding steam pressure
description:
HTR-10 uses a helical-coil once-through modular steam generator with helium on the shell side. The current secondary is a working and tested Rankine cycle but with hard-fixed live steam pressure, so there is no sliding-pressure or drum dynamics.

SCOPE: three-zone moving-boundary once-through SG (subcooled, evaporating, superheated) with helical-coil heat-transfer and pressure-drop correlations, plus SG inventory so that steam pressure becomes a computed variable rather than a constant.

REUSE: the LMTD and NTU algebra already exists in crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs. The zone tracking and the helical correlations do not.

This is the real remaining content of the existing bead op-wqk.9.3 — the other defects that bead lists (simplified IHX duty, fixed secondary mass flow, no real turbine expansion, no condenser balance) are recorded in the scoping doc as ALREADY FIXED AND TESTED. Only fixed steam pressure remains true.

title: outram-park-fork-coolprop — CoolProp thermophysical properties (Rust translation)
description: New workspace crate: a pure-Rust translation of CoolProp (https://github.com/CoolProp/CoolProp, MIT, C++ thermophysical property library — Helmholtz-energy-explicit EOS backend for ~120 pure/pseudo-pure fluids + mixtures, plus incompressibles and humid air). Named with the outram-park-fork- prefix from the start (external-project fork, per the trademark-compliance convention op-ahi). Two hard design constraints from the user: (1) enum dispatch, NOT trait objects, for backend/fluid selection (matches the workspace no-trait-objects rule); (2) hardcode the fluid/EOS data as Rust code -- NO runtime JSON or other file reads (matches njoy's embedded-data philosophy + the workspace static-navigability goal). Verification uses the rfluids crate (https://github.com/portyanikhin/rfluids, a Rust interface to CoolProp) as a DEV-dependency oracle. Book-keeping only; not started.

notes.content:
Crate initiated 2026-07-08: outram-park-fork-coolprop (MIT, workspace member). CoolProp cloned into gitignored reference/. First vertical slice done + verified: Helmholtz engine (Power+Gaussian residual + Lead/LogTau/PlanckEinstein ideal, all derivs), (T,rho) property eval, Water (IAPWS-95) hardcoded (3KB via dev/gen_fluid.py codegen). Water pressure reproduces CoolProp triple-line 611.65 Pa to ~1e-4 at sat liquid+vapor (tests/water_reference.rs). Committed crate 64KB (reference/ 58MB gitignored).
Helium added 2026-07-08 -- verifies to machine precision at its critical point (no non-analytic term). Confirms the Power+Gaussian+ideal engine is exact; Water's ~1e-4 residual is purely the pending non-analytic term (op-kbc.6).

title: Design: enum dispatch for backends/fluids (no trait objects)
description: Per workspace rule + user requirement: model CoolProp's AbstractState/backend polymorphism (HelmholtzEOSMixtureBackend, IncompressibleBackend, HumidAir, ...) and the fluid set as Rust ENUMS with match-based dispatch -- no Box<dyn Trait>/&dyn. Traits may still enforce a per-backend method contract at compile time, just not for runtime dispatch. Exhaustive matches make adding a fluid/backend a compile error until handled.

title: Per-fluid reference tests for the CoolProp fork beyond the 9 pinned
description: All 137 fluids are wired into Fluid + covered by the critical-point smoke test (tests/all_fluids_smoke.rs). Nine have proper reference-state V&V (water/helium/term_types). Add per-fluid triple-line / reference-state checks against CoolProp's tabulated STATES (or rfluids oracle, op-kbc.3) for more fluids, prioritising FHR/working fluids.

title: Wire vendored openfoam_algorithms in coolprop to the CoolProp EOS + rename to OPCP
description: openfoam_algorithms/ was copied verbatim from tampines-steam-tables into outram-park-fork-coolprop (uom-only, no openfoam-basic-lib dep). Follow-ups: (1) rename TampinesSteamArray -> OPCP-prefixed; (2) replace its placeholder rho=psi*p correct_thermo with the CoolProp EOS via OPCPFluidSingleCV / flash (state_ph per cell); (3) once wired, drop the module-level #![allow(dead_code)]/unused_imports on the vendored tree; (4) OPCPFluidSingleCV + flashes are single-phase only (no saturation/VLE) — two-phase needs a dome solver (see op-kbc.7).

notes.content:
2026-07-08: deleted the other vendored solvers (driftFluxFoam, simplefoam, chtMultiRegionTwoPhaseEulerFoam) at user request — only the EOS-wired rhoPimpleFoam solver + shared openfoam_source remain. Remaining: single-phase only (no VLE), no transport (mu/alphaEff) from EOS, and openfoam_source still has unused primitives (dead_code allow stays until rhoPimpleFoam exercises them).
Scaffolded 2026-07-10: added OPCPFluidArray::correct_transport(&mut self) stub (src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs) as the EOS-transport wiring hook — documented no-op (#[allow(dead_code)], not yet called from step). Note: the TampinesSteamArray->OPCPFluidArray rename and the rho=psi*p->EOS correct_thermo replacement are ALREADY done; remaining = add mu/alphaEff VolScalarFields + fill from transport::viscosity/conductivity + feed diffusion terms, then drop the vendored dead_code allows.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-10: OPCPFluidArray::correct_transport() now populates mu/alpha_h per-cell from crate::transport::viscosity/conductivity (falls back to previous value on None, matching correct_thermo's convergence-failure handling); wired into step() right after correct_thermo(). mu/alpha_h fields already existed and were already consumed by the momentum/energy diffusion terms -- this was the last missing piece. Verified: tests/rhoPimpleFoam correct_transport_updates_mu_and_alpha_h_from_eos test. Bead can be closed.

title: Port CoolProp HumidAir (HAPropsSI) — uom + string APIs
description: Port HumidAirProp.cpp: virial coeffs (Baa/Caaa/Bww/Cwww/Baw/Caaw/Caww), enhancement factor f(T,p), psychrometric outputs (W, RH, wet-bulb, dew point, moist-air h/s/rho per kg dry air), inverse solves. Expose both a uom-typed HumidAir API and an HAPropsSI-style string function. Verify vs ASHRAE psychrometric points.

notes.content:
Scaffolded 2026-07-10 (src/humid_air/): mod.rs = HumidAirParam enum + HumidAirState + HumidAirError + ha_props(output,in1,in2,in3) (typed HAPropsSI) + solve_state dispatcher; virials.rs = B_aa/B_ww/B_aw + C_aaa/C_www/C_aaw/C_aww stubs; saturation.rs = p_ws/enhancement_factor/henry_constant stubs. All todo!(). Wired into lib.rs (pub mod humid_air), not in prelude. Builds; existing tests green.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-10 (not just scaffolded): humid_air module ported from CoolProp HumidAirProp.cpp -- virials (literal RP-1485 polynomial fits, B_aa/B_ww/C_aaa/C_www/B_aw/C_aaw/C_aww), enhancement factor secant solve, molar volume secant solve, ideal-gas enthalpy (simplified polynomial correlations). ha_props supports (T,p,W)/(T,p,R) input triples -> W/R/psi_w/H/V/p_w outputs. Verified vs ASHRAE psychrometric c_p/v to <0.1% (tests/humid_air_reference.rs). Found+fixed a real bug during verification: c_aaw was missing a /rhobarstar^2=1e6 factor (CoolProp source has TWO separate /1e6 divisions for that specific correlation, unlike its sibling c_aww), which had made the third-virial correction 4 orders of magnitude too large (5.5% V error before fix, <0.1% after). NOT implemented: entropy (needs CoolProp's ideal-gas reference-state offset calibration), wet-bulb/dew-point (need Brent solves). Remains open for those.
Wet-bulb + dew-point IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-13 (entropy remains open).

dew_point_temperature: ported CoolProp's DewpointTemperature secant solve
almost verbatim, seeded via this crate's own vle::saturation_temperature
(IAPWS-95) in place of IF97 Tsat97. Verified: T=30C/RH=50% -> Tdp=18.451C
(matches the well-known ~18.4C psychrometric-chart value).

wet_bulb_temperature: ported CoolProp's WetBulbSolver energy-balance
residual (LHS-RHS), root-found by bisection on [T_dp, T] instead of
CoolProp's Brent-with-fallback-bracket logic -- T_wb always lies in
[T_dp, T] (standard psychrometric fact), which sidesteps needing
CoolProp's own T_sat-adjacent bracket-clamping special case entirely
(its upstream comments cite real historical bugs #2255/#2690 about that).

Caught and fixed a real bug during verification: the first implementation
evaluated liquid water's enthalpy via flash::state_pt, which only reaches
the vapour/supercritical branch (documented in its own doc comment) --
wrong branch for the subcooled liquid water present at a typical T_wb. It
silently returned a nonsense enthalpy (~-4.2e22 J/kg for liquid water at
20C/1atm) instead of erroring. Fixed by using the saturated-liquid density
at T_wb (vle::saturation_at_temperature) instead, since liquid enthalpy is
only weakly pressure-dependent -- reuses the same pattern
saturation::vbar_ws already relies on elsewhere in this module.

Verified in tests/humid_air_reference.rs: (1) exact saturation identity
T_dp=T_wb=T at R=1 (rigorous, not approximate); (2) cross-check against
Stull (2011) J.Appl.Meteor.Climatol. 50:2267-2269's independent empirical
wet-bulb formula, <0.5C (30C/50%RH: 22.00C vs Stull 22.30C; 25C/60%RH:
19.47C vs Stull 19.50C). All 6 tests in that file pass; full crate suite
(240+ tests across all files) still passes; docs/api.md regenerated.

Remaining: entropy S still needs the ideal-gas reference-state offset
calibration (separate porting effort); T_wb/T_dp still output-only, not
yet supported as input keys.
Entropy S + T_wb/T_dp as input keys IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-13.

T_wb/T_dp as inputs: psi_w_from_dew_point (exact, non-iterative -- the dew
point IS the definition) and psi_w_from_wet_bulb (bisection parameterised
by trial dew point, reusing the already-verified forward wet_bulb_temperature
as the inner black-box). Needed a targeted fix for the exact-saturation
edge case (T_wb=T at R=1): the general bisection bracket degenerates there,
and the forward solve's own secant noise (~1e-7 K) can land T_wb on either
side of T, tripping an over-tight 1e-9 K bounds check. Fixed with a direct
psi_w = psi_ws(T,p) short-circuit + loosened bounds tolerance to 1e-4 K.
Verified via round-trip (T,p,R)->T_dp/T_wb->(T,p,T_dp/T_wb)->R, <1e-4,
including the R=1 edge case.

Entropy: NOT a port of CoolProp's own ensure_ref_offsets/calc_ideal_gas_alpha0
machinery (which needs the real ideal-gas Helmholtz term + a historical
multi-point calibration) -- CoolProp's own C++ literally prints "Not
implemented" for entropy in the simplified-polynomial-enthalpy branch this
crate already uses for H, so there's no CoolProp reference implementation
to port in this configuration at all. Instead: derived via Gibbs' theorem
(pure-component ideal-gas entropies at the mixture's total T,p, Cp(T) from
the SAME polynomials already verified for H) + the standard virial/mixing
corrections, anchored to an explicit ASHRAE zero-point convention (dry air
S=0 at 0C/1atm; water's constant derived via Clausius-Clapeyron from H's
own existing 0C anchor, confirmed consistent: h_w(0C)=2501 kJ/kg matches
the known latent heat of vaporization to 3 figures, now a permanent unit
test in mod.rs).

Caught a real bug during verification: first version used dry air's own
virial-corrected molar volume (+R*ln(v_a/v_a0)) mirroring CoolProp's own
volume-based formula -- but CoolProp's version evaluates the REAL ideal-gas
Helmholtz term there (density-native), while this port integrates Cp (the
CONSTANT-PRESSURE heat capacity), so the volume form silently smuggled in
a second, spurious T-dependence (v_a is proportional to T at fixed p),
breaking dS/dT=Cp/T by ~28% at 25C. Fixed by using -R*ln(p/p0) (total
pressure, Gibbs' theorem) for both air and water instead.

Verified: dS/dT=Cp/T (rigorous, model-independent thermodynamic identity)
holds to 7e-4 to 1.2e-3 across T=1-40C, W=0-0.02 kg/kg -- small, smooth,
and of the same order as the virial correction's own size (consistent with
a residual virial-cross-term path-dependence artifact, not a remaining bug).
CAVEAT, documented in the module doc: S's absolute value is NOT verified
against CoolProp or an external table (different reference-state convention
than CoolProp's own, and H's own mixture value already has a known ~6.6
kJ/kg ASHRAE offset that S likely inherits) -- only the temperature
dependence is rigorously verified. Full crate suite (241+ lib tests, 10 in
humid_air_reference.rs) passes; docs/api.md regenerated.

Remaining open in this bead: absolute-value cross-check for S against a
real external reference, if/when op-kbc.3 (rfluids oracle) lands.

title: Port CoolProp mixtures (multi-fluid Helmholtz + departure)
description: Scaffolded 2026-07-10 (src/mixtures/): Mixture{components,mole_fractions} + MixtureState + reducing.rs (Lorentz-Berthelot + binary beta/gamma) + departure.rs (departure-function terms) + binary_pairs.rs (interaction-parameter table), all todo!(). CoolProp HelmholtzEOSMixtureBackend: alpha_r = sum x_i*alpha_r,i(delta,tau) + departure; reducing T_r(x)/rho_r(x). Remaining: port binary interaction params + departure functions from reference/CoolProp/dev/mixtures, implement reducing + departure eval and multi-fluid (T,rho) state, then VLE/flash.

notes.content: IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-10 (all 840 portable pairs, not just N2-O2): wrote dev/gen_mixture.py + dev/regen_mixture_all.py. Fluid-name resolution by CAS number (mixture_binary_pairs.json uses REFPROP short names like CYCLOHEX, not canonical CoolProp names). Implemented all 3 real departure-function forms for real (Power/GergExponential/Gaussian, ported from CoolProp's ResidualHelmholtzGeneralizedExponential::add_{Power,GERG2008Gaussian,Gaussian} in Helmholtz.h), verified each against finite-difference self-consistency. Discovered the Npower/leading-power-block split in CoolProp's own departure functions is unnecessary to replicate since GergExponential/Gaussian both degenerate exactly to pure power when eta=beta=0 (true for 100% of the surveyed data) -- simplified codegen accordingly. Split binary_pairs.rs into a binary_pairs/ dir (5 generated data_N.rs chunks + hand-maintained mod.rs) to stay under the 1000-line file-size cap (840 pairs would have been 1738 lines in one file). Handled 6 refrigerant-blend pairs (R32/R134a etc) that use xi/zeta instead of betaT/gammaT via CoolProp's LemmonAirHFCReducingFunction::convert_to_GERG formula. 48 of 888 pairs skipped (component outside the 137 ported pure fluids, e.g. R1216, isooctane). Verified: tests/mixture_nitrogen_oxygen.rs (unchanged), new tests/mixture_departure_function.rs (R32-R125, a real F=1.0 departure function, part of R410A -- confirms departure contribution is non-negligible + physical sanity), new tests/all_binary_pairs_smoke.rs (all 840 pairs at a dilute supercritical state). No flash/VLE (matches original scaffold scope). Bead can be closed.

title: General corresponding-states transport (Chung/ECS/rhosr-CS)
description: Scaffolded 2026-07-10 (src/transport_corresponding_states.rs): CorrStatesModel enum {Chung, Ecs, RhosrCs} + corresponding_states_viscosity(fluid,t,rho)->Option<f64> stub (returns None). Closes the ~6-fluid viscosity gap (cyclopentane, isopentane, ethylbenzene, R1234yf, R1234ze(E), R152A) that currently return None. Remaining: implement Chung (1988), extended-corresponding-states (ECS), and rho*sr corresponding-states; then wire into transport::ViscosityModel + Fluid::transport().

notes.content: PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-10: Chung (1988) viscosity fully ported into transport.rs (ViscosityModel::Chung variant + chung_viscosity fn) and wired via dev/gen_fluid.py codegen for the 2 fluids CoolProp actually assigns Chung to (Cyclopentane, Isopentane -- confirmed by inspecting their JSON TRANSPORT.viscosity.type). Verified vs gas-phase viscosity ballpark (tests/chung_viscosity.rs). Investigated the other 4 fluids in the original 'Chung/ECS/rhosr-CS ~6 fluids' framing: EthylBenzene actually uses ECS (reference fluid = Propane), R1234yf/R1234ze(E) use rhosr-CS+ECS fallback, R152A uses rhosr-CS+None. title: Extend OPCPFluidArray with TUAS-FluidArray-like interface (lateral coupling, heat source, geometry, flow bookkeeping)
description:
Give OPCPFluidArray (rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs) a subset of tuas_boussinesq_solver's
FluidArray interface, so a future TAMPINES Pipe component can enum-dispatch
between a TUAS backend and a coolprop backend interchangeably. Scope
(confirmed with user via plan-mode session 2026-07-13, see
outram-park-dt-plan.md at workspace root and the full planning-tool record):

- New fields: lateral_adjacent_array_temperature_vector/conductance_vector
  (Vec<Vec<T>>, not Array1 -- coolprop has no ndarray dep), q_vector/
  q_fraction_vector (heat source), wetted_perimeter, incline_angle,
  mass_flowrate, pressure_loss, internal_pressure_source.
- Simplified vs TUAS: no NusseltCorrelation or DimensionlessDarcyLossCorrelations
  port -- caller supplies conductance/pressure-loss values directly.
- Lateral coupling + heat source wired into step()'s energy equation now
  (one-line addition to the existing explicit source-term loop, alongside
  conv_he/dp_dt). Geometry/flow-bookkeeping fields stay pure bookkeeping,
  not read by step() (matches TUAS itself).
- New error type OPCPFluidArrayError::LengthMismatch (own type, not a
  MeshError reuse), properly re-exported from lib.rs (fixes the existing
  MeshError-not-exported gap in the same pass).
- New file rhoPimpleFoam/lateral_coupling.rs (mirrors TUAS's own
  directory-per-concern split for this exact feature) -- 13 new methods,
  7 new tests.
- set_temperature_vector needs a real per-cell (p,T) flash + write
  he/rho/t/psi together, NOT a plain t field write (he is the actual PIMPLE
  state variable; a plain t write would be silently undone by the next
  correct_thermo() call).

This is Part 1 of a 3-part plan (Part 2: new tampines crate, Part 3: new
outram-park-digital-twin-gui crate) -- this bead covers Part 1 only.

notes.content: Done 2026-07-13: lateral_coupling.rs created (13 methods, 7 tests), new() field initializers added, step() wires lateral conductance + heat source into the energy-equation source term (extensive Watts, matching conv_he/dp_dt units), clear_vectors() called at end of step(). OPCPFluidArrayError re-exported from lib.rs. Test fix: test fluid changed from Water (liquid at 300K/1bar -- unreachable by the vapor-branch flash, silently no-ops every correct_thermo/state_pt call) to Nitrogen (matches existing passing tests' fluid choice). Also found t/rho lag he by one outer-corrector iteration in this PIMPLE solver -- tests call correct_thermo() after step() to sync t before reading temperature. Verified: cargo build --release clean, cargo test --release 248 lib tests passed (241 existing + 7 new) + all integration tests green, cargo check --workspace --lib --tests --release clean (no downstream breakage).

title: coolprop incompressibles: port T_freeze, saturation_pressure, entropy & internal energy
description: Audit (2026-07-16) found these dropped at port time although the upstream coeffs sit unused in the JSON: T_freeze (49 fluids, the brine/glycol families), saturation_pressure/TminPsat (38 fluids), and smass/umass are not computed. Re-port is mechanical (coeffs already in dev/incompressible_liquids/json).
acceptance_criteria: T_freeze() and psat() fields+methods populated for the fluids that carry upstream coeffs; smass/umass computed from the existing cp polynomial; verification test against a known brine freeze point and an oil vapor-pressure value.

title: Hardcode fluid/EOS data as Rust code -- no runtime JSON/file reads
description: CoolProp reads fluid EOS coefficients + ancillary equations from JSON (bundled/compiled). This fork hardcodes that data as Rust constants/data structures (const arrays / typed structs), so there is NO runtime file or JSON parsing and the data is rust-analyzer-navigable. Likely a codegen step (script that reads CoolProp's JSON once at authoring time and emits Rust source) rather than hand-transcription -- decide codegen vs hand-port when starting. Mirrors njoy's embedded-data-blob approach.

title: coolprop fluids: port surface tension correlations + data
description: Audit found surface tension entirely absent (upstream ships it for ~109/137 fluids). No fork fluid file has sigma data and no public surface_tension() exists.
acceptance_criteria: surface_tension(Fluid,T) implemented with per-fluid coeffs generated from CoolProp JSON; verified against water surface tension (IAPWS) and 1-2 other fluids with documented accuracy bounds.

title: coolprop fluids: port melting/sublimation lines
description: Audit found melting-line/sublimation data absent (upstream has melting_line for ~30/137). Niche for TH work but a whole capability; enables solid-boundary bounding.
acceptance_criteria: melting_line / sublimation_line data + evaluator for the fluids upstream provides; verified against a reference melting point (e.g. water/CO2).

title: coolprop mixtures: flash/VLE + mixture derivatives (phase equilibrium)
description: LARGE follow-up. Mixtures are currently EVALUATION-ONLY: 840/888 binary pairs + all 40 departure functions ported and self-consistent, but there is NO flash/VLE, no fugacity coefficient, no dArdxj / n.dAdni (MixtureDerivatives), which upstream implements in ~13.6k lines (Flash/VLE/PhaseEnvelope). Needs its own focused, verified effort; do NOT one-shot autonomously. Prereq: MixtureDerivatives before any flash.
acceptance_criteria: MixtureDerivatives (fugacity, composition derivatives) implemented + FD-verified; PT/PH/PQ mixture flash + bubble/dew; validated against GERG-2008 tabulated mixture densities/enthalpies.

title: coolprop mixtures: predefined mixtures + composition normalization hygiene
description: Audit: no predefined mixtures (Air, natural-gas/refrigerant blends) so users hand-build composition arrays; Mixture::new has a TODO and does not assert sum(x)~1 (silently trusts caller).
acceptance_criteria: A handful of predefined mixtures (at least Air) exposed; Mixture::new validates/normalizes composition or documents the caller contract; test for Air reproducing a reference property.

title: coolprop HumidAir: complete derivative family, transport, ice branch, more inversions
description: Extends op-kbc.14. Audit: only ~11/25 HAPropsSI output keys and a rigid (T,p,X)-only input grid. Missing: cp/cp_ha, cv/cv_ha, speed_of_sound, isentropic_exponent, Z, internal energy U/Uha, humid-air-basis variants (Vha/Hha/Sha/Uha); transport mu and k; the ice/sublimation branch below 273.16 K; and all inversions where T is unknown or an energy/state variable (H,S,V,U) is an input. Also: absolute-entropy reference not cross-checked vs CoolProp.
acceptance_criteria: cp/cv/Z/U + humid-air-basis variants added and verified vs ASHRAE/CoolProp; mu & k added; ice branch ported; at least the (W,R,P) and energy-input-solve-for-T inversions supported; entropy reference reconciled.

title: coolprop HumidAir: cp/cv/Z/U + humid-air-basis variants (Vha/Hha/Sha/Uha)
Verification: rfluids as dev-dependency (CoolProp reference oracle)
description: Add rfluids (https://github.com/portyanikhin/rfluids -- Rust interface to CoolProp, likely FFI to the CoolProp shared lib) as a DEV-dependency and write V&V tests comparing this fork's properties against rfluids/CoolProp reference values across the ported fluids + state points (methodology + measured results per the workspace V&V rule). NOTE: rfluids may require the CoolProp native lib / build toolchain on the test host -- confirm its build requirements and licensing (CoolProp is MIT). Dev-dep only, so it does not affect the shipped crate.

title: Scope decision: which CoolProp backend + fluid subset to port first
description: CoolProp is large. Suggested first slice: the HEOS (Helmholtz-energy-explicit) backend for a handful of pure fluids -- start with Water (CoolProp's IAPWS-95, which cross-checks the user's tampines-steam-tables IAPWS-IF97), then common refrigerants / working fluids relevant to the FHR + multiphase work (e.g. the salts/coolants of interest). Defer incompressible backend, humid air (HAPropsSI), mixtures, and the tabulated TTSE/bicubic backends. User to confirm the target fluid list + backend order before starting.

title: License + attribution: CoolProp is MIT
description: CoolProp is MIT-licensed. Decide this fork's license (MIT-derivative can be kept MIT or relicensed; most OUTRAM PARK crates are GPL-3.0, chem-eng is Apache-2.0) and ship a NOTICE crediting CoolProp + the original authors, plus a TRADEMARKS.md consistent with the other forks. Also confirm rfluids' license (dev-dep).

notes.content: SUPERSEDED 2026-07-16: license corrected MIT -> GPL-3.0-only. The crate ships GPL-3.0 OpenFOAM-derived code (src/openfoam_algorithms/openfoam_source/*), which is infective, so MIT was legally incorrect for the shipped artifact. Cargo.toml now license.workspace=true (GPL-3.0-only); LICENSE (GPL-3.0) added; CoolProp MIT provenance retained in-tree (NOTICE). Crate PUBLISHED to crates.io as v0.1.0 with an explicit 'no human V&V yet' caveat. rfluids/CoolProp-oracle validation remains open under op-kbc.3.

title: outram-mc-libs: 2 pre-existing doctest failures in geometry::surface::torus_distance
description:
`cargo test --release -p outram-mc-libs --doc` fails 2 of 12 doctests:

  test crates/outram-mc-libs/src/geometry/surface.rs - geometry::surface::torus_distance (line 824) ... FAILED
  test crates/outram-mc-libs/src/geometry/surface.rs - geometry::surface::torus_distance (line 829) ... FAILED

CAUSE: the doc comment on `torus_distance` writes its quartic derivation as 4-space-indented prose lines, e.g.

    ///     rho^2(t) + a^2 - b^2 + (b^2/c^2)*ax^2(t)  =  2a*R_perp(t)
    ///     F(t) = G(t)^2 - 4a^2*rho^2(t) = 0.

A 4-space indent inside a /// block is a Markdown indented code block, so rustdoc compiles those math lines as Rust doctests and they fail to parse. They are documentation, not code.

FIX: wrap the derivation in a ```text fence (or ```ignore), matching how the rest of the crate writes non-Rust display math.

Confirmed PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to that change — reproduced on develop with the op-rbo edits stashed (baseline: 9 passed / 2 failed; with the op-rbo fix: 10 passed / 2 failed, the extra pass being a new init_seed doctest). Not fixed there to keep that change scoped to the RNG.

title: HTR-10 meshing: tet-dual polyMesh of the core, shared by neutronics and TH, with a measured quality report
description:
Parent: op-841p. Meshing sits UPSTREAM of rung 3 - GeN-Foam cannot run without a mesh - so it is part of the pipeline, not beside it.

MAINTAINER DECISIONS: (1) CLI tools first, not a GUI. (2) ONE tet-dual mesh used for BOTH neutronics and thermal hydraulics, not two. (3) GUI later via op-hzs.53.

START FROM WHAT EXISTS (verified 2026-08-11):
- crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/pipeline.rs:312 surface_to_tet_dual_mesh(points, tris, opts) -> Result<(VolumeMesh, TetDualReport), String>. IMPLEMENTED, body is run_pipeline at :392. Seven stages (carve, snap, tetrahedralize, Delaunay flip, dual, Laplacian smooth, boundary layers), each optional stage gated by acceptable() at :243 with graceful fallback via keep_if_ok at :253. TetDualReport at :217 already carries max_non_orthogonality_deg, max_skewness, n_negative_volume_cells. Multipatch variant at :379 with a documented limitation at :346-353 (boundary layers grow on the whole boundary, not per patch).
- Quality metrics implemented at crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/checks.rs:78 (check_quality): non-orthogonality :95-97, skewness :99-106, aspect ratio :130, OpenFOAM thresholds in is_good() at :70.
- CLI tools that generate or convert a mesh TODAY: blockMesh, ideasUnvToFoam, polyDualMesh in crates/outram-foam-cli/src/bin/. outram-foam-mesh has NO binaries - it is a pure library (block_mesh.rs:490, snappy_hex_mesh.rs:186, poly_dual_mesh.rs:779, driver.rs:345 mesh_from_surface with write_case at :306, mesh_quality.rs:274 assess_quality).

INPUTS: HTR-10 core geometry - 180 cm diameter, 197 cm average height, 100 cm side reflector including carbon bricks, the conus and discharge tube, plus 10 control-rod borings (13 cm at r = 102.1 cm), 7 absorber-ball, 3 irradiation, and 20 helium channels (8 cm at r = 144.6 cm). CAUTION: the axial build is NOT fully specified in the open text - see the geometry bead.

OUTPUTS: a polyMesh consumed by GeN-Foam, plus a quality report. Non-orthogonality and skewness MUST be measured and reported, and the mesh plus its generation parameters go in the run manifest - a result on an unrecorded mesh is not reproducible.

WHY ONE MESH: it avoids cross-mesh mapping error at the coupling seam. op-p6p.8 (genfoam multiRegion cross-mesh coupling) exists precisely for the case where meshes DO differ, so the shared-mesh choice is a deliberate simplification that sidesteps it. OPEN QUESTION for the maintainer: neutronics wants resolution at the core/reflector interface and rod channels, TH wants it at the near-wall porosity rise and the axial thermal gradient. On a shared mesh the union must be resolved, which costs cells the coarser physics does not need.

title: Derive by hand: rarefied-tail density taper for HybridAllMach stability (for paper methods)
description: By-hand analytical derivation/justification of the rarefied-tail density taper that stabilised the full 600ms hybrid run (op-21g.15.7). Author's own derivation for the paper methods (Phase II row C of the Edwards debug timeline table, index.tex). Derive: (1) analytically why the explicit KNP correction is ill-conditioned as rho -> 0 -- the cell diagonal rho_cont*V/dt collapses, so a fixed explicit flux correction produces an unbounded enthalpy update (the stability criterion motivating the taper); show how a rarefied cell enthalpy diverges and trips the (p,h) 273.15K validity edge; (2) justify the taper g(rho) = clamp((rho-50)/(100-50),0,1) -- below 50 kg/m3 there is no flashing shock left to capture so switching KNP off costs no accuracy, and the taper is inert above 100 kg/m3 so it does not perturb the validated plateau (bit-identical ringing reduction and plateau).
acceptance_criteria: Written derivation of the ill-conditioning stability criterion + [50,100] kg/m3 taper justification, ready for paper methods.

title: outram-mc: one unreproduced test failure under concurrent cargo test load
description:
Recorded 2026-08-11 so it is not lost. NOT diagnosed — I could not name the failing test, and I am not guessing at a cause.

WHAT HAPPENED: `cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --tests --release` exited non-zero with

That run was executing CONCURRENTLY with `cargo test -p njoy-outram-park-fork --lib --tests --release` in a separate process, both started at the same moment on the same machine.

WHY THE NAME IS MISSING: the invocation was piped through `grep -E '^(test result:|failures:|error|...)'`, which filtered out the per-test FAILED line before it was written to the log. My mistake in the harness, not the test's.

DID NOT REPRODUCE. Three subsequent runs with nothing else building:
- `cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --release` -> 212 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored (twice)
- `cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --tests --release` -> 212 + 5 + 30 + 7 = 254 passed, 0 failed

PLAUSIBLE BUT UNPROVEN: the lib target holds the GPU tests (`gpu::surface_distance`, `gpu::xs_interp`, `gpu::batched_flight`, `gpu::union_grid`), and this host has a single NVIDIA RTX 3050. A second heavy build competing for CPU and memory, or two processes contending for the one GPU device, is the obvious suspect. But njoy's suite has no GPU tests, so a pure GPU-contention story is not clean, and a plain build-lock/CPU-starvation timeout is equally consistent with the evidence. Do not write either into a doc as the cause.

NEXT STEP IF IT RECURS: re-run WITHOUT a grep filter, capture the full log, and get the failing test name. Then decide whether the GPU tests need serialising (a test-level mutex or a `--test-threads` carve-out for the gpu module only — NOT for the whole suite, per the workspace rule against serialising slow suites).

title: tampines components/: add gas-phase variants so gas_phase components slot into the Pipe/Pump component layer
description:
tampines::gas_phase landed 2026-08-11 (op-jyyp.12) with three working component models -- GasDuct (Churchill friction + Gnielinski/Dittus-Boelter heat transfer, low-Mach compressible), KtaBed (KTA 3102.3 packed-bed pressure drop) and Circulator (idealised fixed-rise/fixed-ratio compression). They are deliberately NOT wired into src/components/, which bead op-ql8 owns.

Interface notes for whoever does that wiring:

1. PipeBackend (components/pipe.rs) is an enum over stateful fluid ARRAYS (SinglePhaseFluidArray, CompressibleFluidArray, TampinesSteamArray, InsulatedFluidComponent). gas_phase::GasDuct is a different shape: it is stateless plain-data geometry plus a one-shot steady solve(mass_flow, T_in, p_in, boundary) -> GasDuctResult. It is NOT a drop-in PipeBackend variant.
   Suggested resolution: add a separate `SteadyGas(GasDuct)` variant, and accept that Pipe's methods split into a transient path (the array backends) and a steady path (this one), rather than forcing GasDuct to carry cell state it does not have.

2. KtaBed has no components/ counterpart at all -- a porous/packed-bed component struct would be new. It composes cleanly with crate::pebble_bed::zbs::ZbsBed (friction side + conduction side of the same bed).

3. Circulator is the gas analogue of components::Pump. Pump is currently a NotYetImplemented wrapper, so the cleanest move is probably a `PumpBackend` enum with a `GasCirculator(Circulator)` variant, mirroring PipeBackend.

4. All three take/return uom types and use crate::TampinesError, so error and unit conventions already match components/.

5. gas_phase exposes two public uom aliases -- MassFlux (kg/(m^2 s)) and PressureGradient (Pa/m) -- because uom ships no named types for those dimensions. If components/ needs them, re-export rather than redefining; note outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/kta.rs independently defines identical aliases.

Blocked on op-ql8 finishing the NotYetImplemented wrapper pass.

title: outram-mc: ThermalScattering handles incoherent-inelastic only — no elastic channel, so graphite/ZrH moderation is wrong
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-11 by code inspection.

STATE: crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/thermal.rs is explicit at lines 24-26: 'Scope. Only the incoherent-*inelastic* channel — the one H-in-H2O needs (light water has no thermal elastic). Coherent / incoherent-elastic bound scattering (graphite, ZrH) is deliberately not wired here yet.'

The struct holds only xs_e/xs_sigma (sigma_inel) and emit_tables. Nuclide::with_thermal_scattering (src/material/nuclide.rs:221) attaches one ThermalScattering, and nuclide.rs:331-339 REPLACES the free-gas elastic channel with sigma_inel below the cutoff. For a scatterer whose thermal elastic is non-zero that substitution is doubly wrong: it drops the dominant channel AND removes the free-gas stand-in for it.

WHY IT MATTERS (HTR-10 critical path): for graphite at 0.0253 eV, measured through the njoy port against ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-crystalline-graphite (MAT=30): sigma_coh_el = 4.55 b, sigma_inel = 0.49 b. Wiring only the inelastic channel would give a graphite pebble ~11% of its true thermal scattering cross section — a materially wrong thermal spectrum and k_eff, and worse than the free-gas treatment it replaces.

WORK: extend ThermalScattering to carry an optional elastic channel (coherent: pre-tabulated sigma_coh_el(E) plus the Bragg (mu, weight) table per incident energy; incoherent: sigma(E,T) plus equiprobable cosines). At a thermal collision, choose elastic vs inelastic in proportion to their cross sections; an elastic scatter keeps E and samples mu from the Bragg weights (lab frame, no CM transform). Mirror OpenMC src/thermal.cpp ThermalData::sample, which does exactly this elastic/inelastic split. Depends on op-u5ju for the njoy-side surface.

SIZE: medium. Mostly plumbing + one sampling branch, but it changes the ThermalScattering shape and the nuclide.rs cross-section substitution, and needs a test.

notes.content:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11 (this session; AI-assisted draft, NOT human-reviewed, NOT committed - coordinator holds the diff).

WHAT LANDED
- crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/thermal.rs: new pub enum ThermalElastic {None, Coherent(CoherentElasticTable), Incoherent(IncoherentElasticTable)} (enum dispatch, no trait objects/Box/lifetimes). ThermalScattering now owns an elastic channel alongside the inelastic one, with elastic_xs(E), total_xs(E) and elastic() accessors. from_endf_file() reads the ENDF tape ONCE and DETECTS the elastic law from the evaluation (MT=2 LTHR=1/3 -> coherent, LTHR=2/3 -> incoherent, absent -> None); its signature is unchanged so every existing caller is source-compatible. NjoyError::NotPorted from a channel constructor is treated as 'this evaluation has no such section'; every other error, notably TemperatureOutOfRange, is propagated rather than silently dropping graphite's dominant channel.
- ThermalScattering::sample() now splits elastic vs inelastic with probability sigma_el/sigma_thermal, mirroring OpenMC src/thermal.cpp:296-302 ThermalData::sample_dist. The coherent branch mirrors src/secondary_thermal.cpp:34-54 CoherentElasticAE::sample (invert the cumulative structure factor, mu = 1 - 2 E_k/E, E_out = E_in).
- COHERENT IS STORED EXACTLY, NOT RESAMPLED. sigma_coh_el(E) is a 1/E sawtooth with 221 discontinuities for graphite, so a log-grid resample would smear every Bragg edge. CoherentElasticTable holds the Bragg-edge table itself (221 (E,sigma) pairs, ~3.5 kB - cheaper than the resample AND exact). Incoherent elastic IS resampled (it is smooth); grid sized by measurement at 400 points.
- crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/thermr/scattering.rs: added CoherentElasticScattering::bragg_edge_table() -> Vec<(NeutronEnergy, CrossSection)>, the uom-typed accessor that makes the exact storage possible. Mirrors the OpenMC CoherentElasticXS::bragg_edges()/factors() pair. This is the ONLY njoy-side change; the data/transport boundary is intact (outram-mc still parses no ENDF).
- crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/nuclide.rs: xs_at_energy's thermal substitution now swaps in th.total_xs(e) = sigma_inel + sigma_el, not sigma_inel alone. THIS IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT THIS BEAD NAMED.

MEASURED (ENDF/B-VIII.0, release mode, 2026-08-11; full methodology + results in the module header of crates/outram-mc-libs/tests/thermal_graphite_elastic.rs, 7 tests, all green)
- Graphite MAT 30, 296 K, barn per carbon atom at 0.0253 eV: sigma_coh_el 4.5514, sigma_inel 0.4863, elastic fraction 0.9035. Confirms the ~90 % figure this bead was filed on.
- Exactness: worst relative deviation of the stored Bragg table vs the njoy surface = 7.67e-16 over 21199 points spanning 1e-4 to 4 eV. Bragg cutoff 1.822327e-3 eV (graphite (002)); sigma_el exactly 0.0 below it.
- Nuclide-level, C0 + graphite table vs bare C0, MicroXS::elastic at 0.0253 eV: free-gas 4.9398, bound-new 5.0378, bound-OLD (inel only) 0.4863. The pre-fix path gave graphite 9.8 % of its free-gas scattering; the fixed path gives 102.0 %.

notes.content:
Stagnation inflow BC now EXERCISED AND VERIFIED for the single-phase subcooled steady path, 2026-08-11 (~17:00 SGT). Items 2, 3, 4 of this bead are done; item 1 (land vs hold) stays a maintainer decision.

NEW TEST: reservoir_inlet_reaches_the_bernoulli_limit_in_subcooled_water in crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/tests.rs (+~390 lines incl. V&V doc). Closed form derived from the DISCRETE steady state of the scheme's own momentum balances (not the continuum limit): p0 - p_out = rho u^2/2 + rho F L with Darcy F, giving u = sqrt(2 dp / (rho (1 + f L/D))), friction incorporated (not neglected) via the code's own laminar-64/Re / Blasius closure. Case: p0 1.000 MPa -> p_out 0.980 MPa, T 300 K (~153 K subcooled), L 0.5 m, D 0.1 m, 20 cells, dt 0.5 ms, 3000 steps; all solver knobs at defaults.

MEASURED: closed-form u 6.225884 m/s vs measured steady inlet u 6.225891 m/s -> relative error +1.12e-6 against a 1.0 % tolerance PRE-COMMITTED in the doc comment before the first run (a-priori budget ~0.1 %, gated 10x looser because reference f is evaluated once at (p_out, mu_f)). Frictionless Bernoulli would be 6.334222 m/s; measured sits 1.7102 % below, matching the friction correction. Continuity |mdot_in - mdot_out|/mdot 1.28e-6; steadiness 3.3e-7; max Courant 0.125; alpha = 0 exactly throughout; ~6-7 s wall clock. Strongest evidence: the three pressure terms match INDIVIDUALLY (p[0] 980661.291 predicted vs 980661.29 measured; interior drop 644.376 vs 644.33; outflow face 16.957 vs 16.96), separately confirming the conservative half-cell inlet convection, the half-cell Dirichlet coefficient dt/(rho dx/2), and friction charged over exactly L. No defect found; the non-conservative alternative the BC doc warns about would sit at ~4.48 m/s (-28 %) and nothing near that appears.

DOCS: AxialBoundary::ReservoirInlet public doc now states both standing assumptions (zero inlet drift velocity; infinite non-depleting plenum) plus a V&V status block — doc-comment-only edits to drift_flux.rs, no code/signature/constant changed.

ALSO EXERCISED INDIRECTLY: the Marviken gates (op-ja3t) drive this BC through 897 marched two-phase transients with 0 refused steps.

STILL UNVERIFIED (stated in the test doc and the ReservoirInlet V&V block): two-phase inflow (InflowState::void_fraction and rho_g never exercised, alpha = 0 throughout the direct test), the h0 - u^2/2 static-enthalpy split only probed at 2e-4 relative head, backflow through either boundary, and transient behaviour. upwind_scalar has no direct unit test — it is private to drift_flux and tests.rs is a sibling module, so it needs a pub(super) visibility change first; filed as a follow-up bead (see op tracker, filed today). Note also Blasius is applied at Re ~ 4.1e6, beyond its nominal ~1e5 range — a property of the code under test, reproduced not corrected. Not closing this bead — maintainer decision.

chem-eng: ProportionalController still routes a pure gain through the full first-order machinery
description:
Follow-up from op-fm5 (fixed 2026-08-11). No longer a performance emergency, but still wasteful and still the thing its own doc comment apologises for.

ProportionalController::new (alpha_nightly/controllers/proportional_controller/mod.rs) realises G(s) = K_c as the first-order transfer function (K_c s + K_c)/(s + 1), so a pure multiply goes through a TransferFnFirstOrder, i.e. TWO blocks (FirstOrderStableTransferFnNoZeroes + FirstOrderStableTransferFnForZeroes), three state variables, three exp() calls and the 9-decimal-place input-change guard, every step. Its Default doc at :58 already says 'This is probably overdoing it in terms of computation cost but that is not an issue ... yet ...'.

MEASURED 2026-08-11 (release, AMD Ryzen 5 5600, rustc 1.97.0), after the op-fm5 O(1) rewrite: a bare ProportionalController costs 0.06 us/step, against roughly 1 ns for the multiply it actually represents -- so about 60x overhead, flat. Before the rewrite it was 9.42 us/step. So the fire is out; what is left is tidiness.

PROPOSED: give ProportionalController a direct multiply path (output = K_c * input + offset) and keep the transfer-function representation only where a dead time is actually set, since dead time is the one thing the plain multiply cannot express. Watch out: the current form is NOT exactly a pure gain when a dead time is applied, so check what set_dead_time is expected to do here before simplifying.

Not urgent. Filed so the apology in the doc comment has somewhere to point.

title: kovan-literature: lit import defaults visibility to Open when the source PDF is outside open/ or proprietary/ (staging imports)
description:
Observed 2026-08-11 during the librarian pass, kovan CLI built from workspace at target/release/kovan (08:40 build).

REPRODUCTION (actually run):
./target/release/kovan lit import 'kovan_import/decay heat tobias.pdf' --json-out crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/tobias1980decay.json --markdown-out crates/kovan-literature/generated/markdown/proprietary/tobias1980decay.md

OBSERVED: the summary printed 'visibility: Open' and the JSON was written with visibility Open — even though both --json-out and --markdown-out point into proprietary/ trees. The path-based visibility inference (storage::visibility_from_path per DECISIONS.md) evidently looks only at the SOURCE path (kovan_import/...), which contains neither open/ nor proprietary/, and the fallback default is Open.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the normal workflow (kovan_import/README.md) imports FROM staging, so every proprietary import gets visibility Open by default. That is the expensive failure direction — DECISIONS.md itself says the design goal was 'proprietary material can't be mislabelled open by accident', and this defeats it. The same run also imported an open document correctly, so only the default is wrong.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION: infer visibility from the --json-out destination path when the source path is indeterminate, and/or default to Proprietary (the cheap failure direction) instead of Open, and/or print a loud warning when falling back.

The tobias1980decay.json record was hand-patched to Proprietary the same day; no mislabelled record remains.

notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-11, pending maintainer verification. Maintainer decision: 'for lit import, visibilty should be closed by default. And open if explicitly stated.'

Implemented in crates/kovan-literature/src/lib.rs, storage::visibility_from_path. A document is now Open ONLY when its path contains an explicit open/ component; everything else, including a path with neither marker, is Proprietary.

WHY THE OLD TEST DID NOT CATCH IT: the existing test asserted exactly two cases, open/papers/x.pdf and proprietary/reports/x.pdf. Both pass under the OLD rule and the NEW one, because neither exercises the unmarked path. The defect lived entirely in the case nobody wrote a test for. The replacement test now covers a bare filename, a kovan_import/ staging path, an absolute Downloads path, case-insensitive OPEN/, and a substring trap (openfoam_cases/ must NOT be read as an open marker). 69 lib tests pass.

Note the ORIGINAL doc comment claimed the function existed 'so proprietary material never gets an open label by accident' — the stated intent was right all along and the implementation contradicted it. Worth remembering as a review heuristic: when a doc comment states a safety property, check the code actually delivers it.

chem-eng: step-cost regression tests use wall-clock assertions and flake under load
description:
Observed twice on 2026-08-11. The tests alpha_nightly::stable_transfer_functions::recurrence_tests::pid_step_cost_does_not_grow_with_step_index and its beta_testing sibling assert on measured wall-clock per-step cost. Both failed once and passed on immediate rerun while four other agents were compiling on the same machine.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A USUAL FLAKE. These tests exist to defend the op-fm5 fix — they are the regression guard proving the response vectors no longer grow without bound. A guard that cries wolf gets muted, and the defect it guards against (a plateau at ~28 us/step at dt=0.04, degrading to ~1133 us/step at dt=0.001) is exactly the kind that creeps back in silently.

THE UNDERLYING ISSUE: wall-clock time is not the property under test. The property is that per-step cost is O(1) in the step index, i.e. that internal state does not grow. Wall-clock is a proxy for that, and a poor one on a shared machine.

SUGGESTED FIX: assert on the invariant directly rather than its timing shadow. Assert the internal state SIZE is constant between step 100 and step 100000 — a first-order recurrence keeps a fixed number of coefficients regardless of how many inputs it has seen. That is deterministic, machine-independent, fast, and it fails for the right reason. Note first_order_transfer_fn.rs already gained a state_size() method today (currently dead_code); that is the accessor this needs.

Keep a wall-clock benchmark if it is useful, but make it a benchmark that reports rather than a test that fails.

notes.content:
SUBSTANTIALLY FIXED 2026-08-11 (agent stopped at session end mid-verification; needs a review pass).

The wall-clock flakiness was addressed by changing WHAT is asserted rather than loosening a threshold. The tests now measure a mean-cost window at step 5,000 and again at step 100,000 and assert the RATIO, with a deliberately loose 5x pass criterion. The ratio is machine-independent; the absolute microseconds are not. Measured on AMD Ryzen 5 5600, rustc 1.97.0, release: filtered PID with tau_d = 80.8 s gives 0.279 us/step at both windows, ratio 1.00; a bare P controller 0.105 -> 0.104 us/step, ratio 1.00. Stable across three consecutive runs (32/32 each, ratios 1.00-1.03).

The doc comment now states explicitly that those figures were taken under heavy concurrent build load, which is why they sit above the 0.17 us/step measured on an idle machine — recorded rather than hidden, so a future reader is not confused by the discrepancy. For contrast it also records the pre-0.2.0 behaviour on the same machine: 58.2 us/step at step 1,000 rising to 2329.5 us/step at step 79,000, a ratio of 40 and still climbing.

REMAINING: the agent was stopped with the message 'Let me update the recorded V&V numbers to match the new methodology and re-verify.' The alpha_nightly tier doc comment was verified complete during the session-end sweep; the beta_testing tier was NOT individually inspected. Both files were modified and 32/32 tests pass, so nothing is broken, but the beta tier's recorded numbers should be read against its actual methodology before this bead is closed.

Also still open as originally filed: asserting on internal STATE SIZE rather than timing at all would be strictly better — deterministic, machine-independent, and it fails for the right reason. first_order_transfer_fn.rs has a state_size() method (currently dead_code) which is the accessor for it.

title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
Tutor: rhoPimpleFoam stability issues (teaching doc for OutramFoam/tampines)
description: User wants a step-by-step, teacher-to-student explanation of the rhoPimpleFoam pressure-velocity stability issues discovered 2026-07-14, written as durable documentation in the OutramFoam rhoPimpleFoam solver folder (crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/solvers/rho_pimple_foam/), and referenced from tampines docs. Should walk through, pedagogically: (1) why compressible PISO couples p and U and how the pEqn is assembled from the momentum diagonal (rAU) + laplacian + psi*V/dt compressibility term; (2) the pressure-source clobbering bug -- fvm::laplacian puts the FixedValue-pressure Dirichlet source (coeff*p_bc) into the matrix source, and overwriting it (p_eqn.source = ...) kept the diagonal but dropped the source, silently imposing p_bc=0 and blowing up any fixed-pressure outlet even from equilibrium; the fix is to ADD not overwrite; (3) the phi_hbya boundary write-back for FixedValue velocity patches; (4) stiff-liquid water-hammer: near-incompressible liquid + impulsive inlet -> Joukowsky surge rho*c*du, reflection undershoots to negative absolute pressure -> out of EOS range; why gas (large psi) is well-conditioned but liquid (tiny psi) is stiff; (5) the standard fixes -- OpenFOAM pressureControl pMin/pMax bounding (limit pressure not density for complex EOS), PISO vs SIMPLE vs PIMPLE and under-relaxation, acoustic CFL dt<dx/c, and velocity ramping; (6) BC well-posedness (fixed-velocity inlet + fixed-pressure outlet, inletOutlet for backflow). Cite the OpenFOAM pressureControl source and the rhoSimpleFoam complex-EOS commit. This is the durable pedagogical companion to bead op-21g.12.

title: genfoam: pointKinetics reactivity-feedback + coupling layer (mesh/TH/GEM/FMU/liquid-fuel)

Needs common/timeProfile + neutronics base + multiRegion.

notes.content: Done. Added multi_region/reactivity_feedback.rs: ReactivityFeedback layer turning mesh TH/TM feedback fields (fuel temperature, structure temperature, coolant density) into a scalar Delta-rho via an importance-weighted (volume or phi^2-worth) volume average of per-cell contributions. FeedbackTerm enum (no dyn): Doppler (linear or logarithmic law), Expansion (T_struct), Density (coolant/void, per-fractional-density). Generalises the lumped alpha*(T-Tref) Doppler already in outer_iteration to spatial fields; reduces to it exactly for a uniform field + volume weight. weighted_mean() also collapses TFuel to the feedback point MeshNeutronics uses for XS re-materialization, tying op-p6p.10 to op-p6p.8.4. V&V (release): uniform field -> lumped -3.0e-3; spatial profile negative feedback -3.0e-3; multiterm superposition (Doppler+density cancel to 0) and log-law within 2.7% of linear. NOTE: GEM/control-rod driveline, external neutron source, FMU inputs, and liquid-fuel precursor advection from the full pointKineticNeutronics are NOT ported here (filed as op-p6p.10 follow-ups below).

Core multiRegion ported + verified in-tree (18 tests pass, release): volumetric meshToMesh (mesh_to_mesh.rs), RBF non-conformal path (rbf_mapping.rs, reuses xs::rbf kernel), coupled-feedback assembly MeshHandler=interpolateCouplingFields (coupling_fields.rs), and the Picard outer loop MultiPhysicsSolver enum-dispatched over RegionModel (outer_iteration.rs) driven end-to-end by 0-D point-kinetics <-> lumped-TH. Scaffolded gaps filed as op-p6p.8.1..8.5 (exact polyhedral meshToMesh, deformMesh, dim-reduced RBF, mesh-based RegionModel dispatch, AABB accel). No shared-file edits needed; no new deps. RBF unification into genfoam::common::rbf flagged.
Mesh-based cross-mesh coupling now realised end-to-end (op-p6p.8.4 closed): MeshNeutronics(DiffusionNeutronics)<->MeshThermalHydraulics coupled through MeshHandler/mesh_to_mesh CellVolumeWeight mapping, with the op-p6p.10 ReactivityFeedback layer supplying the Doppler feedback. Power conserved across non-conformal meshes (rel 2.3e-16), negative Doppler feedback verified on the mesh path. Remaining sub-beads: 8.1 exact polyhedral meshToMesh, 8.2 deformMesh/movePoints, 8.3 dim-reduced RBF, 8.5 AABB accel; plus new follow-up for per-cell/dynamic mesh XS feedback (neutronics-subtree API gap). 24 multi_region tests pass release; Android clean.

title: genfoam multiRegion: exact conservative meshToMesh (imCellVolumeWeight polyhedral overlap)
description: multi_region::mesh_to_mesh::MappingMethod::CellVolumeWeight currently approximates upstream's imCellVolumeWeight as nearest-cell addressing + a global integral rescale (globally conservative, not exact local overlap). Exact upstream integrates true polyhedral cell-overlap volumes (supermesh intersection). Needs a basic-lib supermesh/mesh-clipping operator (AABB octree + polyhedron clipping). Until then the degraded mode is documented and conserves the volume integral.

title: genfoam multiRegion: deformMesh / movePoints (apply meshDisp to mesh points)
description: The outer coupling loop (multi_region::outer_iteration::MultiPhysicsSolver) plumbs meshDisp through the coupling but does not move mesh points — upstream multiPhysicsSolver::deformMesh calls movePoints. Needs mutable mesh-point geometry on outram_foam_basic_lib::FvMesh (points + geometry recompute), which basic-lib does not yet expose.

title: genfoam multiRegion: dimension-reduced RBF for 1-D/2-D axial profiles
description: multi_region::rbf_mapping::RbfFieldMap fits a full 3-D polyharmonic spline; a collinear (pure-axial) or coplanar sample set makes the linear polynomial tail rank-deficient => RbfMapError::Singular (documented + tested in build_rejects_collinear_samples). Add an active-dimension detection that reduces the spline to the spanned subspace so a 1-D axial power profile can be RBF-mapped directly.

title: genfoam multiRegion: dispatch mesh-based Neutronics/TH/TM RegionModel variants
description: multi_region::outer_iteration::RegionModel currently realises Neutronics(LumpedNeutronics/point-kinetics), ThermalHydraulics(LumpedThermal), and Prescribed. When the mesh-based genfoam::neutronics diffusion/SP3/SN and genfoam::thermal_hydraulics solvers land (op-p6p.6/.7), add them as RegionModel variants and wire their correct()/residual into the Picard loop (the enum is exhaustive so every match site flags). Also unblocked: TM meshDisp source region.

notes.content: Done. Added mesh-based RegionModel variants in multi_region/mesh_region.rs: MeshNeutronics wraps the real DiffusionNeutronics (op-p6p.6) with cross-section (Doppler) temperature feedback via XS re-materialization at the importance-weighted mean TFuel each Picard iterate; MeshThermalHydraulics is a per-cell backward-Euler fuel-energy balance (thermal time-constant tau formulation) that is the integration seam for the full thermal_hydraulics::solver (op-p6p.7). Both wired into MultiPhysicsSolver via enum dispatch (RegionModel::MeshNeutronics/MeshThermalHydraulics; exhaustive match arms in outer_iteration.rs). V&V: mesh Doppler lowers k_eff (3.000->2.700 at 900->1800K); power-density conserved across a 20-cell->8-cell CellVolumeWeight map (rel 2.3e-16); coupled steady state settles at 909.8K with feedback -9.8 pcm and k_eff 2.9953. Fixed a cold-start false-convergence in the Picard loop (coupled >1-region needs >=2 sweeps). 24 multi_region tests pass release; Android check clean.

title: genfoam multiRegion: AABB/octree acceleration for meshToMesh addressing
description: MeshToMesh::new builds nearest-cell addressing by O(n_target * n_source) brute force. Fine for the reactor meshes coupled now; upstream uses an AABB octree (pmAABB) for scale-up. Add a spatial acceleration structure when large-mesh coupling performance matters.

title: genfoam multiRegion: per-cell / dynamic mesh XS feedback (neutronics-subtree API gap)
description: MeshNeutronics (multi_region/mesh_region.rs) currently drives DiffusionNeutronics with a GLOBAL Doppler feedback: it collapses the mapped TFuel field to one importance-weighted mean temperature and re-materialises the whole-mesh cross sections at that single point (DiffusionXsFields::materialize takes one feedback vector for all cells). Two neutronics-subtree API additions would lift this to full fidelity: (1) a materialize variant accepting a PER-CELL parameter array so each cell's XS use its local temperature (upstream setNeutronicsVariables.H evaluates per cell); (2) a public DiffusionNeutronics::set_k_eff / dynamic-reactivity setter so a scalar Delta-rho from the ReactivityFeedback layer can be injected into a diffusion TRANSIENT step (step() currently reads k_eff only from solve_eigenvalue; there is no public mutator, so the mesh path demonstrates negative feedback via steady eigenvalue re-solves, not a dynamic transient reactivity insertion). Both are edits to crate::genfoam::neutronics (owned by the neutronics fleet), out of scope for the multi_region subtree. Until then the global-feedback + steady path is real and closes the loop (V&V in mesh_region.rs tests).

title: appbuilder: close the Sod / Riemann V&V record gaps (missing numbers, date conflict, corrupted appendix)
description: From the 2026-08-07 bookkeeping pass of outram-foam-appbuilder-lib. Per the workspace V&V rule (methodology AND measured results), six gaps remain open after the pass: (1) tests/foam_vv_cases/main.rs test exact_riemann_matches_sod_table_ii has NO recorded result anywhere, yet it defines the faithful-station classification the primary Sod gate consumes -- run it and record the numbers in its doc comment; (2) no test in the crate records measurement uncertainty, and four say 'this machine' without identifying it -- add rustc version + CPU to each Results block; (3) Sod DATE CONFLICT: module doc and README say measured 2026-07-06, RESULTS.md and REVIEW_MANIFEST.md say 2026-07-17 for the same case -- determine which run produced the Table II numbers and reconcile; (4) tests/sod_shock_tube_validation/README.md appendix is character-corrupted from 'Step 3' on (~230 lines, '*' substituted into prose where '*' is also the star-state notation, so automated repair is unsafe) -- restore the derivation by hand against Toro (2013); a warning banner and the fixed DOI are already in place; (5) REVIEW_MANIFEST.md's human-verify checklist is entirely unchecked three weeks on -- maintainer action; (6) verification_and_validation/README.md mandates one .md per benchmark but only Sod has one. NOTE the pass already fixed a genuine numerical error (analytical k_eff 1.000010 -> 1.000004, confirmed by hand and by test output) and transcribed real measured results into three previously number-free Results sections (k_eff = 1.000008, +0.4 pcm; drift-flux u_settle = 1.1372e-3 m/s; bubble-column slip 0.2922 m/s; 2026-08-07, rustc 1.97.0).

notes.content:
DETECTION METHOD, added 2026-08-11. Item (4), the character-corrupted Sod appendix, is caught automatically by the workspace's own mandated README check:

  pandoc -f gfm+tex_math_dollars -t html --mathml <file> > /dev/null

It reports: [WARNING] Could not convert TeX math p / \*ho^\gamma = \text{const}. That is a corrupted \rho.

A full sweep of all 118 git-tracked README.md files on 2026-08-11 with pandoc 3.6.1 produced exactly ONE warning across the whole workspace, and it was this file. Every other README, including the ten that carry LaTeX math, converts cleanly with zero warnings and exit 0. So this is the sole outstanding markdown defect in the repository, which makes it cheap to confirm fixed later — re-run the sweep and expect zero warnings.

CONFIRMING THE BEAD'S OWN WARNING against a fresh look: automated repair really is unsafe. The file contains 160 '*' characters. Legitimate ones are the star-state notation (\rho^*_L, \rho^*_R, pStar) and ordinary markdown emphasis; corrupted ones are single characters substituted at random positions. Observed substitutions include a space in 'rarefaction*relation' and 'a*Riemann', 'i' in 'rarefaction *s' and 'rat*o', 'r' in '\*ho' and '*atio', 's' in 'post-*hock', a backslash in '\sqrt{*gamma', 'n' in 'ha*dy', 'o' in '*f', 'c' in 'post-rarefa*tion', and an underscore in '\rho^**L'. The replaced characters follow no pattern, so there is no rule that separates corruption from notation. Hand restoration against Toro (2013) remains the only safe route.

Only the pandoc-visible math error is machine-detectable; the corrupted PROSE is invisible to every automated check, so a clean pandoc run after a partial fix would NOT mean the appendix is restored.
