title: tampines zbs: human transcription check vs van Antwerpen (2010) eqs (12)-(16), and cite-or-drop the SANA/HTTU claim
description:
Follow-up from op-jyyp.16 (ZBS test suite written 2026-08-11).

Two items in crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/zbs.rs need a HUMAN with sources in hand; neither can be closed by running code:

1. TRANSCRIPTION. The dimensionless ZBS form (B, k_r, N, k_c, k_eff/k_f) was implemented without page-level access to the printed originals. The new test suite verifies the k_r -> 0 degeneration to the classic Zehner-Schlunder closed form to 1.398e-16 relative, but that is an ALGEBRAIC cross-check of the same expression regrouped -- it cannot detect a transcription error in the source equations. Needs checking against van Antwerpen, du Toit & Rousseau, Nucl. Eng. Des. 240 (2010) 1803-1818, eqs (12)-(16) (proprietary tier). Until then the module stays at Prototype in the V&V pipeline.

2. UNCITED CLAIM. The module docs previously asserted that stagnant-helium graphite beds measure order 1-2 W/(m K) at ambient in SANA/HTTU-class experiments, used as support for the finding that the VTB 18-point table is not reproducible. On 2026-08-11 this was flagged in-file as an uncited recollection, NOT checked against any source. It must be either given a real citation (source, tier, URL/DOI, date accessed per DATA_POLICY.md) or removed. None of the measured numbers in the module depend on it.

Also note the near-wall profile coefficients (1.36, 5.0) in ZbsBed::wall_region_porosity carry the same unverified-coefficient caveat.

Context: the VTB table mismatch itself is already tracked as op-jvua. Measured 2026-08-11: model/table ratio 0.176932 at 300 K rising to 0.644374 at 2000 K; reproducing the 300 K point would need k_f = 3.8367 W/(m K), 23.99x helium at 300 K / 6 MPa.

title: outram-mc-libs: init_seed derives streams 1 step apart, not 1 stride apart
description:
`outram_mc_libs::rng::lcg::init_seed(id, offset, master_seed)` (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/rng/lcg.rs:90) computes:

    let base = future_seed(DEFAULT_STRIDE, master_seed as u64);
    future_seed((id + offset) as u64, base)

i.e. future_seed(DEFAULT_STRIDE + id + offset, master). Consecutive ids therefore land ONE LCG step apart.

OpenMC's own init_seed (canonical source, /home/teddy0/Documents/research/openmc/src/random_lcg.cpp:60) is:

    return future_seed(static_cast<uint64_t>(id) * prn_stride, master_seed + offset);

i.e. id * STRIDE steps apart. The port drops the multiplication.

IMPACT: any caller using init_seed for per-particle / per-stream separation gets streams that are a one-draw shift of each other rather than independent — the exact opposite of the reproducible-parallel-MC guarantee the doc comment claims ('Each particle gets a unique starting seed by striding from the master seed'). Two particles' histories would be near-perfectly correlated. Needs checking against the actual transport call sites: if init_seed is used to seed particle streams, k-eff statistics may be affected.

FOUND BY: the raffles samplers port (op-vjw.2), which needs independent per-dimension streams for Latin hypercube sampling. raffles works around it by calling future_seed(stream * DEFAULT_STRIDE, master) directly with OpenMC's semantics; the workaround and the discrepancy are documented in crates/raffles/src/samplers.rs (stream_seed) and crates/raffles/CLAUDE.md.

SUGGESTED FIX: future_seed((id + offset) as u64 * DEFAULT_STRIDE, master_seed as u64), plus a regression test asserting that init_seed(k) and init_seed(k+1) are DEFAULT_STRIDE steps apart. Verify against the C++ before changing — the offset placement differs too (OpenMC adds offset to the master seed, this port adds it to the id).

notes.content:
FIX IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-06 (uncommitted, awaiting maintainer review — AI output is untrusted draft per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md).

crates/outram-mc-libs/src/rng/lcg.rs now mirrors /home/teddy0/Documents/research/openmc/src/random_lcg.cpp:60-64:

    pub fn init_seed(id: i64, offset: i64, master_seed: i64) -> u64 {
        future_seed(
            (id as u64).wrapping_mul(DEFAULT_STRIDE),
            master_seed.wrapping_add(offset) as u64,
        )
    }

Both defects in this bead are fixed: id now MULTIPLIES the stride (streams 152917 draws apart, not 1), and offset is added to the MASTER SEED (independent run, not a shift within one). Signature kept per the maintainer's instruction; the master_seed parameter is documented as a deliberate deviation from OpenMC's global.

BLAST RADIUS (measured, not assumed): init_seed had ZERO library call sites. Its only users are 5 sites in examples/triso_stochastic_gpu.rs. All library transport code (physics::keff, pebble_beds::keff_delta, physics::transport_csg, gpu::batched_*) already calls future_seed(idx * STRIDE, base) directly with correct OpenMC semantics, so no k-eff or transport statistic was ever produced through the bug.

TESTS: 4 new regression tests in rng::lcg::tests, each verified to FAIL against the old implementation:
  - init_seed_consecutive_ids_are_one_full_stride_apart
  - init_seed_matches_openmc_golden_values (5 golden seeds computed by an independent Python implementation of the upstream recurrence)
  - init_seed_streams_do_not_overlap (old impl: 4095/4095 lag-1 exact matches — stream 1 WAS stream 0 shifted one draw)
  - init_seed_offset_selects_an_independent_run
Suite: 234 -> 238 passing, 0 failed, 0 pre-existing test moved.

RECORDED RESULTS: verification_and_validation/gpu_benchmarks/triso_stochastic_cls_gpu.csv was stale (produced 2026-07-21 through the bug). Re-run 2026-08-06 on an RTX A5000; CSV regenerated and the example's V&V doc block updated with the new measured values plus an explicit supersession note. CPU f64 reference moved 0.7013826 -> 0.7014103 (+0.0000277, 0.04 sigma) — the central value was barely biased; what was invalid was the quoted binomial sigma, since neighbouring histories were not independent samples.

SIBLING DEFECT FOUND, NOT FIXED HERE: rng::lcg::prn omits OpenMC's PCG-RXS-M-XS output permutation -> filed as op-jis (P1). Larger blast radius (all recorded stats + WGSL shaders + raffles), needs its own planned change.
ALSO: 2 pre-existing doctest failures in geometry::surface unrelated to this -> op-keh (P2).

tuas: parallel-branch flow solver panics via todo!() on non-convergence (:1347)
description:
In crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/array_control_vol_and_fluid_component_collections/fluid_component_collection/super_collection_series_and_parallel_functions.rs, the fn calculate_pressure_change_using_guessed_branch_mass_flowrate (declared :1184) sets SimpleConvergency { eps: 1e-9, max_iter: 70 } (:1310), tries find_root_brent (:1315), falls through its Err arm with only a dbg!, tries find_root_regula_falsi (:1332), falls through that Err arm with only a dbg!, and then reaches:

    todo!("debugging: all root finding methods used not successful");   // :1347

This ABORTS THE PROCESS on ordinary non-convergence. With max_iter 70 and eps 1e-9 that is a routine runtime outcome for a hard parallel network, not a theoretical one. The crate already has a TuasLibError type in scope, so returning Err is available.

Call sites: 5 in this file (:870, :993, :1027, :1075, :1098) plus 4 on a same-named sibling in collection_series_and_parallel_functions.rs (:620, :724, :758, :806).

This is the only todo!() in the file. (The crate has ~100 crate-wide, but those are overwhelmingly in test/calibration modules, not the library dispatch path -- this one is notable precisely because it is in the hot path.)

Fix: change the signature to return Result<Pressure, TuasLibError> and propagate, or return the best-effort bracket with a diagnostic error.

Verified 2026-08-07 against the working tree.

title: scripts/push-beads-store.sh printed a false 'beads remain local only' warning
description:
Observed once, 2026-08-11 ~15:16 SGT, on develop.

WHAT HAPPENED, exactly:
  $ ./scripts/push-beads-store.sh
  warning: could not push beads store ref to origin; beads remain local only

Immediately afterwards, by hand:
  $ git push origin refs/heads/beads/store:refs/heads/beads/store
  Everything up-to-date
  $ git rev-parse refs/heads/beads/store
  4beb401e2abc278df219140a944edc7d60eacbfe
  $ git ls-remote origin refs/heads/beads/store
  4beb401e2abc278df219140a944edc7d60eacbfe  refs/heads/beads/store
  $ git show refs/heads/beads/store:state.jsonl | grep -c op-nik1
  1

So the ref WAS published, including the bead created minutes earlier — the warning was false. No beads were actually stranded.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the whole point of the Stop-hook carve-out is that beads filed in a session are never left on one machine. A warning that cries wolf trains the reader to ignore the one time it is real.

SUSPECTED CAUSE, not confirmed: the script compares `git rev-parse` against `git ls-remote` and only pushes on a mismatch. Two plausible races, both consistent with what was seen — (a) the kopi-beans daemon was mid-flush, so local_sha moved between the rev-parse and the push; (b) a concurrent push (the Stop hook firing alongside the manual invocation) held the ref lock, so `git push` exited nonzero even though the ref reached origin. `git push` output is sent to /dev/null, so there is no evidence either way.

SUGGESTED FIX: capture the push's stderr instead of discarding it and include it in the warning, and re-check `git ls-remote` before warning — if the remote now matches the local ref, the push effectively succeeded and the warning should not fire. Do not silence the warning outright; make it accurate.

title: tampines: Edwards-O'Brien two-fluid (6-eqn) test -- blocked until op-dt3.13/op-dt3.19 deliver the solver
description:
BLOCKED on the six-equation solver existing. Placeholder test already landed: multiphase_1d::edwards_tests::two_fluid_step_still_refuses_to_pretend pins the documented contract that TwoFluid1d::step() returns NotYetImplemented, and its doc comment describes the Edwards case to write once the solver exists.

Test-ownership split (maintainer instruction, 2026-08-11): tampines-steam-tables tests own the HEM models; tampines tests own drift flux and the six-equation model.

Landed on 2026-08-11 in crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/edwards_tests.rs:
- edwards_drift_flux_gs1_pressure_history (ACTIVE gate, 36-39 s): full 600 ms Edwards-O'Brien blowdown on DriftFlux1d, 24 cells, dt = 30 us, Hendrie non-isothermal IC, HEM-choked break through 0.87 A with the 1 ms rupture-disc ramp. Measured: GS-1 pressure RMSE 29.0 psia vs the digitised Edwards curve over 16 points (0-0.30 s), worst +52.0 psia at t = 0.100 s, flashing plateau 354.3 psia (experimental band ~350-367), break peak 101.0 lbm/s, 99.7 % drained, no cold tail (min 372.6 K) and +0.0 psia rebound.
- edwards_drift_flux_slip_and_tau_sensitivity (#[ignore], 132 s) and edwards_drift_flux_explore (#[ignore] scratch runner).

Key finding for the future six-equation case: turning the slip closure off entirely (C0 = 1, Vgj = 0) changes GS-1 pressure by at most 1.44 psia even though peak |v_g - v_l| goes 57.6 m/s -> 0. Edwards-O'Brien GS-1 pressure is therefore a poor discriminator of MECHANICAL non-equilibrium; a six-equation Edwards case should be judged on whether THERMAL non-equilibrium (max_thermal_nonequilibrium) changes anything, not on pressure RMSE alone. Mesh refinement (48 cells) moves GS-1 more (6.89 psia) than any model parameter does.

DoD: once TwoFluid1d::step() computes, write the Edwards two-fluid case in edwards_tests.rs mirroring run_edwards(), report max_thermal_nonequilibrium alongside the GS-1 pressure comparison, and record methodology + measured results per the workspace V&V doc rule.

NUREG/CR-2671 Table 4:2 row 7 (initial nozzle-inlet temperature) is OCR-truncated for Marviken tests 23 and 24
description:
In crates/kovan-literature/open/reports/nureg-cr-2671-marviken.pdf, report p.21 / PDF p.37, Table 4:2 row 7 'Initial temperature at nozzle inlet ~ degC' returns only two digits for tests 23 and 24 ('19' and '27') where every neighbouring column is three digits (T19=167, T20=181, T21=184, T22=168, T25=189, T26=135, T27=167). Both pdftotext -layout and -raw give the same truncation, so the text layer is at fault, not the extraction command. Physically the values must be three-digit.

Impact today: none. The Marviken V&V in crates/tampines-steam-tables (bead op-21g.16) does not need row 7 — it builds the stagnation state from row 6 'Min fluid temperature in the vessel' (260 degC for test 23, 230 degC for test 24), which is readable and consistent with row 5's nominal subcooling (3 K and 33 K) and with the universal stagnation qualities of Table 8:3.

Impact later: a model that wants the discharge-pipe inlet temperature rather than the vessel bulk temperature will need row 7. Fix by re-OCRing PDF p.37 at higher resolution, or by reading the page visually and recording the two values in the KovanDocument metadata. Do not guess them.

title: kovan-literature: lit import metadata extraction is unreliable on EU/JRC report PDFs
description:
Observed 2026-08-11 ingesting EUR 28712 EN (JRC HTR safety book, 264 pages) with kovan lit import. Command run:

./target/release/kovan lit import ~/Downloads/kjna28712enn.pdf --json-out crates/kovan-literature/open/reports/vhtr-modul-safety-jrc.json --markdown-out crates/kovan-literature/generated/markdown/open/vhtr-modul-safety-jrc.md

The Markdown body extraction was GOOD — 264 pages, 5373 lines, 498k chars, content intact. The METADATA was wrong in five ways, all of which had to be hand-patched afterwards:

1. TITLE TRUNCATED AT A LINE BREAK. Got "The High Temperature"; the actual title is "The High Temperature Gas-cooled Reactor: Safety considerations of the (V)HTR-Modul". The cover sets the title across three lines and only the first was taken.
2. EDITOR MISTAKEN FOR AUTHOR. Got authors = [Scheuermann, Walter], who is the first EDITOR. The actual authors are Kugeler, K., Nabielek, H. and Buckthorpe, D., listed above the editors on the cover. There is no editor field in KovanDocument at all, which is part of the problem — consider adding one.
3. document_type = Other, though the document carries strong Report markers: an EUR number, a JRC catalogue number, an ISSN and a Publications Office imprint. A heuristic on "EUR NNNNN EN" or "JRC NNNNNN" would catch this class.
4. source_sha256 left null even though the tool has the file open. It should hash what it ingests — provenance under DATA_POLICY.md wants it, and it is free to compute.
5. slug derived from the wrong author, giving scheuermann2017the — which also shows the truncated-title bug feeding into slug generation.

Also note: doi, year, page_count and visibility were all extracted CORRECTLY, so the extractor is not broadly broken, just weak on multi-line cover layouts and author/editor blocks.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION: for the title, join consecutive large-font cover lines rather than taking the first. For authors, prefer the block above an "Editors:" label when one is present. For document_type, add report-identifier heuristics. Always populate source_sha256.

Not urgent — hand-patching the JSON is quick and lit bibtex round-trips correctly afterwards. But every ingested document currently needs a manual metadata pass, which will not scale.

title: tuas: Sieder-Tate Reynolds validity bounds inverted (accepts only 4000-10000, rejects Re > 1e4 where it is valid)
description: Found 2026-08-11 by correlation audit during op-4542. crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/heat_transfer_correlations/nusselt_number_correlations/pipe_correlations.rs:246-248 panics on Re > 10000, and the doc at ~L183-187 states 4000 < Re_D < 10000. Sieder & Tate (1936) is a turbulent correlation valid for Re > 1e4 -- 10000 is the LOWER bound, not the upper. Combined with the Re < 4000 panic below it, the function accepts only 4000-10000, a window almost entirely outside the correlation's validity, and refuses every Reynolds number where it is actually valid. The algebra itself (0.027 Re^0.8 Pr^(1/3) (mu_b/mu_w)^0.14) is correct.

title: njoy THERMR: no consumer surface for the thermal ELASTIC channels — thermr::scattering exposes incoherent-inelastic only
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-11 by code inspection + a live parse of ENDF/B-VIII.0 graphite.

STATE: src/thermr/scattering.rs is the documented 'hand-off' surface that outram-mc-libs consumes, but it exposes exactly one type, IncoherentInelasticScattering, covering MF=7/MT=4 only. The two ELASTIC channels are implemented as bare impl blocks on the raw parser structs:
  - CoherentElastic::cross_section / ::bragg_reflections  (src/thermr/coherent.rs:29,53)
  - IncoherentElastic::cross_section / ::equiprobable_cosines / ::debye_waller  (src/thermr/incoherent_elastic.rs:36,64,83)
Neither has a uom-typed, temperature-selecting, pre-tabulated consumer struct analogous to IncoherentInelasticScattering, and grep shows the ONLY in-tree consumer of either is src/acer/thermal.rs (the ACE writer). No transport crate can reach them through the documented surface.

WHY IT MATTERS (HTR-10 critical path): graphite (tsl-crystalline-graphite MAT=30, tsl-reactor-graphite-10P MAT=31, -30P MAT=32) is coherent-elastic + incoherent-inelastic, with NO incoherent-elastic (verified: parse_mf7 reports coherent_elastic=true, incoherent_elastic=false, incoherent_inelastic=true for all three). Coherent elastic is ~90% of graphite thermal scattering at 0.0253 eV. So the one channel that dominates the HTR-10 moderator is the one with no consumer surface.

WORK: add a CoherentElasticScattering consumer struct in thermr::scattering mirroring IncoherentInelasticScattering — from_endf_file(path, mat, temperature), uom-typed cross_section(E), and a sample-a-Bragg-reflection method returning (E_out = E_in, mu) from bragg_reflections' (mu, weight) pairs. Do the same for IncoherentElastic (needed later for ZrH, not for graphite). Depends on op-1y4y for correct temperature behaviour.

SIZE: small. The physics is already implemented and tested; this is a typed wrapper + temperature selection.

notes.content: DONE 2026-08-11 (this session; unverified-by-human, not committed yet). thermr::scattering now exposes all three channels: CoherentElasticScattering (from_endf_file/from_tape at a uom Temperature; uom cross_section(E) per principal atom; bragg_cutoff() = first edge with nonzero S, 1.8223 meV for graphite; bragg_reflections(E) normalised-probability (mu,p) list, zero-weight grid points filtered; sample(E, xi)->(E_out=E_in, mu) with caller-owned RNG) and IncoherentElasticScattering (cross_section(E), equiprobable_cosines(E,nbin); constructor refuses temps outside the W'(T) table range) alongside IncoherentInelasticScattering. All re-exported from thermr. Temperature resolution at construction per the shared mf7 policy (tolerance/interpolate/refuse). Consumer-surface consistency V&V in tests/thermal_graphite_coherent.rs passes (surface == mf7-level to machine precision; probabilities sum to 1; sampling elastic). Downstream MC wiring (op-nhoa/op-hc2o) untouched per scope.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
One addition to this surface, 2026-08-11 (uncommitted), made while implementing op-nhoa: CoherentElasticScattering::bragg_edge_table() -> Vec<(NeutronEnergy, CrossSection)>, one uom-typed pair per tabulated Bragg edge (221 for ENDF/B-VIII.0 crystalline graphite), where sigma_i = S(E_i,T)/(E_i*natom) is the value cross_section() takes throughout [E_i, E_{i+1}).

WHY IT WAS NEEDED: sigma_coh_el(E) is a 1/E sawtooth with a discontinuity at every edge. A consumer that pre-tabulates it on its own log grid - which outram-mc must do, to keep the transport hot loop cheap - smears all 221 edges. Exposing the step table lets the consumer cache the channel EXACTLY instead: measured worst relative deviation of outram-mc's cached copy vs this surface is 7.67e-16 over 21199 points from 1e-4 to 4 eV, and the whole table is ~3.5 kB, cheaper than the resample it replaces. Everything else (the cumulative structure factor S_i/natom = sigma_i*E_i, and each edge's sampling weight as its increment) is recoverable from the pairs exactly.

It mirrors the CoherentElasticXS::bragg_edges() / ::factors() pair that OpenMC's CoherentElasticAE::sample consumes (src/secondary_thermal.cpp:34-54), so it is a port move rather than an invention. No behaviour change to any existing method. njoy full suite green after it (393 lib tests + all integration, scripts/test.sh, release). Not closing - human review still owed on this bead's original work too.

title: Wire VirtualLattice into Cell/Universe so transport actually uses it
description:
The virtual-lattice port (src/geometry/virtual_lattice/) is currently a STANDALONE data structure: it builds, traverses and locates correctly, but nothing in the transport path calls it. Cell::distance_to_boundary still scans every surface in the region.

Upstream wires it at three points (vendored fork, commit be04e28):
  - src/cell.cpp:631  CSGCell::distance() branches to distance_in_virtual_lattice when the cell carries the virtual_lattice flag
  - src/universe.cpp:42  Universe::find_cell() branches to find_cell_in_virtual_lattice when filled_with_triso_base_ != -1
  - src/geometry.cpp:299  find_cell_in_virtual_lattice handles the coord-level/material bookkeeping

The third is deep OpenMC model:: global machinery (coord levels, distribcell, sqrtkT) and was deliberately NOT ported — it needs a decision about how our Geometry/Universe types carry the equivalent state.

Scope: add an optional virtual lattice to Cell, branch distance_to_boundary onto it, and decide the Universe-level story. Until this lands the port is dead code in the transport sense — see the workspace 'no orphaned dead code' rule.

NOTE: not ported and probably not wanted — the XML (pugixml) input parsing for the virtual_lattice/lower_left/pitch/shape/triso_particle nodes, and the openmc/cell.py + openmc/model/triso.py Python API. XML parsing is explicitly out of scope for this crate.

Investigate an event-based/Woodcock collision-site batch so more of the sweep's XS lookups go through the GPU (or document that history-based transport fundamentally caps GPU penetration here).

notes.content: Deep GPU penetration pass delivered (worktree, 2026-07-17). DONE: (a) native-breakpoint union grid — Nuclide::native_energy_grid + UnionTotalXs::tabulate_native (10834 nodes on Godiva, ~2.7x more accurate than equal-size dense-log). (b) event-based batched-flight GPU kernel — a batch of live neutrons stays resident in GPU buffers; per dispatch the GPU does RNG(emulated 64-bit LCG, bit-exact state) + native-union Sigma_t binary-search + d_col sample + sphere flight + leak test for the WHOLE batch; only branchy collision physics stays on CPU. Wired under ComputeType::Gpu (run_keff_gpu_batched), CPU fallback + Android gating intact. k agreement: GPU within 0.16 sigma of single-thread reference. RNG decision: per-history LCG streams, GPU state advance bit-exact, f32 flight -> reproducible run-to-run but NOT bit-identical to single-thread; CPU single stays trusted reference. HONEST TIMING VERDICT: GPU loses to CpuMultiThread at ALL batch sizes 1e3..1e6, NO crossover (1e6: multi ~3-7s vs GPU ~19-34s). Cause: memory-transfer/launch bound — event loop round-trips CPU/GPU boundary once per event because collision physics is on CPU. NOT closing (GPU did not win anywhere). Tests: 80->90 lib tests pass, Android clean. See docs/ai-fleet-review/gpu-deep-transport/REVIEW_MANIFEST.md + verification_and_validation/gpu_batched_transport/README.md.

description: Follow-up from op-u6s.7 (2026-07-17). The event-based batched-flight GPU path (run_keff_gpu_batched) puts the per-event flight (RNG+Sigma_t lookup+distance+streaming) on the GPU but keeps the branchy collision physics on the CPU, forcing a CPU/GPU round-trip (upload live batch, dispatch, read back pos+rng+outcome, CPU collide, re-upload) PER EVENT. Measured verdict: memory-transfer/launch bound, GPU ~4-5x SLOWER than CpuMultiThread at every batch size 1e3..1e6, no crossover. To actually beat multi-thread the collision kernel (nuclide sampling, reaction partition fission|capture|inelastic|n2n|elastic, secondary energy/angle laws, on-GPU fission banking + stream compaction) must run on the GPU too, so a batch advances through many events WITHOUT leaving GPU memory. Large, branch-heavy effort. Alternatively evaluate Woodcock/delta-tracking on GPU (single majorant, no per-nuclide branch) as a more GPU-friendly collision scheme.

title: basic-lib: add traction (sigma.n=0) BC on D and anisotropic (tensor-coeff) laplacian for thermo-mechanics
description: Follow-ups surfaced by genfoam thermoMechanics mesh solve (op-p6p.11). (1) fvm::laplacian_vec only takes a scalar coefficient (2mu+lambda); an anisotropic stiffness needs a tensor-coefficient laplacian operator. (2) The field boundary layer offers only Dirichlet (FixedValue) and zero-gradient on D; a traction boundary condition (sigma.n = given, e.g. stress-free surface under thermal load where dD/dn != 0) is not expressible, so the stress-free free-thermal-expansion case can only be reached via a non-uniform temperature with Dirichlet ends. (3) fvc::grad_vec sets a zero-gradient output boundary, so the compact-normal-stress divSigmaExp correction carries no boundary-gradient info (exact on 1-D columns, approximate near 2-D/3-D boundaries). (4) No non-orthogonal gradient correction. See src/genfoam/thermo_mechanics/mesh_solve.rs limitations note.

title: GeN-Foam build blocked in container: ESI OpenFOAM v2506 unreachable
description:
GeN-Foam (gitlab.com/foam-for-nuclear/GeN-Foam, cloned OK to /opt/foam/GeN-Foam) declares in its README that it is built on the OpenFOAM ESI/OpenCFD distribution, currently v2506 (openfoam.com) — NOT the OpenFOAM Foundation 'dev' distribution (openfoam.org) that this repo vendors at crates/outram-foam-turbulence-lib/upstream_source/OpenFOAM. The two distributions are API-incompatible for a solver as deeply integrated as GeN-Foam.

Blocker: the remote-execution container's network policy denies both dl.openfoam.com and develop.openfoam.com (agent proxy returns 403 to CONNECT). github.com and gitlab.com ARE reachable. There is no official ESI mirror on those hosts, and pulling an unofficial third-party mirror was deliberately NOT done — provenance/licence review is required per RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md, so an unverified mirror is not acceptable for this project.

Consequence: GeN-Foam cannot be compiled or run in this container. This is an environment constraint, not a code defect.

What WAS delivered instead (commit ce4bd82): the OUTRAM PARK equivalent V&V case for GeN-Foam's Tutorials/guidedCases/1_reactorSlab_1D_1Gr_neutronicDiffusion, built from that tutorial's nuclearData verbatim (D=0.1275, sigmaRemoval=5.0082, nuSigmaEff=5.5675, P0 scatter 0.1, IV, 6-group beta/lambda) on a 151-cell 1.5 m slab. It verifies against the closed-form one-group bare-slab solution: k_eff = 1.000008 vs analytical 1.000004 (0.4 pcm), and reproduces the k_inf = 1.111677 quoted in the upstream README — confirming the in-group-scattering convention matches.

To unblock: either (a) allowlist dl.openfoam.com / develop.openfoam.com for this environment, or (b) build on a machine with ESI OpenFOAM v2506 already installed, or (c) run the GeN-Foam tutorial elsewhere and commit its reference output as a stored benchmark for regression comparison.

Haverkamp (1977) constitutive model + kr(pc) interface
description: The Celia 1990 problem uses Haverkamp et al. description: root@vm
title: root@vm
tampines-steam-tables: choked-flow and Joule-Thomson solvers should return Result, not panic on non-convergence
description:
Found while doing op-dt3.26 (extending interfaces::checked). These panics are NOT envelope violations, so no bounds-checking facade can exclude them - the honest fix is in the solvers themselves.

PANIC SITES (traced 2026-08-11):
  - steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/choked_flow/mod.rs:241
    panic!('unable to find bracket for critical mass flux root finding') - fires when
    the downward pressure scan from p0 finds no sign change in
    (g_energy - g_hem). Reached from get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_multiphase_ph
    and thus from TampinesSteamTableCV::get_crit_pressure_and_massflux.
  - converging_diverging_nozzles/joule_thomson.rs:157 panic!('bounds are same sign!')
  - converging_diverging_nozzles/joule_thomson.rs:201 panic!('Joule-Thomson algorithm:
    failed to converge')

WHY A FACADE CANNOT HELP. Whether a bracket exists is a property of the function over
the whole scan interval, not of the stagnation state (p0, h0). Deciding it requires
running the scan - at which point you have done the work and can just return the
failure. A checked wrapper that gated only the (p,h) envelope of the stagnation state
would claim a safety it does not provide, which op-dt3.26's no-half-gating rule
forbids. So interfaces::checked deliberately leaves these alone and says so in its
'Known gaps' section.

WHAT op-dt3.26 DID COVER in this area: ps::try_mass_flux_ps_eqm_throat, which is a
genuine envelope check - the unchecked mass_flux_ps_eqm_throat differentiates v(p,s)
by finite difference (dp = p*1e-5), so it evaluates the (p,s) flash at p, p+dp and
max(p-dp, floor). Near 100 MPa and near the 1073.15 K isotherm the step walks out of
the envelope and the raw function panics; the checked version re-runs the envelope
check at all three pressures (and gates the s_tp_eqm_two_phase bubble-point lookup)
and rejects instead. Verified: 162 394 accepted points, zero leaked panics.

PROPOSED FIX (needs maintainer sign-off - it CHANGES PUBLIC SIGNATURES and so was out
of scope for op-dt3.26's additive-only remit):
  - a NonConvergent-style error variant (the crate CLAUDE.md already forbids papering
    over NonConvergent with a default value, so an error type is the intended shape)
  - get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_* -> Result
  - the Joule-Thomson root finder -> Result
  - TampinesSteamTableCV::get_crit_pressure_and_massflux gets a try_ sibling
Alternatively keep the panicking functions and add try_ siblings that return Result,
which would stay additive.

title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
v1 GUI clobbers shared state with a stale full-struct overwrite (lost-update race)
description:
Found 2026-07-28 while porting to v2. v1's GUI does: clone CIETState early in the egui repaint, mutate a couple of control fields on the clone, then overwrite_state(clone) at the end -- a full-struct store from a stale snapshot, ~20x/second. Sites: examples/ciet_educational_simulator/ciet_simulator_v1/app/panels_and_pages/main_page.rs:109 and :1194, and the frequency-response block in app.rs.

Impact in v1: mild and self-healing. CIETState is a publication surface, not the solver's internal state -- the physics thread recomputes temperatures from its own tuas component objects each timestep, so clobbered OUTPUTS are restored within one step. That is presumably why this was never noticed.

Impact in v2: NOT benign. CIETState also carries the CONTROLS the solver reads each timestep (heater power, pump pressure, set points). With OPC-UA writes arriving from remote clients at arbitrary times, a client write landing between the GUI's clone and its store is silently discarded -- remote control would appear to randomly not take effect, and would be near-impossible to diagnose from the client side.

Fixed in v2 by writing only the specific fields the GUI actually changed, under a short write guard, instead of overwriting the whole struct (main_page.rs:134 and :1236).

Consequence for port equivalence (op-wqk.13.6): v1 and v2 will NOT agree step-for-step with a GUI running, because v1 discards updates and v2 does not. The comparison must therefore be run HEADLESS on both sides to be meaningful.

No fix proposed for v1 itself -- out of scope for the v2 request, and v1 is the maintainer-validated reference. Flagging for his decision.

title: Widget Studio — gallery app for developing and QC-ing the visual component library
description:
A gallery/dogfooding app in outram-park-digital-twin-engine that displays every visual component on one screen with live controls, so each widget can be built and quality-controlled ONE AT A TIME (maintainer's framing, 2026-08-03: 'construct widget by widget so there is some quality control').

SCOPE: gallery only. An authoring tool (compose a plant schematic interactively) is explicitly deferred to a future epic.

WHY: the components/ layer is far weaker than its bead history suggests. Inventory 2026-08-03 -- 1 genuine widget (PipeVisual, 281 lines, per-FV-cell colouring + tracers), 1 modest (ReactorVesselVisual), 4 single-rectangle colour-only (cooling tower, steam generator, turbine, valve), and 4 with NO state-derived detail at all (pump, condenser, heat exchanger, instrumentation -- flat circles/rects). op-wqk.3 is closed, but it delivered wrappers, not good widgets.

Corroborating symptom: op-wqk.9.4 records that htgr_sim_v1's schematic OMITS PipeVisual because standing up its fluid-array backend is disproportionate -- i.e. the one good widget is too awkward to use. A studio surfaces exactly this class of problem early.

DESIGN BAR (maintainer, 2026-08-03/04): a widget's look must derive from the real dimensions and design of the component -- turbine sizing, pipe bore and run -- not from arbitrary screen coordinates. Aesthetically: pipes connect smoothly, thickness reflects cross-sectional area, displayed length is proportional to real length, and angle follows elevation so natural-circulation loops read correctly. Avoid over-detailing; too much may confuse the end user.

CONSTRAINT: the engine crate forbids new physics (crate CLAUDE.md). Any missing dimension is added in tampines -- see op-dt3.17 and its children.

title: TurbineVisual: per-stage blade angulation from the physical turbine model (replace placeholders)
description:
Maintainer, 2026-08-04: 'the turbine blades are reaction + impulse. They are angled differently at each stage. Have placeholder angles for those. When detailed turbine design lands (and it should later), then take the angulation from the physical turbine model.'

INTERIM (done under op-wqk.14.3): stator + rotor blades are drawn with a PLACEHOLDER per-stage angle schedule. These are illustrative only and MUST be labelled as such in the doc comments -- they are not derived from any turbine design and must never be presented as if they were.

THE PHYSICS THEY STAND IN FOR:
  - Degree of reaction is the fraction of the stage enthalpy drop taken across the ROTOR. Impulse ~ 0% (all expansion in the fixed nozzle/stator, rotor just turns the flow); reaction typically ~50% (expansion split between stator and rotor).
  - Classic steam-turbine practice puts impulse stages at the HP inlet (Rateau/Curtis) and reaction stages toward the LP exhaust (Parsons), so a multi-stage machine is a MIXTURE and the blade angles vary stage by stage -- which is exactly why one fixed angle for all rows is wrong.
  - The blade SHAPES differ too, not just the angles: impulse rotor blades are near-symmetric buckets; reaction blades are asymmetric aerofoils. If the drawing is to distinguish stage types honestly, shape should follow angle.

WHEN THIS IS DONE: the angles must come from the real turbine model rather than the placeholder schedule -- stator exit angle alpha and rotor inlet/outlet angles beta per stage, plus the degree of reaction per stage. That model does not exist yet; it arrives with the detailed turbine design work (see op-dt3.18, the TampinesSteamArray-coupled turbine). Wire the dependency and delete the placeholder schedule at that point; do not leave both paths live.

title: Widget library: standard PWR HP and LP turbines (single-flow vs double-flow)
description:
Maintainer, 2026-08-04: 'we should have a standard HP and LP turbine as it is for the PWR plants' -- in the widget library.

CORRECTION THIS CARRIES. On 2026-08-04 the mirrored 'hourglass' silhouette inherited from fhr_sim_v2 was called an artwork defect and replaced with monotonic inlet-to-exhaust blade growth (commit b44f549). That was only half right. A PWR LP turbine is normally DOUBLE-FLOW: steam admits at the centre and expands outward in BOTH directions, so its rotor genuinely is mirrored about the mid-plane. The real defect was applying one silhouette unconditionally, plus proportions that collapsed at wide aspect ratios. Flow path is a property of the machine, not a drawing style.

WHAT TO BUILD:
  - Single-flow: monotonic expansion, inlet one end, exhaust the other. Typical HP.
  - Double-flow: centre admission, mirrored expansion to an exhaust at each end. Typical PWR LP, and how the original fhr_sim_v2 artwork was actually shaped.

Closed set -> enum dispatch, per the workspace no-trait-objects rule.

STANDARD PWR SECONDARY ARRANGEMENT to represent:
  - Steam generators deliver SATURATED (not superheated) steam, roughly 6-7 MPa.
  - HP turbine expands to roughly 1 MPa. Wet steam throughout, so erosion matters.
  - A moisture separator reheater (MSR) sits between HP and LP -- it is a distinct component and is NOT currently in the widget library at all. Worth its own bead.
  - Typically two or three double-flow LP turbines exhaust to the condenser at vacuum (~5 kPa).
  - LP last-stage blades are very long; the annulus area ratio between HP and LP is large and should be visible when the two widgets are shown side by side.

RELATION TO OTHER BEADS: per-stage blade angulation and the impulse/reaction mix are op-wqk.14.11 (placeholders now, real angles when the physical turbine model lands, op-dt3.18). Physical envelope dimensions remain blocked on op-dt3.17.1. This bead is about the FLOW PATH and the HP/LP presets, which are independent of both.

DO NOT present the presets as a specific vendor's or plant's design -- they are illustrative standard-arrangement values per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md, and the data policy forbids using any actual plant data.

notes.content:
DECIDED 2026-08-04 (maintainer): DOUBLE-FLOW IS THE DEFAULT for turbine widgets. Single-flow remains available as the other enum variant, but a TurbineVisual built without specifying a flow path draws double-flow.

This matches large-PWR practice rather than being merely a drawing preference: at PWR secondary-side volumetric flows, the HP turbine is commonly double-flow as well as the LP set (a typical large PWR turbine-generator is one double-flow HP plus two or three double-flow LP cylinders). So double-flow is the right default for BOTH presets, not just LP.

Practical consequence for the implementation: the mirrored silhouette from the original fhr_sim_v2 artwork becomes the DEFAULT rendering again, with centre admission and an exhaust at each end -- but now with the pitch-derived proportions from b44f549 so it no longer collapses at wide aspect ratios, and with the blade-height growth running outward from the centre admission plane toward both exhausts (not inward, and not mirrored-by-accident as before).
notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

description: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
TurbineVisual: settle stator/rotor blade lean direction (deferred)
description:
Deferred by the maintainer 2026-08-04 after several rounds of on-screen iteration. The turbine looks acceptable; the blade LEAN convention is not settled and should be decided against a proper reference rather than by eye.

WHAT IS SETTLED (do not redo):
  - Blade HEIGHT mirrors about the admission plane for double flow. Enforced by the test double_flow_geometry_is_symmetric_about_the_admission_plane. The rotor radius must blend from the LESS-EXPANDED neighbour (nearer admission), not from row+1 -- +x is downstream on one half and upstream on the other, and blending toward row+1 on both halves broke the symmetry.
  - Blades are rooted at the hub, run radially to the tip, and project root and tip by the same cos(phi) so they shorten onto the shaft edge-on.
  - Blades are cambered quadratic Beziers; camber runs in OPPOSITE senses for stator and rotor. That opposition is what turns the flow and extracts work.
  - The stator ring is drawn whole; only the ROTOR hides its far half (that is what reads as rotation).

WHAT IS NOT SETTLED -- the lean (overall slant), as distinct from the camber:
  - Attempt 1: lean applied in a fixed x direction. Maintainer: rotor blades not symmetric.
  - Attempt 2: lean mirrored with flow direction via a flow_sign helper. Maintainer: stator wrong on the left, rotor wrong on the right. Those four observations are only satisfiable by uniform lean with the rotor base inverted, so flow_sign was removed.
  - Attempt 3 (current): lean uniform across the machine; stator negative (angles down, maintainer-verified for SINGLE flow), rotor negative. Consequence: the two rows now lean the SAME way, and only the camber opposes.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
  1. Should lean mirror with flow direction on a double-flow machine, or stay uniform because the shaft turns one way along its whole length? Physical argument exists both ways: mirrored blades are what cancel axial thrust in a double-flow rotor, but rotation sense is common.
  2. Is it right that stator and rotor lean the same way and only the camber opposes?
  3. Double flow has NOT been re-checked since the stator lean was flipped on 2026-08-04; the earlier 'stator looks right on the right half' judgement predates that flip.

HOW TO SETTLE IT: against a published turbine velocity-triangle / blade-profile reference, not by eye. Anything adopted must be documented with its source per the workspace provenance rule. Note the angles themselves are still placeholders (op-wqk.14.11) and become real when the physical turbine model lands (op-dt3.18) -- it may be cheapest to settle lean and angles together at that point.

title: color_maps: add a perceptually-uniform temperature colour map (licence-clean)
description:
Maintainer asked 2026-08-05 about using the NASA GISS Panoply colorbars (https://www.giss.nasa.gov/tools/panoply/colorbars/) for temperature colouring, and flagged uncertainty about the copyright. That uncertainty was correct.

FINDING -- DO NOT ADOPT PANOPLY'S SET IN BULK (checked 2026-08-05):
The Panoply colorbars page carries NO licence, terms of use, or redistribution statement of any kind. The tables are explicitly third-party in origin, by the page's own attribution text:
  CB*   -> ColorBrewer2.org, Cynthia A. Brewer
  NCL*  -> NCL Graphics Color Table Gallery, UCAR
  GMT*  -> Generic Mapping Tools, SOEST, University of Hawai'i
  EO/NEO-> NASA Earth Observatory / NASA Earth Observations
  plus NOAA, UK Met Office, Scientific Visualization Studio, and individual researchers (e.g. Joshua Stevens)

So 'it is NASA, therefore public domain' does not hold: US Government works are public domain only for the parts NASA actually authored, and the page does not mark which those are. Taking the CB* tables via Panoply would additionally STRIP the attribution notice ColorBrewer's own licence requires. This fails RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md (documented source/author/licence/URL/date) and the CLAUDE.md rule against introducing code whose licence has not been checked.

TWO VERIFIED, GPL-3.0-COMPATIBLE ALTERNATIVES:

1. RECOMMENDED -- Scientific colour maps, Fabio Crameri.
   Licence: MIT (verified on the Zenodo record, v8.0.1, published 2023-10-05).
   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.1243862 ; https://www.fabiocrameri.ch/colourmaps/
   Built for scientific data: perceptually uniform (equal steps in temperature look like equal steps in colour) and readable with colour-vision deficiency. Diverging hot/cold candidates: vik, roma. Sequential: lajolla, lipari. Citable, which suits the V&V write-ups.

2. ColorBrewer. Licence: Apache-2.0, (c) 2002 Cynthia Brewer, Mark Harrower, The Pennsylvania State University.
   GPL-3.0-compatible (NOT GPL-2-compatible). Conditions: retain the copyright notice; end-user documentation must acknowledge 'This product includes color specifications and designs developed by Cynthia Brewer (http://colorbrewer.org/)'; the ColorBrewer name may not be used to endorse derivatives.

HOW TO IMPLEMENT WHEN PICKED UP:
  - ADD alongside the existing maps, never replace them. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/color_maps/ is documented as already-validated code whose exact values call sites depend on. hot_to_cold_colour_mark_1 stays.
  - New map gets a provenance header (project, author, version/DOI, licence, URL, date accessed) and a References.md entry.
  - If ColorBrewer is chosen, the attribution string above must appear in user-facing docs, not just source.

Callers that would benefit: PipeVisual cell fills, TurbineVisual casing, and the per-stage steam-quality tint (which currently reuses steam_quality_colour_mark_1 normalised over a display range).

notes.content:
COLORBREWER SOURCE CLARIFICATION (checked 2026-08-06, prompted by the maintainer asking whether github.com/axismaps/colorbrewer is 'the' ColorBrewer):

Yes -- axismaps/colorbrewer is the official repository behind colorbrewer2.org, maintained by Axis Maps, with the schemes based on Dr Cynthia Brewer's research.

BUT THE TWO LICENCE FILES ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE:
  - github.com/axismaps/colorbrewer/LICENCE.txt is the STOCK Apache-2.0 boilerplate with the placeholders left unfilled ('Copyright {yyyy} {name of copyright owner}'). It names no copyright holder and carries no acknowledgement clause. It governs Axis Maps' website/software.
  - colorbrewer2.org/export/LICENSE.txt is Apache-2.0 WITH the copyright filled in -- (c) 2002 Cynthia Brewer, Mark Harrower, The Pennsylvania State University -- and the specific condition that end-user documentation acknowledge: 'This product includes color specifications and designs developed by Cynthia Brewer (http://colorbrewer.org/)'. It also forbids using the ColorBrewer name to endorse derivatives.

The colour SPECIFICATIONS are the part this project would use, so the export licence is the authoritative one to cite. Taking the GitHub boilerplate instead would mean redistributing the colour data with no named copyright holder and no attribution -- the same defect as taking them via Panoply.

Unchanged recommendation: Crameri's Scientific colour maps (MIT, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1243862) remain the simpler choice, with no attribution clause to carry and better suitability for scientific data. ColorBrewer stays viable if its acknowledgement is honoured in user-facing docs.
notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

notes.content:
DECIDED 2026-08-06 (maintainer): use CRAMERI'S SCIENTIFIC COLOUR MAPS. ColorBrewer is not being adopted; the licence comparison above is retained only as the record of why.

Licence: MIT. Verified on the Zenodo record, v8.0.1, published 2023-10-05.
Cite: Crameri, F. (2018). Scientific colour maps. Zenodo. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1243862
Home: https://www.fabiocrameri.ch/colourmaps/  Supporting paper: Geoscientific Model Development (2018).
MIT is compatible with this workspace's GPL-3.0-only and carries no attribution clause to thread through user-facing docs.

WHY CRAMERI RATHER THAN COLORBREWER (the reason is technical, not preference):
ColorBrewer's schemes were designed to make DISCRETE choropleth classes distinguishable and are NOT perceptually uniform. Stretched across a continuous field they manufacture apparent banding -- fast-changing stretches read as steep gradients and flat stretches as isothermal, when the underlying data is smooth. For widgets whose stated premise is that rendering derives directly from physics state, a colour map that invents structure is actively wrong. Crameri's are perceptually uniform by construction: equal steps in the quantity read as equal steps in colour.

Two further properties that matter here:
  - Greyscale-safe: stays readable printed black-and-white, which the V&V write-ups will need.
  - CYCLIC maps (romaO, vikO, ...). ColorBrewer has no equivalent, and the turbine rotor angle is a cyclic quantity -- a cyclic map is the correct way to colour one.

ColorBrewer's qualitative sets remain the more battle-tested option IF categorical palettes are ever wanted (flow regimes, component types, material IDs). Revisit only for that.

MAP SELECTION (suggested, confirm when implementing):
  - temperature / hot-cold, diverging: vik or roma
  - sequential (quality, burnup, flux): lajolla, lipari, or batlow
  - cyclic (rotor angle, phase): romaO or vikO

IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINTS (unchanged):
  - ADD alongside the existing maps; never replace them. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/color_maps/ is documented as already-validated code whose exact values call sites depend on. hot_to_cold_colour_mark_1 and steam_quality_colour_mark_1 both stay.
  - Provenance header on the new module (project, author, version, DOI, licence, URL, date accessed) plus a References.md entry, per RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md.
  - Vendor only the specific map tables used, with their MIT notice, rather than the whole suite.
  - Callers that would benefit: PipeVisual cell fills, TurbineVisual casing, the per-stage steam-quality tint.

notes.content:
NEUTRAL-MIDPOINT ALTERNATIVES (measured 2026-08-06, from the official archive). Maintainer asked whether anything other than white could carry 'neither hot nor cold'; decision was to KEEP WHITE (vik). Recorded so the option is not re-derived.

Diverging maps in the suite, sampled at t=0 / t=0.5 / t=1 with Rec.601 luma at the midpoint:
  vik      (  0, 18, 97) (236,229,224) ( 89,  0,  8)  mid-luma 230.5   <- in use
  broc     ( 44, 26, 76) (235,238,236) ( 38, 38,  0)  236.9
  cork     ( 44, 25, 76) (230,237,236) ( 15, 41,  3)  234.8
  bam      (101,  2, 75) (246,241,240) ( 13, 76,  0)  242.4
  roma     (126, 23,  0) (192,234,195) (  3, 49,152)  217.0
  berlin   (158,176,255) ( 25, 12,  9) (255,173,173)   15.5   <- dark neutral
  lisbon   (230,229,255) ( 23, 25, 25) (255,255,217)   24.4
  tofino   (222,217,255) ( 13, 22, 19) (219,230,155)   19.0
  vanimo   (255,205,253) ( 26, 21, 19) (190,253,165)   22.3
  managua  (255,207,103) ( 87, 41, 73) (129,231,255)   58.4

berlin is the direct drop-in if a dark neutral is ever wanted: same blue-cold / red-hot semantics, but the midpoint recedes on a dark UI instead of being the brightest thing on screen.

WHY WHITE WAS KEPT: berlin and the other dark-neutral maps invert the intensity relationship -- extremes become light, the middle dark -- so they read oddly printed or on a light background. vik behaves sensibly either way, which matters if studio output ends up in figures. Switching is a one-line change in components::temperature_colour; the blue/white/red convention test would need updating with it.

title: Widget Studio: app shell — widget picker, live state controls, egui/eframe skeleton
description:
The studio frame everything else plugs into. An eframe app (target-gated off Android per the windowing exemption, like mesh_studio/mc_studio) with: a list/picker of every visual component, a live-state control panel (sliders for temperature, flow, opening fraction, etc.) so a widget can be driven across its full range by hand, and a panel showing the widget's derived geometry inputs so it is obvious what drives what.

Follow the crate's existing example-app conventions (examples/ with required-features, app_scaffold/ for shared panels). Tracer state is APPLICATION-owned and advanced once per frame, then copied into the widget at build time -- widgets are rebuilt every repaint, so a train owned by a widget resets its phase each frame (crate CLAUDE.md).

Parent: the Widget Studio bead.

title: Widget Studio: plant-space layout layer — metres to screen transform, node graph, elevation
description:
The substrate that makes the aesthetic bar achievable, and the missing abstraction today. PipeVisual currently takes screen_position: Pos2 + screen_vector: Vec2 in raw SCREEN POINTS, hardcodes PIPE_STROKE_WIDTH = 4.0, and has no elevation and no connection concept -- so every endpoint is hand-placed by the app and nothing about the drawing is derived.

Needed: a layout module owning a plant-space (metres, with elevation) -> screen transform plus a node graph, so components are placed at real coordinates and connected by node. Pipe direction/length then follow from real geometry, connections are shared nodes (so runs meet smoothly), and elevation makes natural-circulation loops read correctly.

tampines::components::Pipe ALREADY exposes everything needed -- diameter: Length, length: Length, inclination: Angle, roughness: Length (crates/tampines/src/components/pipe.rs:37-43), all uom-typed and stable (step() is inert, so they are caller-supplied and trustworthy). No tampines change required for pipes.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, deferred by the maintainer (2026-08-04) -- resolve before building: is stroke width proportional to DIAMETER (a true scale drawing; bore area then reads correctly to the eye as width^2) or to AREA (width proportional to d^2, exaggerating large pipes)? Note also that bores (~0.05 m) and runs (~10 m) cannot share one scale or pipes render as invisible hairlines, so diameter needs its own exaggerated scale -- which must be documented honestly as exaggeration, not as proportionality. The V&V write-up has to state which convention is used.

title: Pump widgets: cavitation bubbles at the impeller eye (DEFERRED)
description:
Maintainer: defer until later. Steam-generator bubble work (the 'ngeow' bead) is higher priority and should be done first -- both would share the same deterministic-scatter machinery, so doing SG first makes this cheaper.

IDEA: draw cavitation in the pump widgets (crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/pump.rs).

Cavitation is LOCALISED AND DIAGNOSTIC, not diffuse -- which is what makes it worth drawing. Vapour forms where local static pressure falls below saturation: the SUCTION SIDE OF THE BLADE LEADING EDGES NEAR THE IMPELLER EYE, where velocity is highest and pressure lowest. It should appear as a cloud hugging the leading edges, growing along the blade as NPSH margin falls, and collapsing further out where pressure recovers -- that collapse is what erodes impellers.

Drawn well it reads instantly as 'this pump is in trouble', which is the kind of thing an operator-facing twin should show.

INPUT NEEDED: one scalar -- available NPSH against required, or simply a margin fraction in [0,1].

CONSTRAINT: offline demonstration artwork, not a two-phase model. Same rule as the SG bubbles -- put the bubbles where the physics puts them, but keep it a display heuristic and say so.

Applies to PumpKind::Centrifugal and VerticalCannedRotor. The axial propeller cavitates differently (tip vortex) and is lower value.

title: Real-time multi-fidelity simulator loop: make the low band solid first
description:
Source: docs/real-time-multifidelity-scoping.md (written 2026-08-07; self-labelled "scoping analysis, not an approved plan", AI-assisted draft, not human-reviewed; audited against develop at 8c9ddd05).

VERDICT THE DOC REACHES: exactly one fidelity band runs in real time today and it is the lowest one -- lumped/system TH plus point kinetics, measured on CIET v2 at 94.7 s simulated in 94.7 s wall-clock, 27 ms median compute per 100 ms step (27% duty cycle). The gap to the next rung is ~3 orders of magnitude and does NOT close by optimisation. Design rule: a band that cannot meet its deadline is not allowed in the loop -- it goes offline and its output becomes a table.

TWO LEADING FINDINGS: (1) the crate literally named "real-time process control simulator" is the one component whose per-step cost is UNBOUNDED, and it is still in TUAS's PID path; (2) nothing in the workspace is a surrogate or ROM -- raffles/src/surrogate.rs is 54 lines of doc comment and zero code. There is also NO benchmarking infrastructure anywhere (no criterion, no benches/).

RECOMMENDED ARCHITECTURE: generalise what tampines' fhr_sim_v2 already does -- enum-dispatched fidelity levels on wall-paced threads at separate rates sharing Arc<RwLock<PlantState>>, with conservation-asserting state handoff. KEY SEQUENCING INSIGHT: snapshot/restore must come FIRST, because fidelity switching is a state-serialisation problem in disguise; doing it after the FidelityLevel enum means building it twice.

PHASE 1 is making the band that already runs actually TRUSTWORTHY: remove the unbounded-cost control path, the live todo!() panic paths in the flagship FHR simulator, the ~40 IF97 panic sites that kill the physics thread, and the two pacing defects; and stand up a criterion harness so any of it is measurable.
PHASE 2 is the capability: snapshot/restore/backtrack, then a FidelityLevel enum with conservation-asserted handoff, then a reduced circulating-fuel PRKE demonstrated against moltres.

DONE = a wall-clock-paced simulator sustaining >= 1.0x real-time factor with <= 200 ms control-to-response latency UNDER LOAD (not idle), whose per-step cost is bounded and measured by a committed benchmark baseline per band, that can snapshot and restore plant state, and that can switch fidelity at a timestep boundary with total mass and energy asserted conserved BY TEST.

Everything here remains an OFFLINE DEMONSTRATION ONLY -- never an operational digital twin, never plant monitoring.

DO NOT FILE AS DECIDED PLAN (the doc's own flags):
- The >= 1.0x / 200 ms / 20 Hz figures in section 3.2 are self-labelled ENGINEERING JUDGEMENT, "not values taken from a cited standard". Whether an ANSI/ANS-3.5 anchor is obtainable at all is OPEN, because ANS-3.5 validation needs reference-plant data DATA_POLICY.md forbids. Do not file them as requirements.
- MSRE-first CONTRADICTS docs/reactor-scoping/README.md:120-133, which recommends finishing the FHR widget migration first. That is a maintainer decision; the two docs must be reconciled.
- The bedok seam is gated on an OPEN DECISION (is bedok the neutronics path?), not ready to file as approved work. Until that call is made the nodal-diffusion band cannot even be costed -- it has never executed.
- Do NOT file a raffles::surrogate implementation issue. The doc explicitly says: do not block real-time work on raffles; build surrogates as tabulated offline coefficients and physics-form reduced models in the crates that own the physics. Neural surrogates are recommended AGAINST (auditability posture, no training data).
- Nine explicitly-undetermined items in section 7 must not be cited as facts, notably: the LOADED CIET step cost (unmeasured; the 27 ms is the IDLE state and is "certainly higher" under load); any bedok timing (the 76.5 s figure is Octave running the original MATLAB, not the Rust port); whether CIET v2 physics matches v1 (port-equivalence V&V op-wqk.13.6 has NOT been run -- v2 is "a faithful port of validated physics", not "validated"); Android/Termux real-time behaviour (compile proxy only); all GUI claims (no display available).
- The full tuas_boussinesq_solver suite was NOT run and its pass state is unreliable by construction: 46 #[ignore]d tests plus ~48 more with the #[ignore] commented out by hand.
- All [M] timings are machine-specific to the maintainer's box; re-measure before citing.

  cargo test --release -p chem-eng...              -> 21 passed, 0 failed
  cargo test --release -p teh-o-prke --lib --tests -> 28 passed, 0 failed
WHAT WAS NOT:
  cargo test --release -p tuas_boussinesq_solver --lib --tests
  Started, ran ~70 minutes wall clock (2.5+ hours CPU, ~920% CPU, actively progressing, NOT hung), then was killed to free the cargo build lock at end of session. NO RESULT WAS OBTAINED -- do not read this as a pass or a fail.

TO RESUME: just run it. Budget well over an hour; consider --no-fail-fast and capturing per-test output rather than piping through tail, so a partial run is still informative.

RISK ASSESSMENT (why this is P2 and not P0): the chem-eng change is a cost change, not a physics change. The summed controller output over six benchmark runs of 40k-80k steps was IDENTICAL before and after to the printed 3 decimal places (e.g. 17175484.304 in both). The only intended numerical difference is that the old code discarded exp(-20) = 2.06e-9 of each step response on retirement and the new code carries it, so any TUAS assertion tighter than about 1e-9 relative on a PID-driven quantity is the only plausible failure mode. TUAS regression tolerances are typically far looser than that. Still needs the actual run.

Blocks closing op-fm5.

notes.content:
GATE SATISFIED 2026-08-11. The TUAS suite completed on a run that was allowed to finish:

  cargo test --release -p tuas_boussinesq_solver --lib
  test result: ok. 323 passed; 0 failed; 46 ignored; 0 measured; finished in 2959.84s

That is 49 minutes wall-clock, and it ran while a second unrelated TUAS test binary was executing concurrently on the same machine. So the two earlier ~70-minute runs that were killed were not hung — they were simply not given enough time, which is exactly why this bead insisted a killed run is neither a pass nor a fail.

This also confirms the CLAUDE.md guidance added today: these tests must run in parallel and need a generous timeout or a background run. A default 120 s command timeout is off by a factor of twenty-five.

Note the 46 ignored are pre-existing and were not investigated here. Recommend closing this bead once the maintainer has eyeballed the number, and separately checking whether any of those 46 should be running.

title: kovan-literature: derive Elsevier DOIs from the PII in the PDF Info /Title
description:
Follow-up found while finishing op-szai, measured against the hand-verified records in crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/.

Both HTR-10 Elsevier papers still import with doi: null, but the correct DOI is mechanically derivable from data the extractor already reads and currently only *discards*:

  wu2002htr10.pdf   Info /Title = 'PII: S0029-5493(02)00182-6'
                    reference JSON doi = 10.1016/S0029-5493(02)00182-6
  gao2002htr10th.pdf Info /Title = 'PII: S0029-5493(02)00198-X'
                    reference JSON doi = 10.1016/S0029-5493(02)00198-X

i.e. DOI = '10.1016/' + PII, the standard Elsevier serial-item convention. metadata.rs already rejects the PII string as a title (is_title_junk / TITLE_JUNK_MARKERS 'pii:'), so the parse site exists; it just needs to keep the value instead of dropping it, and only when find_doi() found nothing in the front matter.

Not done under op-szai because it was outside that bead's stated scope (title/authors/document_type/sha256/slug) and it introduces a publisher-specific inference — 10.1016 is asserted to be Elsevier — which deserves the maintainer's sign-off rather than being slipped in. title: outram-foam-basic-lib: hybrid wgpu/multi-CPU backend for the numerical-math kernels
description:
Filed after hours (2026-08-11 23:55 +08) as a record only, per the CLAUDE.md
working-hours guardrail. No code was written and none should be until the next
active window.

## Ask

Give `outram-foam-basic-lib`'s numerical-math kernels an optional **hybrid
execution backend**: the same API can run serial, multi-CPU (rayon), or on the
GPU (wgpu), chosen at run time, with the serial CPU path always present as the
reference implementation.

Scope named by the maintainer:

- root finding
- golden-ratio (golden-section) search / 1-D minimisation
- matrix solutions (LDU + Krylov + dense)
- numerical integration
- numerical differentiation

## Why here

These are Layer 1-3 building blocks (`polynomial/`, `math/`, `matrix/`,
`krylov/`, `ldu_matrix/`, `ode/`), so every solver crate above
(`outram-foam-appbuilder-lib`, `outram-foam-turbulence-lib`, `tampines`,
GeN-Foam) inherits the acceleration without its own GPU code. The workspace
already has a wgpu precedent in `njoy-outram-park-fork` (Faddeeva/WMP kernels)
and `outram-mc-libs` (`op-u6s`, `op-9s8`), so the backend-enum + CPU-fallback
shape is established rather than novel.

## Constraints that bind this work

- **Hybrid means dispatch, not two APIs.** One public entry point per kernel;
  the backend is a parameter. The batch size / problem size decides whether GPU
  dispatch is worth the transfer, and that policy is explicit and documented,
  not hidden.
- **Enum dispatch, no trait objects, no `Box`, no lifetime params** (workspace
  Rust design rules). `ComputeBackend { Serial, CpuMulti, Gpu }`.
- **Android/Termux hard rule.** wgpu and any GPU-only test/example must be
  target-gated so `cargo check -p outram-foam-basic-lib --all-targets --target
  aarch64-linux-android` still passes and a native Termux build still works.
  Default features must stay Android-clean. Relates to epic `op-zfr`.
- **`uom` typing is not to be stripped** to get data onto the GPU. Convert at
  the buffer boundary and convert back; the public signature stays typed.
- **CPU is the oracle.** Every GPU kernel needs a parity gate against the
  serial CPU path with a stated tolerance, and the docs must carry both the
  methodology and the measured numbers (workspace V&V documentation rule). f32
  GPU accuracy is a known open question elsewhere in the workspace (`op-0nh`)
  — do not assume f64 on the GPU.
- **No human V&V is claimed** by any of this until the maintainer signs off.

notes.content: Maintainer decision, 2026-08-12: f32 GPU accuracy accepted for now, to be carried as a documented caveat in each kernel's docs and in the crate README rather than solved. See the note on op-yvj.4.7 for what the caveat must state. Also confirmed: the batched/lane-per-cell formulation is the right shape for these kernels -- batch N independent problems, keep single-problem solves serial.

  does not (human-interface-layer rule).

outram-foam-basic-lib: batched root finding (bracketed/Newton/Brent + closed-form poly roots) on the hybrid backend
description:
Batched **root finding** across the three backends.

Existing serial code to build on, not replace:

- `src/polynomial/` — `linear_eqn.rs`, `quadratic_eqn.rs`, `cubic_eqn.rs`,
  `roots.rs` (closed-form/analytic roots).
- `src/math/` — `erf_inv.rs`, `inv_inc_gamma.rs` (iterative inversions).
- The JANAF thermo Newton solve and the `PengRobinsonGas` Z-root selection are
  the real per-cell callers (see `op-sisf`, `op-17ke`).

What to add:

- A **batched** entry point: solve N independent scalar root problems at once
  (one per cell/face), which is the shape that actually maps onto a GPU. A
  single root solve should stay serial — say so in the docs.
- Bracketing + safeguarded methods, not bare Newton: bisection, Brent /
  safeguarded Newton-with-fallback. Divergent or non-bracketed cases must
  return an error per lane, not poison the whole batch.
- **Per-lane convergence flags** returned to the caller — on a GPU every lane
  runs the same iteration count, so a lane that failed must be identifiable
  rather than silently returning its last iterate.
- Closed-form polynomial roots (quadratic/cubic) get their own batched kernel;
  they are branch-light and a good first GPU target.

iterative ones; record measured max/RMS error and the tolerance in the doc
comment.

title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
outram-foam-basic-lib: golden-section (golden-ratio) 1-D minimisation, batched on the hybrid backend
description:
Batched **golden-section search** (golden-ratio 1-D minimisation) across the
three backends. There is no golden-section implementation in the crate today —
this is new code, in `src/math/` or a new `src/optimise/`.

Why it is wanted: derivative-free bracketed minimisation of a scalar function
on `[a, b]`, for the cases where a root-find is the wrong tool (minimising a
residual, a limiter blend factor, a property-inversion objective that is not
monotone).

What to deliver:

- Serial reference: classic golden-section with the fixed `(3 - sqrt(5)) / 2`
  contraction, a stated bracketing precondition (unimodal on `[a, b]` — say
  loudly in the doc that a non-unimodal input gives *a* local minimum, not
  *the* minimum), and both absolute and relative interval tolerances.
- **Batched** form: N independent brackets contracted in lockstep. Golden
  section is uniformly convergent and branch-free, so this is one of the
  cleanest GPU fits in the whole epic — the interval count after k iterations
  is identical in every lane.
- Optional Brent-style parabolic-interpolation variant as a CPU-only faster
  path; do **not** put it on the GPU, its branching kills the lockstep
  property that makes the batched version worth doing.

V&V: analytic minima of smooth test functions with known answers, plus the
theoretical contraction rate (interval width should shrink by the golden ratio
per iteration — assert it). Record the measured numbers per the workspace V&V
documentation rule.

title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
outram-foam-basic-lib: matrix solutions on the hybrid backend (vecops, LDU SpMV, BiCGStab/GMRES, preconditioners)
description:
**Matrix solutions** on the hybrid backend. This is the highest-value item in
the epic — the linear solve dominates every FV timestep — and the hardest.

Existing serial code:

- `src/krylov/` — `bicgstab.rs`, `gmres.rs`, `preconditioner.rs`, `vecops.rs`
- `src/ldu_matrix/` — the OpenFOAM LDU sparse form
- `src/matrix/square_matrix.rs` — small dense

What to deliver, in rough dependency order:

1. **`vecops` on the backend** — axpy, dot, norm, scale. Cheap to port,
   immediately reusable, and a dot-product reduction is the honest first test
   of the GPU path. Note that a GPU tree reduction changes summation order, so
   results will differ from the serial path in the last bits; the parity gate
   must be a tolerance, and the tolerance must be stated.
2. **LDU sparse matrix-vector product** on the backend — the inner-loop cost of
   every Krylov iteration. Needs the host-side LDU-to-buffer serialisation
   (owner/neighbour addressing) done once per mesh, not per iteration.
3. **BiCGStab and GMRES drivers** that keep their control flow on the host and
   dispatch only the kernels. Do not try to move the whole Arnoldi loop into
   WGSL on the first pass.
4. **Preconditioners** — diagonal/Jacobi is trivially parallel and should come
   first. DIC/DILU are *sequential by construction*; they do not port directly,
   and the honest options are a block-Jacobi-over-subdomains variant (changes
   the preconditioner, so it changes the iteration count and must be
   re-validated) or keeping them CPU-only. Do not quietly substitute one for
   the other.
5. Dense `SquareMatrix` LU/back-substitution — small, so `CpuMulti` at most;
   flag it explicitly as not a GPU target unless batched over many small
   systems.

Known related work: `op-hzs.9` wants `outram-blender` to consume these sparse
solvers, and `op-ulo.5` notes the symmetric-solver (DIC-PCG / GAMG) seam is
still missing — so a CG path and GAMG are adjacent but out of scope here
unless they land first.

V&V: solve a system with a known analytic solution and a fixed-seed random SPD
system; compare CPU vs GPU residual histories, not just the final answer — a
diverging iteration count is the signal that a preconditioner was silently
changed. Record iteration counts and final residuals with the date.

title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
outram-foam-basic-lib: numerical integration on the hybrid backend (batched quadrature + ODE ensembles)
description:
**Numerical integration** on the hybrid backend — two distinct things, both
named by the maintainer under one heading, kept separate here because they
parallelise differently.

**(a) Quadrature.** No general quadrature module exists in the crate today.
Add one (`src/math/quadrature.rs` or `src/integration/`):

- Fixed-order Gauss-Legendre and Simpson/trapezoid on `[a, b]`, plus an
  adaptive variant on the CPU.
- The GPU-worthy shape is **N independent integrals evaluated at once** (one
  per cell/face/band), not one integral split across threads. Fixed-order rules
  are branch-free and map cleanly; adaptive subdivision does not — keep
  adaptive CPU-only and say why in the doc.
- A summation-order note is required: a parallel reduction is not
  bit-identical to serial accumulation.

**(b) ODE integration ensembles.** Existing serial code in `src/ode/` —
`euler.rs`, `rkf45.rs`, `rosenbrock23.rs`, `integrator.rs`.

- The parallel shape is an **ensemble**: N independent IVPs advanced together
  (per-cell chemistry/thermo relaxation, particle histories). One stiff ODE is
  inherently sequential in time and must stay serial.
- `rkf45` is adaptive-step, so an ensemble on the GPU either runs lockstep at
  the smallest step in the batch (wasteful but simple) or needs per-lane step
  control (correct but divergent). Pick one deliberately, document the choice,
  and measure the cost.
- `rosenbrock23` needs a Jacobian per lane — depends on the numerical
  differentiation work in the sibling bead.

V&V: integrals with closed-form values (polynomials exact to the Gauss order,
a Gaussian, a log singularity for the adaptive path); ODEs with analytic
solutions plus an order-of-convergence check that the observed order matches
the method's theoretical order. Record measured errors and the date.

title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
outram-foam-basic-lib: numerical differentiation on the hybrid backend (finite differences + batched Jacobians)
description:
**Numerical differentiation** on the hybrid backend.

Note the distinction up front, because the crate already has one of these:
`src/fv_operators/` implements *spatial* FV gradient/divergence/laplacian over
a mesh. This bead is about **general-purpose numerical differentiation of a
supplied function** — the derivative and Jacobian machinery that root finders,
Rosenbrock ODE integrators, and sensitivity work need. Do not duplicate the FV
operators; cross-reference them in the docs so a reader knows which is which.

What to deliver:

- Finite differences: forward, backward, central, and a Richardson-extrapolated
  variant, with a documented step-size rule (the `sqrt(eps) * scale` trade-off
  between truncation and round-off error) rather than a hard-coded `h`.
- **Batched derivative evaluation** — N independent points, the GPU-worthy
  shape.
- **Jacobian assembly** for an N-dimensional function: N+1 (forward) or 2N
  (central) evaluations, all independent, which is the genuinely useful
  parallel win here and the direct feeder for `rosenbrock23` and for
  multi-dimensional Newton in the root-finding bead.

outram-foam-basic-lib: CPU-vs-GPU parity gates + crossover benchmarks for the hybrid math kernels
description:
The gate that makes the rest of `op-yvj.4` trustworthy. Blocked by every
kernel bead; nothing in the epic may be described as working until this passes.

**Parity gate.** For every kernel added under this epic, a test that runs the
same problem through `Serial`, `CpuMulti`, and `Gpu` and compares:

- `Serial` vs `CpuMulti` should agree to near machine precision **unless** a
  reduction reorders summation — in which case say so and use a stated
  tolerance, do not just widen it silently.
- `Serial` vs `Gpu` needs an explicit tolerance justified by the precision the
  kernel actually runs at. **Do not assume f64 on the GPU** — many adapters
  give f32 for compute, and f32 accuracy across a full parameter range is
  already an open human-review question elsewhere in this workspace
  (`op-0nh`, Faddeeva). State the precision and the measured error, per kernel.
- For iterative solvers, compare **residual histories and iteration counts**,
  not just the final answer. A changed preconditioner shows up as a different
  iteration count long before it shows up as a wrong answer.

**Benchmarks.** Measure, do not assert, that the GPU path is actually faster:
report the crossover problem size per kernel, including the host-device
transfer, and record the hardware it was measured on. If a kernel never beats
`CpuMulti` at realistic sizes, that is a legitimate result — write it down and
leave the kernel off the auto-select policy rather than shipping a slower
default.

**Documentation** (workspace V&V rule — methodology *and* results): each gate's
doc comment states what is computed, the reference, the inputs, the pass
criterion, and then the actual measured numbers with the date and the hardware.

**No human V&V is claimed by any of this.** These are automated verification
gates written by an AI-assisted draft process; the crate README's
`## Bookkeeping status` axes stay ❌ until the maintainer personally signs off.

CI note: GPU tests must skip cleanly (not fail) on a host with no adapter, and
must not run at all on Android/Termux.

notes.content: Maintainer decision, 2026-08-12: f32 on the GPU is ACCEPTED for now. Do not block this epic on f64 GPU support or on the op-0nh Faddeeva f32 accuracy review. Requirement is a DOCUMENTED CAVEAT, not a fix: every GPU kernel's doc comment must state (a) the precision it actually runs at, (b) the measured max/RMS deviation from the f64 serial CPU oracle on the stated test problem, and (c) that the GPU path is therefore not the reference result. The parity-gate tolerances are set to pass at f32 deliberately -- that is the maintainer's call, not a loosened tolerance of convenience. Iterative solvers keep the stricter check: a changed ITERATION COUNT or residual history is a real defect even at f32, and must not be waved through as precision noise. Revisit if a validation case is ever gated on GPU output.
